events_display.ww1936_imjin_admiral_trusted: The admiral keeps the fleet in port; his enemies at court call it cowardice.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_command_obeyed: The righteous army leaders take the court's orders.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_command_refused: The righteous army leaders ignore the court's orders.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_court_held: The ministers stay in office; the {ideology} are pushed aside, and the court grumbles.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_court_yielded: The {ideology} take the chief councillor's seat.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_fleet_scuttled: A Joseon fleet has sunk its own ships. Its crews go to the walls.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_fleet_stands: A Joseon fleet stands to fight.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_fleet_withdrawn: A Joseon fleet withdraws to the west.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_flight_cross: The court crosses the Yalu into Ming.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_flight_flee: The court rides north and settles in {region}.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_flight_split: The king settles in {region}; the crown prince holds a court of his own and raises men.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_chungju_a: The cavalry forms up on the plain before Chungju, the river at its back.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_chungju_b: Men and timber go up to Joryeong. The pass and Chungju's walls are made ready.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_chungju_c: The army falls back on the capital and its walls. The south is left to itself.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_crown_prince_a: Prince Gwanghae is named heir. The court settles, and the Westerners stand higher.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_crown_prince_b: Jeong Cheol goes into exile at Ganggye and the Westerners are thrown out. The Easterners argue over how hard to strike them, and begin to split.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_crown_prince_c: The question is put aside, and the court whispers.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_defence_system_a: The counties are told where to gather and whom to wait for.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_defence_system_b: Each district commander is told to hold his own ground.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_embassy_a: The court orders the south to make ready. The people are uneasy, and the Westerners' word carries weight.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_embassy_b: The court calls the alarm groundless. The people are calm, and the coast stands as it was.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_embassy_c: Quietly, the walls of Dongnae and Gimhae are repaired.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_famine_a: Relief kitchens open. The people bless the king, and the treasury empties.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_famine_b: Rich men buy titles with grain. The granaries fill, and the court's honours lose their worth.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_famine_c: Grain goes to the army. The soldiers eat; the villages do not.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_haengju_a: Palisades go up on the hill at Haengju. Gwon Yul's men will not come down.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_haengju_b: Gwon Yul's men march north to join Ming.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_half_warned: The Japanese have landed; the country was only half ready
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_imjin_river_a: The crossings of the Imjin are watched, and Gaeseong's walls are strengthened.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_imjin_river_b: The army marches north to gather at Pyongyang, and the city's walls are made ready.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_jinju_a: Jinju shuts its gates. Townsfolk carry stones and boiling water to the walls.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_jinju_b: Jinju's garrison marches west. Jeonju and Namwon are strengthened, and Jinju's people feel abandoned.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_landing_a: The towns shut their gates. Word that the walls will be held to the last spreads through the country.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_landing_b: The people climb into the hills with what they can carry. Fewer will die, but the towns are left thin.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_landing_c: Every man on the rolls is called up. The roads fill with conscripts, and with grumbling.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_ming_arrives_a: Our granaries feed the Ming army and our generals take its orders. Ming's generals are pleased.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_ming_arrives_b: Our generals keep their own commands. Ming's generals are cool toward us.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_northern_generals_a: The generals ride south. The passes of Joryeong, Chupungnyeong and Jungnyeong get palisades and men.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_northern_generals_b: The generals stay north, and the border is quiet.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_pyongyang_a: Joseon's soldiers stand in the assault columns beside Ming's.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_pyongyang_b: Our men hold the roads and carry the grain; Ming goes up the walls.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_second_war_a: Namwon, Jeonju and Daegu are walled and garrisoned.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_second_war_b: What grain can be carried goes into the hills, and the rest is burned. The people suffer, but our men have stores to live on.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_second_war_c: The court asks Ming to lead the war. Ming's generals take it as their due.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_taiko_dead: Rumour from Japan: Hideyoshi is dead
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_taiko_rumour: Rumour from Japan: Hideyoshi is ill
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_unwarned: The Japanese have landed, and the country was not ready
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_warn_ming_a: An envoy carries the news of Japan's letter to Beijing. Ming takes note.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_warn_ming_b: The letter stays in Seoul. If Ming hears of it from others, it will wonder why.
events_display.ww1936_imjin_jos_warned: The Japanese have landed, and the country was ready for them

bettignies.bio: A Frenchwoman of Lille whom British intelligence called 'Alice Dubois'. From January to September 1915 she ran a network of about a hundred people. In history: taken near Tournai on 20 October 1915, she was sentenced to death, then to forced labour, and died in prison in Cologne on 27 September 1918.
bettignies.name: Louise de Bettignies
bettignies.work: Reports German movements from occupied Lille

bolo.bio: Paul Bolo, a businessman from Marseille. With German money passed through the former Khedive of Egypt he tried to buy into the French press. In history: arrested on 29 September 1917, he was shot at Vincennes on 17 April 1918.
bolo.name: Bolo Pasha
bolo.work: Buys newspapers to break the enemy's nerve

dame_blanche.bio: A network in occupied Belgium working for British intelligence, set up in 1916 by Walthère Dewé, Herman Chauvin and others. People living by the railways counted every train, day and night. In history: by 1918 it had over a thousand members and was never broken.
dame_blanche.name: The White Lady network
dame_blanche.work: Counts German trains day and night

druzhina.bio: A unit of Czechs living in Russia, formed at Kiev in August 1914. Its men went out in small patrols to scout, to question prisoners and to persuade the Czech regiments opposite to come over. In history: it first went into action in November 1914 and grew into the Czechoslovak Legion.
druzhina.name: The Czech Druzhina
druzhina.work: Scouts the Austrian lines and talks to the Czechs across them

duquesne.bio: A Boer who worked for Germany. From Bahia in Brazil he loaded bombs disguised as boxes of mineral samples onto British ships; three sailors died on the Tennyson in February 1916. In history: he faked his own death, was taken in New York in 1917, and in May 1919 escaped from Bellevue Hospital dressed as a woman.
duquesne.name: Fritz Joubert Duquesne
duquesne.work: Puts bombs on British merchant ships

ignatiev.bio: An officer of the Guard Hussars who ran Russia's intelligence and counter-intelligence service in France from 1915. In history: by the spring of 1917 he had built a large network of agents there, and told the story himself in a book published in Paris in 1933.
ignatiev.name: Colonel Pavel Ignatiev
ignatiev.work: Gathers from Paris what Germany means to do

lody.bio: A German naval reserve officer. He landed on 27 August 1914 with the passport of an American, 'Charles A. Inglis'. Counter-intelligence opened every letter he sent. In history: taken at Killarney on 2 October, he was shot in the Tower of London on 6 November 1914.
lody.name: Carl Hans Lody

mata_hari.bio: The Dutch dancer Margaretha Zelle. German intelligence named her H-21; in 1916 she also worked for Captain Ladoux of the French Deuxième Bureau. In history: arrested in Paris on 13 February 1917, she was shot at Vincennes on 15 October 1917.
mata_hari.name: Mata Hari
mata_hari.work: Hears what officers say and passes it on

pow_polish.bio: Piłsudski's underground army, named in November 1914. Its people spied and blew things up behind the Russian lines. In history: from a few hundred members in 1914 it grew to over 30,000 by 1918.
pow_polish.name: The Polish Military Organisation
pow_polish.work: Spies and sabotages behind the Russian lines

reilly.bio: An adventurer born in the Russian Empire. Early in the war he dealt in munitions in New York. In the spring of 1918 Cumming swore him into the Secret Intelligence Service and sent him to Russia, where he joined a plot to overthrow Lenin's government. In history: when it failed he got out through Finland and reached London on 8 November 1918.
reilly.name: Sidney Reilly
reilly.work: Digs into what Russia's rulers mean to do

rintelen.bio: A German naval officer. He reached New York on 3 April 1915 on a false Swiss passport, hid cigar-shaped fire bombs in the holds of ships bound for the Allies, and paid for strikes in munitions works. In history: sailing home that August, he was taken off his ship by the British.
rintelen.name: Franz von Rintelen
rintelen.work: Hides fire bombs in munitions ships

svu.bio: Ukrainians from the Russian side of the border who founded the union at Lemberg on 4 August 1914 and moved to Vienna that same month. With money from Vienna and Berlin they printed papers and pamphlets and ran schools and libraries in the camps of Ukrainian prisoners from the Russian army.
svu.name: The Union for the Liberation of Ukraine
svu.work: Prints papers for Ukrainians and works the prison camps

zurich_net.bio: An office run by Captain Rudolf Mayer inside the Austro-Hungarian consulate in Zurich. Italy blamed it for the explosions that sank the battleship Benedetto Brin at Brindisi on 27 September 1915 and the dreadnought Leonardo da Vinci at Taranto on 2 August 1916. In history: Italian agents broke into the office at the end of February 1917.
zurich_net.name: The Zurich office
zurich_net.work: Hides bombs in Italian warships and arsenals

bargain.propose_how: Every province of {country} is on the map. Paint a fate on each, then put the terms. What is left unpainted goes back.
bargain.propose_plan: A department's plan, if you took one, is painted already. Change any province.

protest.cost: The protest stays on the record. Neutral opinion cools and America turns further from us. {country}'s thirst for revenge and the resistance in the land will grow year by year.
protest.how: Accept or protest each province. A protest goes on the record but blocks nothing, and there is no walking out.
protest.last: Their next answer is the last. Whatever they still protest then goes into the treaty as proposed.

AUH.capital: Vienna? In His Majesty's name we protest.
AUH.heart: {place} is a land of the Crown. We yield it to force, under protest.
AUH.much: Nothing of the Empire will be left. We protest {place} as well.
AUH.unjust: The Monarchy signs because it must. It protests {place}.

DEU.capital: Berlin? Germany protests, and signs nothing of it freely.
DEU.heart: {place} is Germany. We sign under protest, under force.
DEU.much: This is a dictated peace. Germany protests {place} as well.
DEU.unjust: We know the force of the hatred that meets us here. Germany protests {place}.

FRA.capital: Paris? France protests, as she protested in 1871.
FRA.heart: {place} is France. It will come back, as it did before; we protest.
FRA.much: You take more than in 1871. France protests {place} as well.
FRA.unjust: France yields to force and protests {place}.

GBR.capital: London? His Majesty's Government protests formally.
GBR.heart: {place} is a land of the Crown. We protest, for the record.
GBR.much: You have taken more than enough. We protest {place} as well.
GBR.unjust: His Majesty's Government enters its formal protest over {place}.

RUS.capital: Petrograd? Russia protests. This paper will not last.
RUS.heart: {place} is Russian land. We sign without discussion, at gunpoint.
RUS.much: This is plunder, not peace. Russia protests {place} as well.
RUS.unjust: We will not even debate these terms. We sign them under compulsion and protest {place}.

why.capital: {place} is our capital. We protest, and the world will hear of it.
why.heart: {place} is the heart of this country. It is torn from us; we protest.
why.much: You take everything. We protest {place} as well.
why.unjust: This is not a negotiation but a dictate. We protest {place}.

bargain.tap: Tap a province on the map to decide it on its own.
bargain.ultimatum_now: Ultimatum: take it now or the advance resumes

AUH.again: Ask as often as you like; Vienna's answer is the same.
AUH.allies: Berlin is still fighting. Vienna cannot give up {place} first.
AUH.army: The Emperor's army has not broken. Not {place}.
AUH.beaten: The Empire has lost. {place} is yours.
AUH.capital: Vienna is the head of the Empire. I will not put that before His Majesty.
AUH.heart: {place} is crown land. It is not the Habsburgs' to give.
AUH.held: {place} is in your hands already. We accept.
AUH.much: At this rate there will be no Empire left. Not {place} as well.
AUH.return: You give back {place}. Vienna will remember it.
AUH.soft: On those terms ({fate}), I can put it to His Majesty. {place}, then.
AUH.tired: The Empire's peoples can hold out no longer. {place}: we accept.
AUH.to_ally: Hand {place} to {for}, and what will the Empire's other peoples think? No.

DEU.again: Repeating it will not change Germany's answer.
DEU.allies: Vienna and Sofia still fight. Germany cannot give up {place} alone.
DEU.army: The German army still stands on enemy soil. Not {place}.
DEU.capital: Berlin? I will not even write that down.
DEU.heart: {place} is Germany. No German government can sign that.
DEU.held: Your flag already flies over {place}. We accept.
DEU.much: This is not a peace but a dismemberment. Not {place} as well.
DEU.return: You give back {place}. I shall tell Berlin so.
DEU.soft: On those terms ({fate}), Berlin can bear it. {place}, then.
DEU.tired: Our people are starving. {place}: we accept.

FRA.again: Say it again; France's answer is the same.
FRA.allies: Britain still fights. France will not give up {place} first.
FRA.army: The French army is still in its trenches. Not {place}.
FRA.capital: Paris? France will not answer that.
FRA.heart: {place} is France. No Chamber will ratify that.
FRA.held: Your army is already in {place}. We accept.
FRA.much: You would take more than in 1871. Not {place} as well.
FRA.return: You give back {place}. I shall tell the Chamber so.
FRA.soft: On those terms ({fate}), we accept. France will not forget that land.
FRA.tired: France has bled too much. {place}: we accept.
FRA.to_ally: France will not sign {place} over to {for}.

GBR.again: Say it again; London's answer is the same.
GBR.allies: The Dominions and our allies still fight. We cannot give up {place}.
GBR.army: The fleet still holds the sea. Not {place}.
GBR.capital: London? I will not minute that.
GBR.heart: {place} is the Crown's. The Commons will never accept it.
GBR.held: {place} is in your hands already. We accept.
GBR.much: You have taken quite enough. Not {place} as well.
GBR.return: You give back {place}. London accepts it gladly.
GBR.soft: On those terms ({fate}), I can explain it to the Commons. {place}, then.
GBR.tired: The country is worn out. {place}: we accept.
GBR.to_ally: Britain does not agree to handing {place} to {for}.

RUS.again: Say it again if you like; Russia's answer is the same.
RUS.allies: Our allies still fight. To give up {place} would be to abandon them.
RUS.army: Russia is wide, and its army is still there. Not {place}.
RUS.capital: Petrograd? Russia signs no such paper.
RUS.heart: {place} is Russian land. No Russian will sign that.
RUS.held: Your army is already in {place}. We accept.
RUS.much: This is not a peace but plunder. Not {place} as well.
RUS.return: You give back {place}. I shall wire Petrograd.
RUS.soft: On those terms ({fate}), we accept. Russia knows how to wait.
RUS.tired: The soldiers are walking home. {place}: we accept.

why.again: Saying it again changes nothing. Not {place}.
why.allies: Our allies are still fighting. We will not give up {place}.
why.heart: {place} is the heart of this country. We cannot give it up.
why.held: Your army already stands in {place}. We accept.
why.much: You have taken too much already. Not {place} as well.
why.return: You give back {place}. We accept it gladly.
why.soft: On those terms ({fate}), we can bear it. {place} will come back to us one day.
why.tired: We cannot fight on. {place}: we accept.
why.unjust: This peace is dictated, not negotiated. We protest {place} before the world.

book.hint: Each article holds bills that exclude each other: when one passes, it replaces the one in force.
book.title: Law book

why.closed: The country's state doesn't call for it yet.
why.full: Three bills are already on the agenda.
why.locked: A bill of this article failed lately.
why.moving: A bill of this article is on the agenda.

budget.bonds_note: The public would take up {n}% of what is asked
budget.credits_on: Before the house: lobby and call the vote on the credits' paper.
budget.differs: Where it parts from the minister's draft
budget.effects: What it does in a year
budget.no_more: No more budget meetings are due.
budget.nobody: Nobody says no to this budget.
budget.put_again: Amend it and put it again
budget.put_hint: The amended plan goes onto the budget's paper. Win the parties there, then call the vote.
budget.refused_now: Refused. Change it and send it again, force it, or last year's runs on.

tax_who.consumption: Everyone pays it at the shop, and the poor pay most.
tax_who.income: Paid on what one earns: salaried men and the well-off.
tax_who.profits: Paid by the firms that grew rich on war orders.
tax_who.property: Paid on land and wealth held or left behind: landowners and old money.

budget.title: National budget
budget.unsigned: Unsigned, the finance holder's draft is signed by proxy.

claims.ask: Say on the map what land this war is for.
claims.how: Tap a place on the map to paint it; tap it again to take the paint off.
claims.nudge: The war is on and nobody has said what land it is for. Paint it on the map.
claims.priced: A map once signed can only be changed at a price.
claims.title: The land we want

agenda.desk: The paper to pick this year's project is on the desk. Pick one there.
agenda.ended: This year's project is over. We pick the next one in the new year.
agenda.passed: We chose no great work this year. We pick again in the new year.
agenda.soon: The cabinet will soon lay this year's choices on the desk.

craft.early: Went in early: the enemy was ready for it.

progress.exec: Last step: the work is under way. The result is reported when it ends.
progress.opp: Second step: getting past the opposition. One step to go.
progress.prep: First step: gathering people and money. Two steps to go.

raise.total: Put total mobilisation to the table

craft.raise_closed: Not yet: the war does not call for it.
craft.shortage_solved: An answer was found for the {name}.

terms.total: Shells come fastest; bread and order run down.
terms.war: Shells come faster; bread runs down.

counter.against: My vote against a rival's bill
counter.favour: A favour I will owe him
counter.next: A law for a law: his bill next

says.counter_more: Good. But that alone is not enough; add one thing more.
says.counter_refuse: That won't bring my people round.
says.counter_take: That will do. I will tell my people so.
says.threat_condemn: Condemn us? Think what the street will say.
says.threat_dissolve: Dissolve us? We shall see who smiles after the election.
says.threat_file: Bring out your papers, then. After that, we are finished.
says.threat_post: You think one post holds us on a leash?
says.threat_region: You hold my people's bread hostage. They won't forget it.

wing.hello: The party's leaders don't know I'm here. Let's be brief.
wing.take: A few of us will vote with you this time, whatever the party says.

diplo.close_chapter_hint: {n} still reading. What is left on their desks is signed by proxy, as when the clock runs out.
diplo.roads_hint: Accords, bonds and signed treaties open these roads; a leak, a broken accord or a new government closes them.
diplo.slow_ask: Read slowly: ask for 30 more seconds
diplo.slow_hint: The host agrees. {n} left this chapter.
diplo.treaty_hint: A treaty binds when both have signed. Secret until it leaks.
diplo.wire_hint: It arrives next chapter. A weak cipher can be read by a third seat.

ending.fra_end_deadline: The War That Did Not End
ending.gbr_end_island: The Army Back on the Island
ending.rus_abdicated: The Tsar Signs Away the Throne
ending.rus_end_for_heir: The Crown Left to the Son
ending.rus_serbia_abandoned: A Peace That Swallowed Its Word

ending_why.compromise_peace: The war stopped with neither side beaten.
ending_why.deadline: The calendar ran out, but the guns did not stop.
ending_why.first_winter_ahead: The first winter came with our side ahead.
ending_why.first_winter_behind: The first winter came with our side behind.
ending_why.first_winter_level: The first winter came with neither side ahead.
ending_why.home_collapse: The country gave way behind the lines.
ending_why.long_peace: No war came. The guns stayed in their depots.
ending_why.occupation_held: The war goes on, and {country}'s land is in our hands.
ending_why.pair_war_lost: Our war with {country} went against us.
ending_why.pair_war_won: We came out of our war with {country} ahead.
ending_why.separate_peace: We made a peace of our own with {country}.
ending_why.under_occupation: The war goes on, and {country} holds our capital.
ending_why.utopia_realised: A party's idea of the country came true, and you stopped there.

lean.0: will stay out or go the other way

strain.3: near the end of its strength

fleet.asked: You asked the Admiralty to send the fleet to the {area}. The answer comes up in its papers.
fleet.asked_sortie: You ordered the fleet out. How it fights comes up in the Admiralty's papers.
fleet.move: Ask to send it to another sea
fleet.port_seen: seems to be in port at {port}

say.blockade: If we leave the North Sea, the blockade comes apart.
say.repair: Until the ships are mended, we cannot put out.
say.sailing: We are on our way, and will report when we arrive.
say.subs: The boats are out; we hear from them now and then.
say.wait: They may be bigger than us. A fleet in port still guards the sea.
say.watch: They are in port. If we go, they will come out.

fleet.title: {area} · {name}

fleet_paper.hint: Each paper is signed on its own. A paper nobody signs lapses, and the fleet stays where it is.
fleet_paper.overrule: He is against it. Signing it overrules him.

pick.full: The main fleets meet head on
pick.part: Draw out only part of the enemy fleet

auh.agrees: It can be done, Majesty. The fleet will go.
auh.eager: Let the fleet out of Pola for once. The crews are longing for it.
auh.keep_port: The fleet does most by staying at Pola. The enemy must watch it all the same.
auh.repair: The ships are in dock. They cannot go out yet.
auh.thin_home: If the fleet leaves the Adriatic, our coast lies open.
auh.too_strong: The Italians and the French together are too many for us.

deu.agrees: The fleet is ready, Majesty. It waits only for the order.
deu.eager: This is what the fleet was built for. Let us go.
deu.keep_port: A fleet in being binds the British. Lose it and nothing binds them.
deu.repair: The ships are still in the yards. They cannot go out yet.
deu.thin_home: If the fleet leaves the Bight, the British come to our coast.
deu.too_strong: The British have more ships. We would be giving them what they want.

fra.agrees: The Marine can do it, Monsieur le Président.
fra.eager: Our squadron should be where the war is. Send it.
fra.keep_port: Our battleships are few. Better to keep them than to lose them.
fra.repair: The squadron is in dock at Toulon. It needs time.
fra.thin_home: Empty the Mediterranean and the Austrians come out.
fra.too_strong: The enemy has more ships there. It would be a gamble.

gbr.agrees: It can be done. The Grand Fleet can spare it.
gbr.eager: Give me the ships and I will open the way myself.
gbr.keep_port: The fleet is safest at Scapa. We need not seek a battle.
gbr.repair: Half the squadron is in dock. Give the yards a month.
gbr.thin_home: Empty the North Sea and the blockade comes undone.
gbr.too_strong: Their fleet is bigger than the papers say. Not now.

rus.agrees: It can be done, Your Majesty, if the way stays open.
rus.eager: The sea is ours to take. Let us not wait for the Germans.
rus.keep_port: The ships are better behind the minefields. We have few to lose.
rus.repair: The ships are under repair. The yards ask for time.
rus.thin_home: Take the ships away and the capital's sea is empty.
rus.too_strong: The enemy is stronger at sea. We would lose what we cannot build again.

fleet_paper.sortie_line: Out to sea in the {area}, to seek the enemy
fleet_paper.squadron: A squadron of {n} older battleships leaves it; the fleet itself stays.
fleet_paper.title: Admiralty papers
fleet_paper.warned: "The enemy may know and be waiting for us."

why.straits: The straits are being fought for

feed.auh_berlin: The debt to Berlin is large.
feed.deu_army: The General Staff ignores the chancellor.
feed.deu_countersign: The chancellor is reluctant to countersign.
feed.fra_chamber: The Chamber is pressing the cabinet.
feed.fra_gqg: The GQG does not answer to the government.
feed.fra_idle: People say the President does nothing.
feed.gbr_no_conscription: People ask why there is no conscription.
feed.gbr_opposition: The opposition has shut its door.
feed.rus_plot: The talk at table does not stop.

name.gbr_unionists: The other side of the coalition

gov.sub: What threatens your hold on power. The word on the right runs from "rumour" to "any day now" as the danger comes closer.
gov.title: What shakes the government

house.delay: The Lords have put it off until chapter {n}

gone.art87: The Duma is gone: every bill and the budget go out by the Tsar's decree.
gone.dora: Parliament is prorogued: bills and supply go by Order in Council.

house.out_hint: A force in the country has turned on you and is holding up its part until something changes.
house.record: His count so far: right {right}, wrong {wrong}
house.record_hint: How often your vote counter's forecast of a vote came true, and how often it did not.

age.3: old news: it may have changed

fate.fled: got away; can't be used again
fate.recalled: called home when the net was lost

agents.mine_none: Nobody hired yet. Pick from the people below.
agents.none: Our service has no well-known agent to call on. It works with nets alone.
agents.title: Named agents

wait.date: His time has not come yet
wait.full: The service has no room for another agent; more agents abroad make room
wait.gone: That country is out of the war

agents.why: Well-known spies put into a country where we have a net. Reports from there come oftener and surer. If one is caught he is tried, and the net and our standing with that country suffer.

chief.title: Head of intelligence
chief.unmet: We haven't met the head of intelligence yet. He appears in People as the story goes on.
chief.vacant: The post is empty. Without a head, codes and operations go badly.
chief.why: The person who runs the service. The abler he is, the better codes are broken, operations go and enemy agents are caught.

codes.none: We read nobody's codes now. Ours must be better than their codes to read them.
codes.quiet: We can't tell whether they suspect. Calling a bluff or pressing a note on what we read may tell them.
codes.risk: A telegram we read named moves on {fronts}. Sending our main effort there at once may tell them their codes leak.
codes.title: Codebreaking
codes.why: Reading another country's telegrams tells us for certain what it means: in peace whether it will back down, keep its treaty or mobilise; in war its plans at the front. Use it too openly and they notice and change their codes.

countries.none: No rival to watch yet. Countries appear here once a camp or a note stands against us.
countries.nothing: Nothing known yet of {countries}. Plant a net there (covert operations below) and reports come in.
countries.title: What we know of each country
countries.why: Reports on rivals: their war plan, strength, morale, mobilisation, intentions, whether they keep their treaties, unrest at home. They can be wrong, so see who sent them.

fronts.none: Nothing known yet. Plant a net in that country (covert operations below) or read its codes, and reports come in.
fronts.title: The enemy on each front
fronts.why: Whether the enemy is preparing an offensive, and how worn his line is, can only be learned from these reports.

fund.air_hint: Before Neuve Chapelle in March 1915 British airmen photographed the German trenches, and the maps were drawn from the photographs.
fund.air_no: Air photographs: not yet. Artillery research brings them, and then the enemy's preparation for an offensive shows more easily.
fund.air_yes: Air photographs: our aircraft photograph the enemy's trenches and batteries, so his preparation for an offensive shows more easily.
fund.broke: The treasury is empty: a bigger share makes no branch grow now.

nets.1: Nets can be kept in one country only, and one named agent at work. More agents abroad make room for more.
nets.2: Nets can be kept in two countries, and two named agents at work. More agents abroad make room for more.
nets.3: Nets can be kept in three countries, and three named agents at work. More agents abroad make room for more.
nets.4: Nets can be kept in four countries, and four named agents at work.

fund.none: The service hasn't worked yet. After the next chapter you can share its money and men here.

share_hint.0: Take its money and men for other things. Saves a little, but the branch slowly shrinks.
share_hint.1: Give it what it has now. The branch stays as it is.
share_hint.2: Give it more money. The branch grows slowly.
share_hint.3: Give it much more money. The branch grows faster, and counter-intelligence and agents abroad also take men.

fund.title: Money and men

trend.full: as big as it can get

fund.trend_hint: Where this branch is heading with its share now. Growing takes a year or so.
fund.why: How the service's money and men are shared among its four branches. More makes a branch grow slowly; a cut lets it shrink. More costs money, and much more for counter-intelligence or agents abroad also takes men. Britain's counter-intelligence grew from about sixteen people in 1914 to over eight hundred by 1918.

intel.intro: Everything the service knows, in one place. Reports can be wrong: see who sent each one and how sure it is.

nets.none: No nets abroad. You can plant one under covert operations below.
nets.title: Nets and counter-intelligence
nets.why: A net is our agents in another country. It reports on that country, but if caught the net is lost and relations sour.

ops.none: No covert operation can be started now. Rows appear here when the time comes and a schedule slot is free.
ops.title: Covert operations
ops.why: Secret work in another country, paid for in money. Each uses a schedule slot; the result reaches the desk a turn later.

prop.home_on: A campaign at home is under way
prop.hush_on: The censor is keeping bad news out of the papers
prop.none: No campaign can be started now. Rows appear here in wartime when a schedule slot is free.
prop.title: Propaganda and censorship
prop.why: Keep the nerve at home, shake the enemy's people, buy a neutral's opinion. Results come slowly, over months, and money found out turns a country against us.

rings.caught: We hold {country}'s agents. Decide what to do with them on the desk.
rings.none: No spies caught on either side yet.
rings.rolled_up: {country} took every foreign ring it knew of on its mobilisation day. A net of ours there may be gone.
rings.title: Spies caught
rings.turned: We turned {country}'s agents. Their reports on us now carry lies.
rings.we_caught: We caught {country}'s spy ring and made it public.
rings.we_rolled_up: On mobilisation day our counter-intelligence took every foreign ring it knew of.

heard.decoded_hint: We also read this in their codes, so it is sure. Acting on a read is what makes them suspect their codes.
heard.none: Nothing heard yet. When an enemy U-boat goes out or his fleet puts to sea, it shows here.
heard.sortie: Our stations heard {country}'s fleet put to sea.
heard.uboat: Our stations found a U-boat of {country}.

used.sortie: Our fleet was told and went out to meet it.
used.uboat: Our ships were steered around it.

sea.none: We have no direction-finding stations. Order them with the row below.
sea.not_at_sea: Our fleet isn't fighting at sea now. Stations can be ordered once it is.

stations.1: a few stations, one stretch of coast
stations.3: a full chain: we hear the whole sea
stations.hint: Each station takes bearings on the enemy's wireless. Where the bearings cross is where the ship is. A new station goes up every few months.
stations.name: Stations

sea.title: At sea: direction-finding

0.hint: What we hear goes in the files. Nothing at sea changes, and the enemy has no reason to suspect.

1.hint: When the enemy fleet puts out, our fleet is told and goes out first. Seldom used, so seldom noticed.

2.hint: Our ships are also steered away from the U-boats we find. Fewer ships are lost, but the more often it happens, the likelier the enemy changes his codes.
2.word: warn the fleet and steer the ships

sea.why: Coastal stations take bearings on enemy wireless to find U-boats and fleets that put out. The more we act on it, the fewer ships we lose and the better our fleet is placed, but the enemy may notice and change his codes.

abroad.hint: How many men we can place and run in other countries. The more, the more countries can hold our nets, the better operations go, and the better the enemy's preparation shows.
abroad.name: Agents abroad

guard.hint: How hard our telegrams are to read. The stronger, the less the enemy learns of our plans.
guard.name: Our own codes

hunt.hint: How well we find enemy agents at home. The sharper, the shorter their nets last.
hunt.name: Counter-intelligence

skill.none: The service hasn't worked yet, so its skill is unknown. It shows after the first operation or code broken.

read.hint: How well we read enemy telegrams. Codes weaker than this can be read.
read.name: Codebreaking

track.good: This channel has mostly been right so far.
track.mixed: This channel has been right and wrong.
track.poor: This channel has often been wrong.

issue.realign: An alliance with the other camp

waits.shelved: Too soon to bring it again.

hint.bread: Hunger comes to the cities first. Reads the bread of your own country.
hint.nations: Shows how hot the lands of many peoples run. The lower the order, the redder they are painted.
hint.rail: Mobilization trains: how far each country has got in gathering its army at the borders.
hint.rumour: You know other countries only as far as the papers print. Hatched land is rumour.
hint.strikes: Work stops first in the factories and cities. Reads your country's order and its stage of unrest.

lens.nations_how: Only lands with a people of their own are painted. The lower the order, the sooner they boil.
lens.nations_none: {country} has no peoples' question worth a colour.
lens.rail_belgium: When the German trains in the west reach Aachen they stand at the Belgian border. Which road they take is decided when the plan is signed.
lens.rail_head: Mobilization: days gone of the days each army needs to gather at its borders.
lens.rumour_none: No rumour from other countries has reached you yet.

line.bread_rail: The railways can no longer carry grain to the cities.
line.bread_two_halves: The two halves are not sharing grain.
line.budget_army: The army share of the budget.
line.budget_national: The national share of the budget.
line.budget_navy: The navy share of the budget.
line.budget_orders: The army budget sets the works' orders.
line.budget_relief: The food and relief share of the budget.
line.budget_works: The works and welfare share of the budget.
line.econ_eaters: The towns and the army are eating the stores.
line.econ_farms: The fields are bringing in grain.
line.econ_fronts: Every front is firing off shells.
line.econ_held: Works and mines on the land we hold are working for us.
line.econ_imports: Grain is coming in by sea.
line.econ_industry: The country's works are turning out shells.
line.econ_labour: The farmhands are in the army.
line.econ_land: Taxes are coming in from the land we gained.
line.econ_land_lost: The land we lost pays us no taxes.
line.econ_mobilised: All industry has gone over to war work.
line.econ_peace: In peace the stores fill back up to their usual level.
line.econ_trade: Customs and shipping are bringing money in.
line.econ_tribute: A state that depends on us is sending its tribute.
line.econ_tribute_paid: We are paying tribute to the power over us.
line.flu_wave_3: The influenza came a third time.
line.footing_war_bread: The war economy moved the bread.
line.footing_war_money: The war economy moved the money.
line.footing_war_morale: The war economy moved the morale.
line.footing_war_order: The war economy moved the order.
line.footing_war_shells: The war economy moved the shells.
line.left_war_on: We stay out of the war.
line.mediation_half: Only one side took up the mediation.

FRA.0: The Church stands again in the schools and the homes.

FRA.4: Leaning a little to the lay state.

AUH.1: Leaning to property: the great estates feed the country, they say.
AUH.3: Property and labour stand face to face.
AUH.5: Leaning to labour: the workers of Vienna and Budapest carry weight.
AUH.6: Labour's word has become law, and the nobles are afraid.

DEU.0: Owners and landlords have their way; the unions keep their heads down.
DEU.1: Leaning to property: taxes sit lightly on those who own.
DEU.3: Property and labour stand face to face.
DEU.5: Leaning to labour: the unions' words get into the bills.
DEU.6: Labour's word has become law, and the owners are afraid.

FRA.0: The rentiers and landowners have their way; the CGT keeps its head down.
FRA.1: Leaning to property: an income tax is far off.
FRA.3: Property and labour stand face to face.
FRA.5: Leaning to labour: the CGT's words get into the bills.
FRA.6: Labour's word has become law, and the owners are afraid.

GBR.0: The landlords and the City have their way; the unions keep their heads down.
GBR.1: Leaning to property: those with land and money carry weight.
GBR.3: Property and labour stand face to face.
GBR.5: Leaning to labour: the trade unionists' votes carry weight.
GBR.6: Labour's word has become law, and the landlords and the City are afraid.

RUS.0: A country of landlords and factory owners: the peasants have lost the land, the workers their voice.
RUS.1: Leaning to landlords and capital: the land stays with those who own it.
RUS.2: Leaning a little to landlords and capital.
RUS.3: Landlord and peasant, capital and labour stand face to face.
RUS.4: Leaning a little to peasants and workers.
RUS.5: Leaning to peasants and workers: dividing the land is said openly.
RUS.6: Land to those who till it, works to those who work them: the whole country says so.

AUH.0: Vienna and Budapest share out everything; the other peoples are only guests.
AUH.1: Leaning to Dualism: the Magyars and the Germans carry weight.
AUH.3: Dualism and the peoples' demands stand face to face.
AUH.4: Leaning a little to the nations.
AUH.5: Leaning to the nations: the Czechs and the South Slavs carry weight.
AUH.6: Every people rules its own land; Dualism is a thing of the past.

DEU.0: Only what the sword takes counts, says the whole country.
DEU.1: Leaning to force: the calls for annexation are loud.
DEU.3: The country weighs force against accommodation.
DEU.5: Leaning to accommodation: more want to settle with the neighbours by talk.
DEU.6: A peace without annexations is what the country wants.

RUS.0: One Russia, one tongue, one Church; the other peoples keep their heads down.
RUS.1: Leaning to One Russia: even the border schools teach only in Russian.
RUS.2: Leaning a little to One Russia.
RUS.3: The empire and its peoples watch each other.
RUS.4: Leaning a little to the nations.
RUS.5: Leaning to the nations: Poland and Finland speak for themselves.
RUS.6: Every people of the empire has its own diet and its own schools.

AUH.0: The Emperor's decree is the law; parliament might as well not be there.

AUH.3: Decree and parliament hold each other in check.
AUH.5: Leaning to parliament: ministers come to the house and answer.
AUH.6: Parliament governs; the Emperor only sits above it.

DEU.0: The Kaiser's will and the army's are the country's will.
DEU.1: Leaning to the Crown: parliament talks, but does not decide.
DEU.2: Leaning a little to the Crown.
DEU.3: Crown and parliament hold each other in check.
DEU.5: Leaning to parliament: the chancellor minds the house.

FRA.0: A strong hand holds the country; the Chamber only applauds.
FRA.1: Leaning to authority: the generals and the leagues speak loudly.
FRA.3: Authority and the Republic hold each other in check.
FRA.4: Leaning a little to the Republic.
FRA.5: Leaning to the Republic: the Chamber holds the cabinet.
FRA.6: The Republic's principles stand above everything.

GBR.0: The state holds men, works and papers in its hands.
GBR.1: Leaning to control: government orders reach far.
GBR.3: Control and liberty are evenly matched.
GBR.5: Leaning to liberty: much is left alone by the state.
GBR.6: The old Liberal state: the state keeps out of people's lives.

RUS.0: Nothing but the Tsar's will; the Duma is a name.
RUS.1: Leaning to autocracy: the ministers look only to the court.

RUS.4: Leaning a little to the Duma.
RUS.5: Leaning to the Duma: it summons ministers and questions them.
RUS.6: The Duma makes the ministers; the Tsar only signs.

GBR.0: One Union, one Empire, not an inch to divide: that view has won.

GBR.2: Leaning a little to the Union.
GBR.3: Union and Home Rule are evenly matched.
GBR.4: Leaning a little to Home Rule.
GBR.5: Leaning to Home Rule: a parliament in Dublin is the common view.
GBR.6: Ireland and the dominions settling their own affairs is taken for granted.

help_modal.action_attack_altclick: Attack (when left click is set to open menu)
help_modal.action_esc: Closes menu. Cancels unit build preview.
help_modal.action_warship_multiselect: Select multiple warships (drag to draw selection box)
help_modal.ally_betray: Betray your ally, ending the alliance, halting trade, and weakening your defense. Trading between you is paused for 5 minutes (or until you become allies again) and others may stop trading too. And unless the other player was a traitor themselves, you'll be marked a traitor for 30 seconds. During this time an icon will be above your name and you will have a 50% defense debuff. Tribes are less likely to ally with you and players will think twice before doing so.
help_modal.ally_donate: Donate some of your troops to your ally. Used when they're low on troops and are being attacked, or when they need that extra power to crush an enemy.
help_modal.ally_donate_gold: Donate some of your gold to your ally. Used when they're low on gold and need it for buildings, or when your team member is saving for that MIRV.
help_modal.build_atom_desc: Small explosive bomb that destroys territory, buildings, ships and boats. Spawns from the nearest Missile Silo and lands in the area you first clicked to build it.
help_modal.build_city_desc: Increases your max population. Useful when you can't expand your territory or you're about to hit your population limit.
help_modal.build_defense_desc: Increases defenses around nearby borders, which show a checkered pattern. Attacks from enemies are slower and have more casualties.
help_modal.build_factory_desc: Automatically builds railroads to nearby cities, ports and other factories, and can also link up with friendly neighbors. Trains spawn regularly and give you a fixed amount of gold for each building they visit along the route, with extra gold for visiting your neighbors' buildings.
help_modal.build_hydrogen_desc: Large explosive bomb. Spawns from the nearest Missile Silo and lands in the area you first clicked to build it.
help_modal.build_menu_desc: Build these or see how many of each you already build:
help_modal.build_mirv_desc: The most powerful bomb in the game. Splits up into smaller bombs that will cover a huge range of territory. Only damages the player that you first clicked on to build it. Spawns from the nearest Missile Silo and lands in the area you first clicked to build it.
help_modal.build_port_desc: Can only be built near water. Allows building Warships. Automatically sends trade ships between ports of your country and other countries (except when trade is stopped), giving gold to both sides. Trade with a player stops automatically when you attack or are attacked by a player. It resumes after 5 minutes or if you become allies. You can manually toggle trading with "Stop trading" or "Start trading".
help_modal.build_sam_desc: Can intercept enemy missiles in its 100 pixel range. The SAM has a 7.5 second cooldown.
help_modal.build_warship_desc: Patrols in an area, capturing enemy trade ships and destroying their Boats (transport ships) and Warships. Spawns from the nearest Port and patrols the area you first clicked to build it. You can control Warships by attack-clicking on them (see action Attack under Hotkeys) and then attack-clicking the new area you want them to move to. Warships can level up (max level 3) by capturing enemy trade ships and destroying their transport boats and Warships. Leveling up increases the Warship's damage and health.
help_modal.exit_confirmation: Are you sure you want to exit the game?
help_modal.icon_ally: Handshake - Ally. This player is your ally.
help_modal.icon_crown: Crown - Number 1. This is the top player in the leaderboard.
help_modal.icon_desc: Examples of some of the ingame icons you will encounter and what they mean:
help_modal.icon_embargo: Dollar stop sign - Embargo. This player has stopped trading with you automatically or manually.
help_modal.icon_request: Envelope - Alliance request. This player has sent you an alliance request.
help_modal.icon_traitor: Broken shield - Traitor. This player attacked an ally.
help_modal.in_game_tutorial_desc: Learn by playing: a solo game with a step-by-step guide that walks you through spawning, attacking, building and nukes.
help_modal.info_alliance: Send an alliance request to the player. Allies can share resources and troops, but can't attack each other.
help_modal.info_ally_desc: When you ally with a player, the following new icons become available:
help_modal.info_chat: Send a quick chat message to the player. Select a Category, a Phrase, and if the phrase contains [P1] select a Player name to replace it with. Hit Send.
help_modal.info_emoji: Send an emoji to the player.
help_modal.info_enemy_desc: Contains information such as the selected player's name, gold, troops, stopped trading with you, nukes sent to you, and if the player is a traitor. Stopped trading means you won't receive gold from them and they won't sent you gold via trade ships. Manually (if the player clicked "Stop trading", which lasts until you both click "Start trading") or automatically (if you betrayed your alliance, which lasts until you become allies again or after 5 minutes). Traitor displays Yes for 30 seconds when the player betrayed and attacked a player who was in an alliance with them. The icons below represent the following interactions:
help_modal.info_target: Place a target mark on the player, marking it for all allies, used to coordinate attacks.
help_modal.info_trade: Use "Stop trading" to stop giving the player gold and receiving their gold via trade ships. If you both click "Start trading" it will start again.
help_modal.option_pause: Pause/Unpause the game - Unavailable in public games.
help_modal.option_settings: Settings - Open the settings menu. Inside you can toggle things like Alternate view, Emojis, Dark Mode, Hidden names, action on left click and more.
help_modal.option_speed: Speed - Adjust the game speed. Unavailable in public games.
help_modal.option_timer: Timer - Time passed since the start of the game.
help_modal.radial_boat: Send a Boat (transport ship) to attack at the selected location. Only available if you have access to water.
help_modal.radial_desc: Right clicking (or touch on mobile) opens the Radial menu. Right click outside it to close it. From the menu you can:
help_modal.radial_donate_gold: Opens the gold donation slider menu so you can quickly send allies gold.
help_modal.radial_donate_troops: Donate troops equivalent to your attack ratio slider percentage to the ally you opened the radial menu on.
help_modal.troubleshooting_desc: If you experience performance issues, crashes, or other problems while playing, please visit our Troubleshooting page for help diagnosing and fixing common issues:
help_modal.ui_attack_ratio: Attack ratio - The amount of troops that will be used when you attack. You can adjust the attack ratio using the slider. Having more attacking troops than defending troops will make you lose fewer troops in the attack, while having less will increase the damage dealt to your attacking troops. The effect doesn't go beyond ratios of 2:1.
help_modal.ui_control_desc: The control panel contains the following elements:
help_modal.ui_events_alliance: Alliance - Alliance requests can be accepted or rejected. Allies can share resources and troops, but can't attack each other. Clicking Focus moves the view to the player who sent the request.
help_modal.ui_events_attack: Attacks - Incoming attacks and your outgoing attacks are shown. Click the message to center the view on the attack, nuke or Boat (transport ship). You can retreat troops by clicking the red X button. This will cost the lives of 25% of your attacking troops. If you retrieve a Boat attack, the boat returns to its starting point and will attack there if the land has been captured since. Nukes can't be retreated once launched.
help_modal.ui_events_desc: The Event panel displays the latest events, requests and Quick Chat messages. Some examples are:
help_modal.ui_events_quickchat: Quick Chat - You can see sent and received chat messages here. Send a message to a player by clicking the Quick Chat icon in their Info menu.
help_modal.ui_gold: Gold - The amount of gold you have and the rate at which you gain it.
help_modal.ui_leaderboard_desc: Shows the top players of the game and their names, % owned land, gold and troops. Using Show All shows all players in the game. If you don't want to see the leaderboard, click Hide.
help_modal.ui_options_desc: The following elements can be found inside:
help_modal.ui_playeroverlay_desc: When you hover over a country, the Player info overlay appears. It shows the player type (Human, Nation, or Tribe), a Nation's attitude toward you (Hostile to Friendly), defending troops, gold, and the number of Warships and buildings they have.

mode_selector.ranked_pairing_note: In team modes, clanmates and friends in the queue are placed on the same team where possible. Friends are paired first, then clanmates. tutorial.complete: You're ready! Good luck out there.

step.alliance_info: Allies can't attack each other. You can break an alliance at any time — but doing so marks you as a traitor.
step.atom_info: Atom Bomb — small tactical strikes that take out structures.
step.attack_nations: Nations have cut you off from the tribes. Attack a neighboring nation instead — they're stronger than tribes, so bring plenty of troops. The nearest ones are marked with a target. Conquer them until you have {cost} gold for a City.
step.attack_ratio: The attack ratio bar sets how many of your troops are sent out with each attack. Drag the slider to adjust it.
step.attack_wilderness: The pulsing ring marks your territory. Click on the unclaimed land next to it to attack and expand.
step.buy_city: You can afford a City! Press {key} (or tap the City icon under the control panel twice: the first tap shows its card, the second starts building), then tap your territory to place it. Cities raise your max troops.
step.buy_defense_post: Now build a Defense Post: press {key}, then click your territory near a border. Attacks on the land around it are much slower and cost the enemy far more troops.
step.buy_factory: Now build a Factory: press {key}, then click your territory to place it.
step.buy_port: Next, build a Port: press {key}, then click your coastline to place it.
step.buy_silo: Finally, build a Missile Silo: press {key}, then click your territory to place it. Silos launch atom bombs, hydrogen bombs and MIRVs.
step.buy_warship: Now build a Warship: press {key}, then click open water near your port. Warships capture trade ships and protect your waters.
step.capture_tribes: Capturing tribes is a great way to earn gold — the nearest ones are marked with a target on the map. Conquer them until you have {cost} gold for a City.
step.earn_gold: Attack neighbors to steal their land, conquer them to take their gold. You need {cost} for a {unit}.
step.factory_info: Factories are connected to cities and other factories by tracks, and spawn trains that grant gold.
step.hydrogen_info: Hydrogen Bomb — large strategic strikes that weaken the enemy.
step.launch_atom: Your silo is armed! Press {key}, then click a neighbor's territory to launch an Atom Bomb.
step.mirv_info: MIRV — a massive missile attack to cripple your enemy.
step.no_coast: You have no coastline yet. Water access is very important — it lets you send boats, build ports and trade by sea. Expand your territory until it reaches the coast.
step.port_info_ships: Ports send out trade ships, which earn you gold.
step.port_info_warships: Ports can also be used to construct warships.
step.propose_alliance: Allies secure your borders. Right-click the nation marked with a target and propose an alliance.
step.sam_info: SAM Launcher — defends against nuclear strikes by shooting down incoming missiles.
step.send_boat: Boats send your troops across water. Right-click an enemy coastline across the water to open the radial menu, then select the boat.
step.silo_loading: Your Missile Silo is loading — a nuke can be launched once it's fully ready.
step.spawn: Click anywhere on the map to pick where you spawn.
step.spawn_wait: Spot picked! You can still move it until the timer runs out — the game starts then.
step.traitor_info: Traitors get a large defense debuff for 30 seconds, so be careful.
step.troop_rate: This is your troop growth rate. Growth slows down and turns orange once your troops approach half of your max.
step.troops: Keep an eye on your troop count. Attacking with too few troops leaves you weak — let them regrow between attacks.

step_touch.attack_wilderness: The pulsing ring marks your territory. Tap the unclaimed land next to it, then tap the sword in the middle of the menu to attack.
step_touch.buy_city: You can afford a City! Tap the City icon under the control panel twice (the first tap shows its card, the second starts building). Then tap your territory to place the City there, and tap it again to build it. Cities raise your max troops.
step_touch.buy_defense_post: Now build a Defense Post: tap your territory near a border, open the wrench menu and pick Defense Post. Attacks on the land around it are much slower and cost the enemy far more troops.
step_touch.buy_factory: Now build a Factory: tap your territory, open the wrench menu and pick Factory.
step_touch.buy_port: Next, build a Port: tap your coastline, open the wrench menu and pick Port.
step_touch.buy_silo: Finally, build a Missile Silo: tap your territory, open the wrench menu and pick Missile Silo. Silos launch atom bombs, hydrogen bombs and MIRVs.
step_touch.buy_warship: Now build a Warship: tap open water near your port, open the sword menu and pick Warship. Warships capture trade ships and protect your waters.
step_touch.launch_atom: Your silo is armed! Tap a neighbor's territory, open the sword menu and pick Atom Bomb.
step_touch.propose_alliance: Allies secure your borders. Tap the nation marked with a target, then tap the handshake to propose an alliance.
