event_desc.deu_annex_west_poland: The Polish government has fled abroad and fights on from exile. Our administrators propose to join the western provinces, the corridor, Posen and eastern Upper Silesia, to the Reich by decree rather than wait for a peace treaty.
event_desc.deu_army_command: War Minister Blomberg has resigned, and the army's commander-in-chief Fritsch has been pushed out as well. Hitler means to abolish the War Ministry and command the armed forces directly through a newly created High Command of the Armed Forces. Among the generals there is talk that the army's independence is over.
event_desc.deu_austria_refused: The Austrian government has rejected the demand for union and vowed to defend its independence by plebiscite. Troops are already massed at the border. Sending them in means war; backing down shakes the regime's prestige.
event_desc.deu_case_anton: With the Allies in North Africa, Berlin no longer trusts the armistice. German columns cross the demarcation line towards the Mediterranean coast and Italian troops land on Corsica. The French State keeps its ministers but loses its last unoccupied territory.
event_desc.deu_compiegne_armistice: In the railway carriage where Germany signed the armistice of 1918, French envoys accept German terms. The north and the Atlantic coast stay occupied, a French government keeps the south and the empire, and the fleet is to be disarmed in its home ports.
event_desc.deu_croatian_state: Yugoslavia has collapsed, and its king and government have fled abroad. In Zagreb a nationalist movement has proclaimed an independent Croatian state and asks for our recognition. It would take in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Italy expects its share of the coast.
event_desc.deu_denmark_takeover: Strikes and sabotage have spread through Danish towns, and the government in Copenhagen has refused our demand for emergency measures. Our plenipotentiary proposes to end the policy of cooperation, disarm the Danish forces and rule the country directly.
event_desc.deu_hungary_coup: The Hungarian Regent has broadcast an armistice. Our troops in Budapest and the Hungarian officers who reject it can take the castle hill, make the Regent step down and hand power to a government that will keep Hungary in the war.
event_desc.deu_italy_betrayal: Rome has announced an armistice with the Allies behind our backs. Our divisions in Italy are ordered to disarm the Italian army, take the Alpine passes and the northern cities, and hold the peninsula as far south as they can.
event_desc.deu_july_plot: A bomb has gone off during a briefing at Hitler's headquarters in East Prussia. In Berlin, officers are using the reserve army's mobilization plan to take over government offices. Within hours it will be decided.
event_desc.deu_mr_pact_offer: Moscow has proposed a non-aggression treaty first. The Soviet foreign commissar also wants to discuss a secret protocol dividing Eastern Europe into spheres of interest. Signing would leave Germany free to face the West without worrying about the East.
event_desc.deu_occupy_hungary: Our envoys report that Budapest is seeking a separate peace while the Red Army nears the Carpathians. The Regent has been summoned to talks in Austria; while he is away, our divisions can secure Hungary and install a reliable government.
event_desc.deu_olympics: The XI Olympic Games open in Berlin. The government has built a new stadium and dressed the streets for foreign visitors. For two weeks the eyes of the world are on Germany, and the regime means to show it a calm and orderly country.
event_desc.deu_poland: German forces crossed the border into Poland at dawn. Panzer divisions and dive bombers lead the way while the Polish army fights back all along the frontier. The question now is whether Poland's allies will keep their word.
event_desc.deu_renounce_polish_pact: Poland has flatly refused the demands over Danzig and the Corridor. Berlin holds that the 1934 German–Polish declaration of non-aggression no longer means anything and prepares to announce in the Reichstag that it is void.
event_desc.deu_rhineland_bluff: France has begun to mobilize in answer to the march into the Rhineland. The generals warn that the few battalions on the border cannot stop the French army. Pulling back costs face; standing firm means risking war.
event_desc.deu_september_coup: Officers around General Ludwig Beck have finally moved. Troops of the Berlin military district are heading for the government quarter, but no one knows how the police and the party will respond. The officers mean to arrest the regime's leaders and form a provisional government.
event_desc.deu_social_republic: German paratroopers have freed Mussolini from his mountain prison. He is ready to head a fascist government in the north of Italy, seated at Salò on Lake Garda, that would keep the occupied provinces at our side.
event_desc.deu_sudeten_refused: Czechoslovakia refuses to give up the Sudetenland. Its border fortifications are strong, and no one knows what the Western powers will do. Choosing war may mean a wider conflict; stepping back costs the regime face.
event_desc.deu_tripartite_signing: Germany has sent the text of a treaty to be signed together in Berlin. The three powers recognize each other's new order in Europe and East Asia and pledge to stand together if any of them is attacked by a power not yet in the war.
event_desc.deu_vienna_award_1: After Munich, Hungary asks for arbitration to recover the Hungarian-populated districts of southern Czechoslovakia. The German and Italian foreign ministers offer to draw a new border in Vienna. If the award goes ahead, southern Slovakia passes to Hungary.
event_desc.deu_vienna_award_2: With Romania having yielded Bessarabia to the Soviets, Hungary demands Transylvania and threatens war. Needing Romania's oil safe, Germany joins Italy in arbitrating once more to draw a line between the two.
event_desc.dnk_german_treaty: Berlin offers Copenhagen a treaty of non-aggression. Sweden and Norway have declined the same offer, but Denmark shares a land border with Germany and has almost no army to defend it. Signing would calm relations with Berlin but displease London.
event_desc.dom_statute_debate: Parliament debates adopting the Statute of Westminster of 1931, which the dominion has not yet made its own. Supporters say the dominion's laws must rest on its own authority, not on Westminster's. Opponents fear that it loosens the bond with Britain.
event_desc.esn_banker_credit: A Majorcan financier who backed the rising offers credit in London and Rome: enough to pay for the first aircraft, the first fuel and the first months of the war.
event_desc.esn_carlist_defiance: The Traditionalists have grown strong inside the single party. Their leader opens a royal military academy without asking the head of state, and the Requetés march under their own flags.
event_desc.esn_eastern_volunteers: Germany has attacked the Soviet Union. In Madrid the Falange calls for volunteers to repay the debt of the civil war, while staying out of the war with the West.
event_desc.esn_generals_letter: Several lieutenant generals sign a courteous letter asking the head of state to restore the monarchy. Courteous, but it is the army asking.
event_desc.esn_hisma_offer: A German trading company offers to handle all Nationalist purchases in Germany. It wants payment in kind: iron ore, pyrites and wolfram from Spanish mines, with rights to the mines themselves to follow.
event_desc.esn_hungry_years: The harvest is poor, the fields lack fertiliser and the trucks lack fuel. Bread is rationed, and the black market is the only full shop in town.
event_desc.esn_iberian_union: Spain proposes that the two Iberian states become one: a union of equals, it says, with Portugal's laws and language kept. Lisbon remembers the last time the crowns were joined.
event_desc.esn_oil_pressure: Washington and London halt oil shipments to Spain until the wolfram sales to Germany end. The tankers wait in port, and the reserves will not last the season.
event_desc.esn_old_shirts: Falangists who joined before the war complain that the generals and the bishops have stolen their revolution. They want the syndicates, the land reform and the purge they were promised.
event_desc.esn_pretender_manifesto: From exile the heir to the throne publishes a manifesto: the regime is tied to the defeated powers, and only a constitutional monarchy can bring Spain back into the world. Monarchist officers read it with interest.
event_desc.esn_rock_offer: German envoys propose a joint assault on Gibraltar. Spain would get the Rock; Germany would get the Strait closed to the British fleet. They say little about Morocco, grain or fuel.
event_desc.esn_shrine_incident: At a mass for Carlist war dead, Falangists throw grenades into the crowd leaving the shrine. A minister of the army was among the faithful, and both camps demand the other's heads.
event_desc.esn_sierra_raids: Guerrilla bands strike a Civil Guard post, a mine office and a train. In the mountain villages nobody saw anything.
event_desc.esn_tangier_zone: Spanish troops have entered the international zone of Tangier. The other powers protest, but none of them can spare a battalion to do more.
event_desc.esn_unification_crisis: The decree merging Falange and Carlists into one party has been read out in Salamanca. The Falange's national chief refuses a seat on the new party's junta, and his followers talk of resistance. The Carlists obey, but sullenly.
event_desc.esn_world_turns_away: The victors of the war bar Spain from their new organisation and recall their ambassadors from Madrid. The regime stands alone, as the last survivor of a defeated order.
event_desc.esp_civil_war: Army garrisons in Morocco and across the mainland have risen against the Republic. Where the rising failed, workers' militias hold the streets; where it succeeded, the generals rule. Spain is split in two. Foreign governments weigh which side to help.
event_desc.esp_civil_war_ends: The last resistance of the other side has collapsed and the guns have fallen silent across Spain. The victors now govern the whole country and must rebuild the towns, railways and fields the war has ruined.
event_desc.esp_civil_war_won: The other side has collapsed and the guns have fallen silent across Spain. The country is exhausted and divided, but the war that split it in two is over. Towns lie in ruins and many thousands have fled across the border.
event_desc.esr_after_victory: The guns have fallen silent and the Republic has won. The coalition that fought together must now decide what it fought for.
event_desc.esr_arms_for_unions: Crowds outside the ministries demand weapons. The rising has failed in the great cities only where the workers fought it. Open the arsenals, or trust the few loyal regiments?
event_desc.esr_brigades_farewell: The International Brigades march through Barcelona for the last time, under a rain of flowers. 'You are history,' a speaker tells them.
event_desc.esr_bt_regiment: A regiment of fast wheel-and-track tanks has arrived, with Spanish crews trained for them. It is the Republic's strongest armoured force.
event_desc.esr_committees_rule: In the rear the committees requisition, judge and govern as they please. The ministries' orders go unread.
event_desc.esr_french_border: For a few weeks Paris lets the trains and lorries through. It may close the border again at any time.
event_desc.esr_international_brigades: Volunteers from dozens of countries are arriving at Albacete to fight for the Republic. Many have never held a rifle, but they come with conviction, and the government has agreed to organise them into brigades of their own.
event_desc.esr_kirovabad_pilots: The first class of Spanish pilots trained in the Soviet Union has returned. They take over the squadrons from the foreign volunteers.
event_desc.esr_komsomol_arrives: A Soviet freighter has docked at Cartagena. Under the crates of 'agricultural machinery' are tanks, with their crews and instructors.
event_desc.esr_may_days: Assault Guards tried to take the telephone exchange from the anarchist union. Now there are barricades in Barcelona, and the parties of the Republic fire on each other.
event_desc.esr_mexican_shipment: A Mexican ship unloads rifles and cartridges. It is little, but it was sold openly by a government that calls the Republic its friend.
event_desc.esr_north_cut_off: The northern coast, with its mines and yards, has fallen. Thousands of soldiers and civilians wait in the harbours.
event_desc.esr_officers_plot: Senior commanders meet with moderate politicians. They say the war is lost and only soldiers can end it.
event_desc.esr_paris_purchases: Dealers in Paris, Antwerp and Prague offer rifles and aircraft, at prices that rise with every refusal of a government to sell.
event_desc.esr_pce_demands: The Communists hold the army's key posts and now ask for the ministries that control the police and the supplies.
event_desc.esr_peace_feelers: Diplomats hint that a mediated peace might be possible. The other side answers that it accepts only surrender.
event_desc.esr_popular_front: The left-wing Popular Front has narrowly won the February general election. A Republican government takes office amid strikes, land seizures and street fighting, while army officers and the right talk openly of a rising. The country is pulling apart.
event_desc.esr_rif_rising: The Republic has promised the Moroccans their independence. Tribes in the protectorate grow restless and recruiting falls off.
event_desc.esr_ships_sunk: Freighters bound for the Republic's ports have been torpedoed by submarines whose flag no one will admit. Their cargoes are on the sea bed.
event_desc.esr_soviet_planes: Snub-nosed biplanes and fast monoplanes appear over the capital, and fast twin-engined bombers with them. The enemy no longer owns the sky.
event_desc.esr_soviet_shipments: More ships have run the gauntlet of the Mediterranean with tanks, aircraft and guns. Moscow sends its bill with them.
event_desc.eth_restoration: British and Commonwealth troops, with Ethiopian patriot fighters, have driven the Italians from Addis Ababa. Emperor Haile Selassie, in exile since 1936, is ready to enter his capital five years to the day after the Italians took it.
event_desc.fin_ev_aland_moscow: The Soviet government asks to see the plans and hints that it would rather fortify the islands itself.
event_desc.fin_ev_aland_proposal: Finland asks Sweden to share the defence of the Åland Islands, demilitarised since the League's ruling. Swedish ministers are tempted and wary.
event_desc.fin_ev_armistice_terms: The Soviet Union will make peace if Finland gives up the 1940 border again, leases a base near Helsinki and expels the German army from its soil.
event_desc.fin_ev_estonia_union_offer: Helsinki offers Tallinn one state, one army and one coast from Tornio to Narva. Estonia would keep its language and its schools.
event_desc.fin_ev_ikl_ban: The interior minister's case against the Patriotic People's Movement reaches the court. The judges dislike the movement and dislike the minister's haste more.
event_desc.fin_ev_karelian_refugees: A tenth of the nation has left the ceded lands rather than live under Soviet rule. They need homes, farms and work.
event_desc.fin_ev_kingdom_offer: The king elected in 1918 renounced the throne. The monarchists must decide whether to seek a prince abroad or a regent at home.
event_desc.fin_ev_lotta_drive: Lotta Svärd's local branches hold bazaars and lotteries across the country. What should the money buy?
event_desc.fin_ev_motti_victory: A whole enemy division is cut into pockets along a forest road. Its men burn their trucks to keep warm.
event_desc.fin_ev_new_order_leader: The patriotic state needs one face. The party apparatus and the youth league each have their man.
event_desc.fin_ev_nickel_dispute: Germany and Britain both want the nickel of Petsamo, and Moscow wants a say in the company. Whoever gets it will remember who refused.
event_desc.fin_ev_peasant_march: Columns of farmers in their Sunday clothes walk towards the capital behind the movement's flags.
event_desc.fin_ev_presidential_election: The electoral college meets in Helsinki. The Agrarians and Social Democrats will not vote for Svinhufvud again, but they must agree on someone.
event_desc.fin_ev_quiet_envoy: A second secretary of the Soviet embassy asks the foreign minister for talks no one else may know of. Leningrad, he says, fears a German landing in Finland.
event_desc.fin_ev_red_cells: The detective police find printing presses and lists of names in a Tampere workers' hall.
event_desc.fin_ev_red_earth: The Agrarian leader offers the Social Democrats seats in the cabinet. For the first time since the civil war the workers' party would share power.
event_desc.fin_ev_red_government: The Comintern has its veteran in Moscow; the Finnish workers have their own hero, just out of prison.
event_desc.fin_ev_transit_request: Berlin asks for the right to move soldiers and supplies by rail through Finland to northern Norway. It offers guns in return.
event_desc.fin_ev_volunteer_call: Helsinki asks for the volunteer corps the Swedish officers promised. Thousands of young Swedes are already queuing at the recruiting offices.
event_desc.fin_ev_western_aid: Fighters from Britain, France and Italy, rifles from everywhere and volunteers from as far as America arrive by way of Sweden.
event_desc.fin_ev_winter_war: Soviet guns open fire along the whole border. The country that was split in two in 1918 answers as one.
event_desc.fin_moscow_armistice: The Soviet summer offensive has broken our lines on the Karelian Isthmus. Moscow's terms: the 1940 border, Petsamo, a lease on the Porkkala peninsula, reparations, and the removal of German troops from Finnish soil, by force if need be.
event_desc.fin_moscow_peace: Moscow offers peace at a heavy price: the whole Karelian Isthmus with Viipuri, the shores of Lake Ladoga and land in the far north. The army can hold for weeks more, not months, and Western help has not arrived.
event_desc.fin_soviet_demands: Moscow demands that we move the border on the Karelian Isthmus back from Leningrad, hand over islands in the Gulf of Finland and lease the port of Hanko as a naval base. Our delegates have come home to consult the government. Most Finns oppose any concession.
event_desc.fin_winter_war_flag: Soviet troops have crossed the Finnish border and bombers have struck Helsinki. Finland's small army digs in on the Karelian Isthmus and in the frozen forests to the north. Most observers expect the fight to last only weeks.
event_desc.fra_daladier: The second Blum cabinet has fallen after less than a month. Édouard Daladier, the Radical minister of war, forms a government that leans to the centre and promises to put rearmament before reform. Parliament prepares to let him govern by decree.
event_desc.fra_election_1936: France goes to the polls deeply divided. The Popular Front of Radicals, Socialists and Communists promises bread, peace and freedom; the parties of the right warn of disorder and strikes. The second round will decide who governs.
event_desc.fra_free_french_africa: Governor Félix Éboué announces that Chad stands with Free France. Within days Cameroon and the French Congo follow, giving General de Gaulle land of his own, a capital at Brazzaville and a road across Africa.
event_desc.fra_hatay_cession: Ankara asks France to let the Sanjak of Alexandretta, now the State of Hatay, join Turkey. Syrian nationalists will call it a betrayal of the mandate, but Turkish goodwill could matter greatly in the Mediterranean if war comes.
event_desc.fra_joins_guarantee: London has pledged to defend an eastern European state against aggression and asks Paris to join the guarantee. France already has treaties of its own in the east; standing beside Britain would show that the two democracies act as one.
event_desc.fra_paris_uprising: Allied armies are closing on the capital. The police, the railwaymen and the resistance groups of Paris seize public buildings and put up barricades against the German garrison.
event_desc.fra_regime_crisis: The entry of the leagues into government has split the country. Strikes and street demonstrations spread, and both the ministers and the parties of the left claim to be defending France.
event_desc.fra_rhineland_response: German battalions have marched into the demilitarised Rhineland, tearing up the Locarno treaty. The General Staff says any answer means general mobilisation weeks before an election, and London urges restraint. Every day of hesitation makes the new line harder to undo.
event_desc.fra_wartime_unity: A year of war has quieted the quarrels of the Third Republic. Parties that fought each other in the streets in 1934 now sit together, and strikes have given way to long shifts in the arms factories. At last France fights the war with one voice.
event_desc.gbr_abdication: Edward VIII insists on marrying Wallis Simpson, who has been divorced twice. The Prime Minister and the Dominion governments refuse to accept her as Queen. Either the King goes or the government does.
event_desc.gbr_abdication_settled: The Duke of York has become King George VI. Shy and troubled by a stammer, he reassures the country with his steady manner. The crisis has passed, and Parliament and Palace return to their normal business.
event_desc.gbr_anglo_soviet_agreement: Three weeks after Germany invaded the Soviet Union, Britain and the USSR sign an agreement in Moscow. Each promises to help the other in the war against Germany and never to make a separate peace.
event_desc.gbr_attlee_government: Labour leader Clement Attlee is now at the head of the government. Trade union leaders take ministerial posts, and the government promises to tackle unemployment and rearmament together through planning.
event_desc.gbr_aus_unrest: Strikes close the docks of Sydney and Melbourne, and old soldiers march behind the banners of the dissolved houses.
event_desc.gbr_can_unrest: Quebec and Ontario, long at odds, find a common cause in refusing the Crown's orders. Mass meetings and walk-outs spread along the border.
event_desc.gbr_chamberlain: Stanley Baldwin retires after the coronation. The Chancellor of the Exchequer, Neville Chamberlain, becomes Conservative leader and Prime Minister, convinced that patient negotiation can keep the peace in Europe.
event_desc.gbr_churchill: Disappointed with the conduct of the war, the House of Commons turns on the government. Labour refuses to serve under Chamberlain, so he resigns, and Winston Churchill forms a government of all parties.
event_desc.gbr_democratic_uprising: Outside Westminster the parties of the old Parliament still hold the loyalty of millions. Councils refuse orders, unions walk out and crowds fill the squares. A steady regime can break the movement by force; an unsteady one watches the realm divide.
event_desc.gbr_eden_resigns: Foreign Secretary Anthony Eden resigns after clashing with the Prime Minister over talks with Italy. Chamberlain wants to deal with Mussolini now; Eden wants concessions from Rome first. Lord Halifax takes over the Foreign Office.
event_desc.gbr_eden_returns: Lord Halifax leaves for Washington as ambassador. Anthony Eden returns to the Foreign Office, where wartime diplomacy now means keeping the Americans and the Soviets close.
event_desc.gbr_election_1945: With the war in Europe over, the coalition breaks up and the first general election in ten years is held. The count waited three weeks for the servicemen's votes. The country has chosen between the leader who won the war and a promise to rebuild.
event_desc.gbr_habbaniya: Iraqi troops have taken the heights above our air base at Habbaniya and threaten the road to the Gulf oil fields. The government in Baghdad will not pull them back. Under the 1930 treaty we have the right to move troops through Iraq.
event_desc.gbr_kings_party_settled: Parliament lets the matter rest. The King keeps his throne, his friends keep their places at court, and the cabinet that tried to remove him learns not to try again.
event_desc.gbr_levant_campaign: German aircraft bound for Iraq have refuelled on Vichy airfields in Syria. The Levant could become an Axis foothold beside Suez. Our forces in Palestine, with the Free French, are ready to march on Damascus and Beirut.
event_desc.gbr_mers_el_kebir: A large part of the French battle fleet lies at Mers-el-Kébir near Oran, and Britain cannot risk those ships passing to Germany. A British squadron arrives off the harbour with terms: sail with us, sail to a distant port under guard, or scuttle.
event_desc.gbr_new_king: On 20 January 1936 King George V dies at Sandringham, and the Prince of Wales succeeds him as Edward VIII. The new King is popular, but his attachment to an American divorcée already worries the Cabinet.
event_desc.gbr_non_intervention_committee: Delegates of twenty-seven governments meet in London and agree that no arms will reach either side in Spain. Germany, Italy and the Soviet Union have signed too, and few expect them to keep their word. Staying out may spare Europe a wider war, or simply leave the Republic alone.
event_desc.gbr_nzl_unrest: Crowds gather in Auckland and Wellington to protest the loss of their parliament. The governor asks what London wishes done.
event_desc.gbr_prague_shock: German troops have entered Prague, less than six months after the promises made at Munich. In a speech in Birmingham the Prime Minister asks whether this is the last attack on a small state, and public opinion decides that the time for concessions is over.
event_desc.gbr_raj_unrest: Unrest sweeps from Bengal to Bombay. Marches, strikes and attacks on the stations of the garrison strain every district office, and the news travels faster than the troops.
event_desc.gbr_soviet_alliance_offer: Having turned Germany away, the Soviet government offers Britain and France a treaty of mutual assistance. With it Germany would face enemies in both east and west, but many in London still distrust the Bolsheviks.
event_desc.gbr_soviet_overture: The British ambassador brings the Kremlin a draft pact: neither country will attack the other, and both will stand against aggression. If they are at war, a clause also lets each side's forces cross the other's territory.
event_desc.gbr_zaf_unrest: Riots in Johannesburg and the Cape spread to the mines. The police report that a secret committee is meeting in the Transvaal.
event_desc.gen_call_to_arms: A member of our faction has gone to war and asks us to fight at its side. Answering the call makes its enemy our enemy. Refusing would keep us out of the war but cost us trust within the alliance.
event_desc.gen_coup_done: Overnight, army units and their political allies seized the ministries and the radio station in the capital. The old government has fallen, and the new one has announced its rule on the radio. Rumours in the streets say a foreign power helped.
event_desc.gen_diplo_access: A government asks that its troops be allowed to cross our territory. If we agree, its armies may move through and stay on our soil. We may withdraw permission whenever we wish.
event_desc.gen_diplo_faction_invite: The leader of a faction has invited us to become a member. Members fight together and defend one another. If the faction is at war, we will be at war with its enemies at once.
event_desc.gen_diplo_faction_request: A government has asked to join our faction. Accepting means its borders become a front we must help to hold. A new member takes part in every war the faction fights.
event_desc.gen_diplo_lend_lease: A government asks us to send equipment from our stockpiles every month, shipped at our expense. The supplies would strengthen a useful friend but leave less for our own divisions.
event_desc.gen_diplo_nap: A government proposes a treaty under which neither side will attack the other. While it lasts, neither may justify a war against the other or declare one. Breaking it later would take time and cost us dearly.
event_desc.gen_election: The polls have closed and every ballot box has been opened. The voters decide who should lead parliament, but how the result is received is for the present government to settle. The whole country is watching.
event_desc.gen_exile_formed: The country's armies have been defeated and its land is occupied, but its government has escaped abroad. From an allied capital it keeps its remaining forces in the war and speaks for the occupied people.
event_desc.gen_government_shift: A political movement has won over most of the nation and now speaks for the majority. Crowds and newspapers demand that the cabinet step down and hand over power. The government cannot put off its answer for long.
event_desc.gen_guarantee_called: A country whose independence we guaranteed has been attacked. Keeping our word means war with the aggressor. Standing aside would spare us the fighting, but our promises would carry little weight again.
event_desc.gen_justified_against: Reports say a foreign government has begun building a case for war against us. The newspapers write daily of troop movements and hostile speeches beyond the border. Now is the time to strengthen our defences.
event_desc.gen_munich_conference: Germany demands the Sudetenland and threatens war if it is refused. The leaders of the great powers meet in Munich to settle Czechoslovakia's frontier, with no Czechoslovak at the table. Our word will decide whether Prague is told to yield or is defended.
event_desc.gen_peace_conference: The guns have fallen silent and the victors are gathering to decide the fate of the defeated. Each will press its claims in turn; the larger its part in the victory, the more it can ask for.
event_desc.gen_peace_movement: As the war drags on, rallies and petitions for peace appear across the country. More deputies speak openly of a negotiated end. The government must let the movement be heard or answer it with propaganda.
event_desc.gen_regime_crisis: For more than a month a movement outside the government has held the support of most of the people. Strikes and demonstrations go on, and doubts are spreading among officers and officials. The government must step aside or hold on by force.
event_desc.gen_strike: Workers angered by low wages and rising prices have laid down their tools. Factories stand idle, and the strike is spreading to the docks and railways. The government can bear the lost output or end the strike with concessions.
event_desc.gen_subject_upgrade: A government under our protection asks to manage more of its own affairs. Granting it would loosen our hold but earn goodwill; refusing would keep it close and may push it toward a break.
event_desc.gen_unrest: Distrust of the government has grown, and protests and clashes break out in several cities. Reports say the police alone can no longer keep order. We must wait for calm or declare martial law.
event_desc.gen_uprising: Armed fighters have driven the occupying garrison out of a region and raised their own flag over its town halls. Whether they can hold it depends on how quickly help arrives.
event_desc.gen_volunteers_arrive: A friendly government has sent volunteers to fight at our side. They come with their own officers and equipment and stay under their own command, but they will fight our enemies.
event_desc.gen_war_weariness: Lost provinces and ever longer casualty lists weigh on the people. More men dodge the draft, and the newspapers have grown gloomy. The government can let morale sag or spend heavily to lift it.
event_desc.grc_ev_army_surrender: The northern armies are cut off. Their generals want to surrender to the Germans rather than the Italians, against the government's orders.
event_desc.grc_ev_balkan_summit: The foreign ministers of the Entente meet. The Turks want a firm military convention, the Yugoslavs a softer word toward Sofia.
event_desc.grc_ev_border_incident: A Bulgarian patrol crossed into Greek Thrace and exchanged fire with a frontier post. Sofia calls it a misunderstanding.
event_desc.grc_ev_caretaker_dies: The elderly professor who led the caretaker cabinet has died. His deputy, a general with a handful of deputies, is ready; the parties are not.
event_desc.grc_ev_chania_revolt: Venizelists in Crete have seized the town hall and the radio of Chania and call on the army to restore the constitution.
event_desc.grc_ev_dictator_dies: The premier who ruled since the suspension of parliament has died after a short illness, in the middle of the war. The king must choose a successor.
event_desc.grc_ev_dodecanese_greeks: Rome closes Greek schools in Rhodes and presses the islanders to take Italian names. Their petitions reach Athens.
event_desc.grc_ev_elli_torpedoed: On a holy day, an unknown submarine has sunk the old cruiser Elli at anchor off Tinos. Everyone knows whose submarine it was.
event_desc.grc_ev_expedition_lands: British, Australian and New Zealand troops come ashore at Piraeus. Where should they go?
event_desc.grc_ev_general_strike: After the police fired on the tobacco workers, the unions call a general strike. The premier asks the king for emergency powers.
event_desc.grc_ev_great_famine: Food is requisitioned for the occupiers and the blockade stops the grain ships. In Athens people die in the streets.
event_desc.grc_ev_island_exiles: Wives and mothers of the island exiles petition the palace. Some prisoners have signed declarations of repentance; most have not.
event_desc.grc_ev_king_leaves: The king and the government embark with the gold reserve. Where should the state of Greece carry on?
event_desc.grc_ev_liberation_front: The party has founded a front with small left parties, open to every patriot. Its bands are forming in the mountains.
event_desc.grc_ev_tobacco_harvest: German buyers offer to take the whole leaf crop again, paid in marks that can only be spent in Germany.
event_desc.grc_ev_ultimatum: The Italian minister arrives before dawn: free passage for the Italian army to occupy strategic points, or war. The answer is expected within hours.
event_desc.grc_ev_venizelos_dies: The old Cretan who doubled Greece's size has died in exile. His body comes home to Crete, and both camps watch the crowds.
event_desc.hun_arrow_cross_rally: Tens of thousands in green shirts fill the square, chanting for their leader. The police ask for orders; the cabinet asks the regent.
event_desc.hun_berlin_answers: The Hungarian envoy asks whether Germany will support Hungary's claims. Budapest is useful as a partner and as a lever against Prague and Bucharest.
event_desc.hun_bled_agreement: At a lakeside resort the Little Entente offers to recognise Hungary's right to rearm, if Hungary renounces force against its members. The generals call it a trap; the diplomats call it a first crack in the treaty.
event_desc.hun_danube_offer: Budapest proposes that our two states unite in a federation of the Danube, one market and one army, standing between Berlin and Moscow. It would be the end of our state as we know it.
event_desc.hun_danube_refused: Our neighbour has turned down the offer of union. Old suspicions run deeper than common interest.
event_desc.hun_first_lands_return: Bells ring in every church as the troops cross the old border. For the first time since the treaty, the map on the classroom wall is a little less wrong.
event_desc.hun_flags_of_1848: Moscow offers to return the banners of the 1848 revolution, taken by the Tsar's army when it crushed Hungary's war of independence. In exchange it wants a communist prisoner released.
event_desc.hun_gombos_dies: The prime minister has died after a long illness, his corporate state half built. The regent must choose a successor: a safe man of the old party, or one of the radicals who loved the dead man's plans.
event_desc.hun_horthy_armistice: The Red Army stands on the Great Hungarian Plain. The Regent's envoys in Moscow have agreed preliminary armistice terms, and he is ready to announce on the radio that Hungary is leaving the war. Berlin will not stand by.
event_desc.hun_horthy_succession: Parliament is ready to elect a deputy regent. The regent's eldest son, a pilot and engineer with Western friends, is the favourite; the right fears a dynasty, the legitimists fear a rival to the crown.
event_desc.hun_kassa_bombing: Unidentified aircraft have bombed Kassa. The general staff blames the Soviets and demands war; some officers whisper that the markings were not clear at all.
event_desc.hun_landless_peasants: Writers touring the puszta describe villages of farmhands living like serfs. Their books sell out, and the government is asked what it will do.
event_desc.hun_maort_oil: The wells in Zala are flowing. The concession belongs to a subsidiary of an American oil company, which offers to drill further if its terms are kept; nationalists want the state to take the field.
event_desc.hun_otto_letter: The young Habsburg answers from Belgium: he is ready to serve the Holy Crown when called. The letter is printed in the legitimist papers, and three capitals protest the next morning.
event_desc.hun_revision_complete: Upper Hungary, Ruthenia and Transylvania are all within the border again. The revision the whole country prayed for is done; holding it is another matter.
event_desc.hun_rome_answers: The Hungarian minister asks whether Italy will stand behind his country's claims against its neighbours. Budapest has been a loyal friend since the Rome Protocols.
event_desc.hun_second_lands_return: Another lost province is home. The regent rides in on a white horse, and the crowds that greet him ask where the next border will run.
event_desc.hun_szalasi_trial: The Arrow Cross leader stands accused of incitement against the state. A sentence would make him a martyr to his followers; an acquittal would make him a victor.
event_desc.hun_talks_discovered: Berlin knows about our emissaries. The German minister asks pointed questions about Istanbul and Lisbon, and hints that the prime minister should go.
event_desc.hun_teleki_dilemma: Germany is at war with Yugoslavia and asks for passage and help. We signed a treaty of eternal friendship with Belgrade only months ago. The prime minister says honour forbids it; the general staff says refusal means occupation.
event_desc.imjin_appoint_gwon: Gwon Yul, the governor of Gwangju in Jeolla, has gathered men of his own. He asks the court for a command.
event_desc.imjin_appoint_yi: Ryu Seong-ryong puts forward Yi Sun-sin, the magistrate of Jeongeup, to command the Jeolla Left Navy. It would raise him over several ranks, and the censors already object.
event_desc.imjin_court_shift: The ruling ministers have lost the court's trust. A rival faction now speaks for most of the officials, and its leaders petition the king for the chief councillor's seat.
event_desc.imjin_double_agent: A go-between from the enemy camp says where and when Katō Kiyomasa's ships will cross. The court wants the admiral to sail out and catch them at sea. The admiral suspects a trap.
event_desc.imjin_flight_border: The court stands on the bank of the Yalu, with Ming across the river. Some ministers say a king on foreign soil is no longer a king; others say a king taken by the enemy is worse.
event_desc.imjin_flight_capital: Japanese troops stand one county away from Hanseong. The ministers argue through the night: some beg the king to stay with his people, others to ride north while the roads are open. The crown prince waits for his father's word.
event_desc.imjin_flight_north: The enemy holds the county next to the king's refuge. The people who took him in watch his ministers pack.
event_desc.imjin_jos_chungju: The enemy is marching up from Gyeongsang toward the capital. Sin Rip, commander of the three provinces, wants to meet them with his cavalry on the open ground before Chungju. His aide Kim Yeo-mul begs him to hold the Joryeong pass instead, where a few can stop many. Others want every man pulled back to defend the capital.
event_desc.imjin_jos_crown_prince: The king has no heir. Jeong Cheol, the Westerner left councillor, means to ask him at the royal lecture to name Prince Gwanghae. The king favours Prince Sinseong, and word has already reached him through Lady Kim's family that Jeong Cheol plots against the prince and his mother. The Easterners wait to see Jeong Cheol fall.
event_desc.imjin_jos_defence_system: Japan's letter has the court debating its defences. Under the muster plan, the men of each county gather at a set place when the enemy comes and wait for a commander sent from the capital. Under the old district garrisons, each commander holds his own ground with his own men. Yi Il pressed for the muster plan years ago; others say men left waiting in a field will scatter.
event_desc.imjin_jos_demand: Envoys of the Sō house of Tsushima bring Hideyoshi's demand: Joseon is to let his army pass on its way to Ming.
event_desc.imjin_jos_embassy: Hwang Yun-gil, Kim Seong-il and Heo Seong are back from Japan with Hideyoshi's letter, which speaks of leading an army into Ming. Hwang reports that war will surely come. Kim says he saw no sign of it. Heo Seong, though of Kim's faction, sides with Hwang. The court waits for the king's word.
event_desc.imjin_jos_famine: War has trampled the fields for a year and more. Refugees crowd the roads, and the granaries the enemy did not take are nearly empty. The army needs grain, and so do the starving.
event_desc.imjin_jos_haengju: Gwon Yul has brought his men, with monks and volunteers, up to the old hill fort at Haengju, on the Han River west of the capital. The enemy in Hanseong can see them. Some officers want to stay and fortify; others want to march to join the Ming army.
event_desc.imjin_jos_imjin_river: The enemy holds Hanseong. Kim Myeong-won has gathered what men he can on the north bank of the Imjin River, and the boats have all been drawn over to his side. Some say the river can hold them; others say the army should gather further north, at Pyongyang, and fight there.
event_desc.imjin_jos_jinju: The enemy is gathering against Jinju, the gate to Jeolla. Kim Si-min, its magistrate, has new arquebuses and a few thousand men, and the townsfolk have come inside the walls. Some say the garrison would be better used in Jeolla, behind the mountains.
event_desc.imjin_jos_landing: Japanese ships have put an army ashore on the Gyeongsang coast. The first walled towns are under attack, and their magistrates have refused the enemy's demand to let them pass. Riders carry the news north.
event_desc.imjin_jos_ming_arrives: Ming's soldiers are across the Yalu. Their generals ask for grain, fodder and guides, and want our commanders under their orders. Some ministers say we must give whatever they ask; others say a Joseon army must still be led by Joseon men.
event_desc.imjin_jos_northern_generals: Sin Rip and Yi Il made their names against the Jurchen on the northern border. Some at court want them sent south to look over the walls and the garrisons there. The northern commanders say the Jurchen will not sit still for long.
event_desc.imjin_jos_omens: Fishermen and the Tsushima traders speak of ships being built across the strait and of soldiers gathering in Kyushu.
event_desc.imjin_jos_omens_grave: There is no longer any doubt among the coastal commanders: a great army is gathering at Nagoya, and transport ships fill the harbours of Tsushima.
event_desc.imjin_jos_pyongyang: Ming's great army stands before Pyongyang with its heavy guns, and its generals mean to storm the walls. Our commanders ask whether Joseon's men should go up the ladders beside them, or leave the walls to Ming.
event_desc.imjin_jos_scuttle: Japan's ships cover the sea off our coast and its army is ashore. The fleet's commander asks for orders.
event_desc.imjin_jos_second_war: The talks are over, and the Japanese are crossing the sea again. The court must choose how to meet them.
event_desc.imjin_jos_truce: Ming and Japan have stopped the fighting. The Japanese hold forts on our southern coast, and the Ming generals forbid our armies to attack them while envoys travel.
event_desc.imjin_jos_truce_broken: Word comes from Japan: the Taikō has sent the Ming envoys away in anger. Japan is mustering again.
event_desc.imjin_jos_tsushima: The Sō house's men hint that the Japanese fleet will sail within the month, and the Tsushima traders say the harbours are full of soldiers, though the muster in Kyushu is not yet done.
event_desc.imjin_jos_warn_ming: Hideyoshi's letter speaks of marching through Joseon into Ming. Yi San-hae, the chief councillor, would let it lie: telling Beijing would only raise questions. Ryu Seong-ryong says Ming must hear it from us, or one day it will think we stood with Japan.
event_desc.imjin_jp_busan: Busan and Dongnae are ours. Asked to give the road, the magistrate of Dongnae, Song Sang-hyeon, had answered that it was easy to die and hard to give the road. Now the roads north lie open.
event_desc.imjin_jp_daimyo_grumble: The great lords count their dead and their spent rice. In their camps men ask what the war has given them, and some letters home speak of the Taikō with less respect than before.
event_desc.imjin_jp_embassy: Envoys from Joseon have come to Kyoto and wait at the Jurakudai palace with their king's letter and gifts. Before they go home they will want the Taikō's answer.
event_desc.imjin_jp_hanseong: The Joseon capital is ours. Smoke still rises over the palaces, and the corps commanders gather to ask what comes next.
event_desc.imjin_jp_hidetsugu: Lady Yodo has borne the Taikō a son. Hidetsugu holds the kampaku's title and the home provinces, and the court whispers that the Taikō regrets giving them away.
event_desc.imjin_jp_investiture: At Osaka Castle the Ming envoys come before Hideyoshi, and their letter is read aloud. It names him King of Japan. Of the terms he sent, it says nothing.
event_desc.imjin_jp_investiture_regents: The Ming envoys arrive with a letter for the Taikō, but he is dead. The regents receive them instead.
event_desc.imjin_jp_jinju: Jinju still stands behind its walls on the Nam River and blocks the way into Jeolla. Letters from Nagoya say the Taikō will not forgive it and wants it taken.
event_desc.imjin_jp_kampaku: The muster is under way, and the Taikō means to direct the war from Nagoya. His nephew Hidetsugu is grown and could take the kampaku's title and rule the home provinces while he is away.
event_desc.imjin_jp_long_war: The war has gone on longer than anyone promised. Clothes are worn through, sickness spreads in the camps and the rice ships are late. The commanders ask whether to hold every town they have taken.
event_desc.imjin_jp_ming_army: Ming has come into the war. Its soldiers are crossing the Yalu with horsemen and heavy guns.
event_desc.imjin_jp_ming_reply: Konishi brings back the Ming reply: Beijing will send envoys to the Taikō. Until they come, the armies are to hold the coast and stop the fighting.
event_desc.imjin_jp_noses: The war has begun again. The Taikō wants proof of every enemy killed, and heads are too heavy to ship. His commissioners propose that the corps salt and send noses instead, counted and receipted, with rewards to follow the count.
event_desc.imjin_jp_princes: In the far north, at Hoeryong, local men led by Kuk Gyeong-in have seized two Joseon princes and their households and handed them over to Katō Kiyomasa.
event_desc.imjin_jp_pyongyang: Pyongyang is ours. Beyond it the road runs on to the Yalu and Ming. The men are tired, the grain comes slowly, and the ships that were to bring more men up the west coast have not been seen.
event_desc.imjin_jp_race: Konishi and Katō hate each other, and each has sworn to reach the Joseon capital first. Their corps march by different roads and send no word to each other.
event_desc.imjin_jp_regents_press: The regents say the war in Korea eats the realm's rice and men, and that no one can hold the daimyo together while their armies are abroad.
event_desc.imjin_jp_righteous: Behind our corps, farmers, scholars and monks have taken up arms. They ambush the rice carts in the hills, kill our messengers and vanish into the villages.
event_desc.imjin_jp_sea_admiral: Captains bring word of a Joseon admiral at Yeosu who drills his crews hard and has heavy ships that carry cannon. Our fleet's commanders cannot agree what to do about him.
event_desc.imjin_jp_shimazu_late: Every lord in Kyushu has sent his quota to Nagoya except the Shimazu of Satsuma. Their men trickle in a few boats at a time, and Shimazu Yoshihiro writes that ships are hard to find.
event_desc.imjin_jp_so_plea: Sō Yoshitoshi of Tsushima has come to Kyoto. His island lives on the Busan trade, and he begs leave to carry the Taikō's demand his own way: to ask Joseon for an embassy first, and speak of the road to Ming later.
event_desc.imjin_jp_strike_again: The truce is over. The daimyo have mustered again, and the forts on Joseon's southern coast still hold Japanese garrisons.
event_desc.imjin_jp_strike_full: Every corps has come in. Ships, rice and powder stand ready at Nagoya and on Tsushima, and the daimyo wait for the word.
event_desc.imjin_jp_strike_ready: Boats crowd the harbours of Kyushu and the first corps are camped about Nagoya. The muster is not complete, but the daimyo say the army can cross now.
event_desc.imjin_jp_taiko_ailing: Hideyoshi keeps to his rooms at Fushimi for days at a time. His physicians speak quietly, and his heir is still a child.
event_desc.imjin_jp_taiko_dies: Toyotomi Hideyoshi is dead. Five great lords will rule for his heir, and the armies in Korea do not yet know.
event_desc.imjin_jp_talks: Shen Weijing, a Ming go-between, has come to Konishi Yukinaga's camp. He says the war can end by talks, if each side sends its terms.
event_desc.imjin_jp_tsurumatsu: The Taikō's little son Tsurumatsu has died of a fever before his third year. Hideyoshi has cut off his topknot in mourning, and no one at court dares speak to him of anything else.
event_desc.imjin_jp_umekita: Umekita Kunikane, a Shimazu retainer on his way to Nagoya, has turned back and seized Sashiki castle in Higo, Katō Kiyomasa's land, while Katō is away at the war. Men who do not want to cross the sea are joining him.
event_desc.imjin_monks_call: Enemy soldiers have burned a mountain temple. The great monks send word: if the king calls, the monks will take up arms.
event_desc.irn_armistice: British troops advance from Iraq and the Gulf, Soviet columns from the Caucasus, and our army cannot hold either front. The two powers demand a supply route to the Soviet Union and the expulsion of German nationals. The Shah's government can stop the fighting today.
event_desc.irn_new_shah: Reza Shah has abdicated as Soviet troops approach Tehran and will leave the country. His son Mohammad Reza takes the oath before the Majlis and promises to rule as a constitutional monarch.
event_desc.irq_armistice: British columns are closing on Baghdad and German air support has come too late. The leaders of the coup are fleeing to Iran. Officers loyal to the regent are ready to sign an armistice and bring back the old government.
event_desc.irq_golden_square: Four army colonels known as the Golden Square have surrounded the palace in Baghdad. The regent has fled, and the officers want a National Defence Government that would end British influence and look to the Axis for help.
event_desc.isl_british_occupation: British warships have landed troops at Reykjavík without asking. London says it must keep Iceland out of German hands now that Denmark is occupied, and promises to leave when the war ends. We have no army to resist them.
event_desc.isl_us_garrison: Washington offers to take over the defence of Iceland from the British, and our government has invited it. American marines will garrison the island while the British troops leave for other fronts.
event_desc.ita_addis_ababa: Italian columns have entered Addis Ababa and the Emperor has left for exile. Rome is ready to proclaim the King of Italy Emperor of Ethiopia and join the country to its East African possessions, whatever the League decides.
event_desc.ita_albania: Italian troops have landed at Durrës and other Albanian ports. King Zog has fled across the border, and Rome prepares to offer the Albanian crown to the King of Italy. The small kingdom's army cannot hold out for long.
event_desc.ita_alpine_armistice: France has laid down its arms, and its delegates have signed a separate armistice with Italy at Villa Incisa near Rome. Italy keeps the ground its troops hold beyond the Alps, and a demilitarised strip is drawn along the frontier.
event_desc.ita_anti_comintern: Berlin and Tokyo invite Rome to join their pact against the Communist International. Membership costs little on paper, but it would bind Italy publicly to Germany and Japan. London and Paris are watching Rome's choice.
event_desc.ita_armistice: The new government has secretly signed an armistice with the Allies at Cassibile in Sicily. Announcing it takes Italy out of the war and out of the Axis at once, while German divisions are already in the north.
event_desc.ita_cobelligerence: From Brindisi, where the King and the government have taken refuge, Italy declares war on Germany. The Allies accept it as a co-belligerent, not as an ally, and Italian units now fight beside the Allied armies moving up the peninsula.
event_desc.ita_grand_council: With the war going badly, the Fascist Grand Council has met for the first time since 1939. After ten hours of debate it passed Dino Grandi's motion asking the King to take back supreme command. The next day the King dismissed Mussolini, had him arrested and gave the government to a marshal.
event_desc.ita_leaves_league: The Fascist Grand Council has decided that Italy will leave the League of Nations, which condemned the war in Ethiopia. The announcement from a balcony in Rome draws cheers at home and cold silence in London and Paris. Rome is no longer bound by anything Geneva decides.
event_desc.ita_mussolini_restrained: Monarchists, generals and a group of moderate Fascists have agreed to act together in the Grand Council. If the vote goes their way, the King will give the government to a marshal; if it fails, Mussolini will settle scores.
event_desc.ita_pact_of_steel: Berlin proposes a full military alliance: each will come to the other's aid in any war, defensive or not. The foreign ministry warns that Italy will not be ready for a great war before 1943.
event_desc.ita_rome_berlin_axis: Italy's foreign minister has signed a protocol in Berlin settling the two governments' differences over Austria, Spain and Ethiopia. Rome can speak of an axis around which Europe will turn, or keep Berlin at arm's length.
event_desc.ita_sanctions_lifted: With Ethiopia in Italian hands, the League of Nations has ended its economic sanctions. They never covered oil and many members ignored them; their end is a quiet admission that collective security has failed.
event_desc.jpn_anti_comintern: Berlin proposes a pact against the Communist International, with a secret annex promising that neither side will help the Soviet Union against the other. The army welcomes it; the navy and the court fear it ties Japan to Germany's quarrels.
event_desc.jpn_burma_state: Under Japanese military rule, Burma's independence preparatory committee has drafted a constitution. Ending military rule and proclaiming an independent State of Burma should win Burmese cooperation. The new state, however, must ally with Japan and declare war on Britain and America.
event_desc.jpn_february_incident: Young army officers have seized the centre of Tokyo and killed senior statesmen, demanding a 'Shōwa Restoration' under direct imperial rule. The throne wants the revolt crushed; the army command is split over how far to meet the rebels.
event_desc.jpn_hull_note: In Washington the Secretary of State has handed the Japanese envoys a note. It asks Japan to withdraw all its forces from China and Indochina and to join a multilateral non-aggression pact. The cabinet reads it as an ultimatum in all but name. The navy's preparations are already complete.
event_desc.jpn_imperial_rule_assistance: The prime minister has gathered the dissolved political parties into a single Imperial Rule Assistance Association. The Diet remains, but every organisation from labour to women's groups is to be folded into one national movement. The cabinet calls it the New Order.
event_desc.jpn_kwantung_break: The generals in Manchuria were promised autonomy and have seen little of it. They no longer answer Tokyo's telegrams. The regime can recall them if it is steady enough, or they take Manchukuo and the leased territory with them.
event_desc.jpn_manchukuo_defiance: The Kwantung generals have cut loose, and Manchukuo is theirs. They leave the camp they were bound to and take up arms against their old masters.
event_desc.jpn_marco_polo_bridge: A night clash between Japanese and Chinese troops near the Marco Polo Bridge outside Beiping has grown into open fighting. Neither government backs down, and the skirmish becomes a full war between Japan and China. Within weeks the front spreads across northern China.
event_desc.jpn_nanjing_government: Nationalist figures who broke with Chongqing propose a new National Government in Nanjing, merging the client regimes Japan set up in northern and central China. It can only rest on Japanese recognition and Japanese garrisons. Chongqing calls it a puppet and vows to fight on.
event_desc.jpn_philippine_republic: In Manila the Preparatory Commission for Philippine Independence has drafted a constitution. If Japan grants independence, military rule ends and a republic under a Filipino president takes its place. The Commonwealth government in exile in Washington does not recognise it.
event_desc.jpn_potsdam_declaration: From Potsdam, the United States, Britain and China have called on Japan to surrender unconditionally. The alternative, they warn, is prompt and utter destruction. The cabinet and the military chiefs are divided over how to answer.
event_desc.jpn_service_revolt: The navy and the Control Faction still hold the loyalty of ministries, ports and half the staff. Orders are ignored, ships stay in harbour, and the old establishment names its own government. The regime can break the movement by force if it is steady enough, or the country divides.
event_desc.jpn_south_indochina: Japan has sent a second demand. This time it wants the airfields and ports of southern Indochina, Saigon among them, and the right to station troops there. With the homeland occupied, there is no strength to resist. Washington is watching and weighing its answer.
event_desc.jpn_soviet_neutrality: Moscow offers a pact of neutrality: each side will stay out of any war the other fights. It would secure the northern frontier while the army is tied down in China and the navy looks south. The pact would run for five years.
event_desc.jpn_surrender_decision: The Soviet Union has declared war and driven into Manchuria, and the cities of the home islands are being destroyed from the air. The Supreme War Council is split three against three over accepting the Potsdam terms. An imperial conference must make the final decision.
event_desc.jpn_surrender_effect: Through neutral governments, Japan has told the Allies it accepts the Potsdam Declaration, and the surrender has been announced to the nation by radio. The armed forces have been ordered to cease fire. The war in Asia and the Pacific is drawing to an end.
event_desc.lat_rio_conference: With the United States at war, the foreign ministers of the American republics meet in Rio de Janeiro. Washington asks every delegation to break relations with Germany, Italy and Japan. The final resolution only recommends it, and each government must now decide for itself whether to follow.
event_desc.ltu_memel_ultimatum: Berlin demands the Memel Territory, detached from Germany after the war and held by Lithuania since 1923, and hints that any delay will be settled by force. Britain and France have just stood aside over Prague.
event_desc.mck_ev_advisers_depart: Japan no longer holds Manchukuo as its subject. The vice-ministers and staff officers who ran the ministries are packing, and Hsinking must decide how to see them off.
event_desc.mck_ev_border_clash: A patrol has crossed a river island that both sides claim, and both sides are now bringing up guns. Neither Hsinking nor Moscow knows exactly where the line runs.
event_desc.mck_ev_china_at_war: Japan and China are at war. In Harbin and Mukden people read the official bulletins in public and listen to Chinese radio at home.
event_desc.mck_ev_concordia_congress: Delegates from every county come to Hsinking to report on harvests, bandits and taxes. Some of them have prepared speeches the organisers did not write.
event_desc.mck_ev_court_intrigue: Kinsmen of the Aisin-Gioro meet the Emperor late at night. They speak of loyal regiments, of old banner families and of a day when the throne gives the orders.
event_desc.mck_ev_guerrilla_raid: Partisans have burned a police post and a timber camp and vanished into the forest. The county asks for troops; the troops ask for guides.
event_desc.mck_ev_imperial_rescript: The Emperor is to install the Japanese sun goddess as the guardian spirit of his state. The Manchu court is appalled; the Kwantung Army is waiting for his answer.
event_desc.mck_ev_jpn_loyalty_question: Hsinking asks to speak for itself in its own affairs. The Kwantung Army calls it ingratitude; the Foreign Ministry calls it a chance to look less like an occupier.
event_desc.mck_ev_kwantung_reacts: Staff officers arrive at the ministries unannounced. They want the old arrangements back, and they have brought a company of infantry to make the point.
event_desc.mck_ev_kwantung_thins: Division after division of the Kwantung Army entrains for the south and the Pacific. The great army that held Manchuria is becoming a shell.
event_desc.mck_ev_mangyo_founded: Ayukawa Yoshisuke's holding company arrives with Nissan's shares and promises of American machinery. The Railway Company, which ran industry until now, is not pleased.
event_desc.mck_ev_partisan_commander_falls: After weeks of pursuit a United Army commander has been killed alone in the snow. The soldiers who cut him open found only bark, grass roots and cotton in his stomach.
event_desc.mck_ev_qing_proclaimed: Officials in court robes read the proclamation before the palace. Outside the city, people wonder which calendar to use on their receipts.
event_desc.mck_ev_recognition: A few governments are ready to recognise Manchukuo, El Salvador and the Vatican's envoys among the first, Italy and Germany close behind. Each one makes the state look a little more real.
event_desc.mck_ev_settler_plan: The first trains of the settler programme arrive with farmers from northern Japan. The land company has already marked the villages they will replace.
event_desc.mck_ev_soviet_storm: Soviet armies are pouring across the frontier from three sides. The garrisons that were told the Kwantung Army stood behind them find that it does not.
event_desc.mck_ev_tokyo_answers_qing: The restored Qing court in Hsinking claims the Forbidden City as its capital. It is a claim on the heart of China, made by a state Japan created.
event_desc.mck_ev_vice_ministers: Each ministry has a Chinese minister and a Japanese vice-minister. The ministers sign what the vice-ministers bring them. One of the ministers has begun to read the papers first.
event_desc.mck_ev_young_marshal_message: Copies of a letter from Zhang Xueliang pass from hand to hand among former Fengtian officers. He asks them to remember whose army they once served.
event_desc.mex_ev_calles_exiled: Soldiers woke Calles at his ranch and put him on a plane to San Diego with a few of his men. Some generals still look north for orders.
event_desc.mex_ev_cedillo_revolt: The old caudillo of San Luis Potosí has called his agrarian colonists to arms against the government. A few planes and a few thousand men follow him into the sierra.
event_desc.mex_ev_companies_refuse: The oil companies say they cannot pay the award and will not obey the court. Their lawyers hint that Washington and London will back them.
event_desc.mex_ev_coyoacan: Months after a failed machine-gun raid on his house, the exile has been killed with an ice axe by a man who had won his trust.
event_desc.mex_ev_cristero_embers: In the villages of the west, armed men attack the new rural teachers; some have lost their ears, some their lives. The bishops blame the socialist school.
event_desc.mex_ev_disputed_election: Gunfire at the polling places, ballot boxes carried off, and two candidates each claiming victory. The official count gives the party's man a vast majority.
event_desc.mex_ev_gold_shirts: Mounted Gold Shirts charged the workers' parade in the main square; the taxi drivers' union drove their cars into the horses. There are dead on both sides.
event_desc.mex_ev_isthmus_offer: Mexico City proposes that our republic join the Mexican union as a free state, with its own governor and its own deputies.
event_desc.mex_ev_north_claim: The Mexican government now openly claims the lands it lost in 1848, from Texas to California, and has moved troops to the border.
event_desc.mex_ev_oil_gbr: Mexico has expropriated the oil companies, El Águila among them, a Shell subsidiary built with British capital. The Foreign Office demands its return.
event_desc.mex_ev_oil_settlement: Mexico proposes that a mixed commission value the expropriated properties and that it pay in instalments. The companies call the figure an insult.
event_desc.mex_ev_oil_usa: Standard Oil wants the State Department to punish Mexico. The ambassador in Mexico City argues that a quarrel now would push Mexico toward Germany.
event_desc.mex_ev_pacific_alarm: Fishermen report submarines off Baja California and the coast has no defences to speak of. The Americans offer to help guard it.
event_desc.mex_ev_potrero_del_llano: A Mexican tanker sailing lit and flying the national flag has been torpedoed off Florida by a German submarine. A second follows within days.
event_desc.mex_ev_sinaia: The first ships from France bring thousands of Spanish Republicans: doctors, engineers, poets, printers, teachers and soldiers.
event_desc.mex_ev_tankers_idle: The companies have closed every market they control. Crude piles up in the tanks, spare parts are refused, and the foreign tankers do not come.
event_desc.mex_ev_trotsky_asylum: The painter asks the president to give asylum to Leon Trotsky, expelled from Norway and hunted by Stalin. Moscow and the Mexican Communists will be furious.
event_desc.mex_ev_washington_frowns: American papers report Mexican oil sailing for Hamburg, Genoa and Yokohama. The State Department asks for an explanation.
event_desc.mex_oil_crisis: The foreign oil companies refuse to accept the labour award upheld by the Supreme Court. Output is stalling and the oil workers' union warns of a general strike. Tonight the President will speak to the nation by radio, and the cabinet must decide what he will announce.
event_desc.new_state_proclaimed: A new government has taken charge of these lands and proclaimed its own state. Ministries must be staffed, an army raised and foreign governments approached. Whatever its origins, the administration must first make the state work.
event_desc.nld_bankers_letter: The Netherlands Bank and the great houses of Amsterdam write that leaving gold would ruin the guilder's name. The economists in the ministries quietly say the opposite.
event_desc.nld_belgian_proposal: Belgium, as uneasy as we are, proposes secret talks between the two general staffs. Berlin would call it a breach of neutrality if it learned of them.
event_desc.nld_cabinet_falls: The coalition has broken over the budget. The queen may ask the Social Democrats into government for the first time, or call on a cabinet of officials above the parties.
event_desc.nld_february_strike: In occupied Amsterdam the dockers, the tram men and the city workers stop work in protest at the round-ups of their Jewish neighbours.
event_desc.nld_indies_invaded: Japanese forces land on Borneo and Celebes and head for the oil and for Java.
event_desc.nld_invasion: German columns cross the IJssel and the Maas, and paratroopers land around The Hague and Rotterdam. The army falls back on the water lines.
event_desc.nld_japanese_demands: A Japanese delegation in Batavia asks for far more oil than the Indies have ever sold it, with a warning not quite spoken.
event_desc.nld_lunteren_day: Tens of thousands in black and red fill the movement's field in the Veluwe. The police watch from the road and the press asks whether uniforms should be banned again.
event_desc.nld_mobilisation_question: Germany is at war. Full mobilisation would put every man under arms and empty the factories; a partial one would cost less and protect less.
event_desc.nld_nsb_at_the_polls: The NSB campaigns hard for the coming elections. The bishops forbid Catholics to join it and the Protestant churches speak against it.
event_desc.nld_oslo_convention: The Scandinavians, the Belgians and the Dutch meet once more to keep trade open between the small states while the great powers raise their walls.
event_desc.nld_polder_falls_dry: Where fishermen sailed a few years ago, the new land lies dry. Who should settle it, and what should be built there?
event_desc.nld_queens_jubilee: The queen has reigned for forty years. Orange flags hang from every window and the parties set their quarrels aside for a week.
event_desc.nld_rotterdam_threat: The enemy demands the surrender of Rotterdam and threatens to destroy the city from the air. Other cities would follow.
event_desc.nld_soetardjo_petition: A member of the Volksraad asks for a conference on self-government for the Indies within the kingdom. The colonial ministry advises a polite refusal.
event_desc.nld_unemployed_march: Thousands of unemployed men walk to The Hague behind red banners to protest another cut in their benefit.
event_desc.nld_union_offer: The Netherlands proposes that our country join it in one state of the Low Countries.
event_desc.nld_union_refused: Our neighbour has refused to join the union.
event_desc.nld_venlo_incident: German agents posing as plotters lured two British officers to the border at Venlo and seized them. A Dutch officer was killed. Berlin now says the Netherlands is not neutral at all.
event_desc.nor_bank_gold: Tons of gold sit in the vaults in Oslo. Trucks, trains and fishing boats could carry it beyond the enemy's reach.
event_desc.nor_defence_vote: The defence committee proposes extra money for rifles, guns and stores. Labour's left calls it militarism, the Conservatives call it too little.
event_desc.nor_farmers_price: The Farmers' Party reminds the government that its votes were bought with support prices, and the price has gone up.
event_desc.nor_finland_appeal: The Finns ask for arms and volunteers. Britain and France want to send troops to Finland across Norway's ore railway.
event_desc.nor_fjord_at_dawn: Darkened warships are steaming up the fjord towards the capital. The fortress commander has no orders and little time.
event_desc.nor_guarantee_request: Oslo asks us to declare openly that we will defend Norway if it is attacked.
event_desc.nor_heavy_water_order: A German chemical firm wants far more heavy water than any laboratory needs and asks Vemork to raise output.
event_desc.nor_heavy_water_raid: A raid has wrecked the heavy-water plant at Vemork in Telemark. The electrolysis cells and the stored heavy water are gone, and production will be stopped for a long time. Only a few scientists know what the heavy water was meant for.
event_desc.nor_mined_waters: British ships have laid mines off the coast to stop the ore traffic to Germany. Berlin says Norway cannot keep its own neutrality.
event_desc.nor_mot_dag_dissolves: The radical circle has dissolved itself, and many of its members ask to join Labour. Some in the party fear a cuckoo in the nest.
event_desc.nor_ns_at_the_polls: Quisling's party has campaigned hard with rallies and uniforms. The votes are being counted.
event_desc.nor_prison_ship: A German supply ship carrying British prisoners shelters in Norwegian waters. A British destroyer follows it in and boards it.
event_desc.nor_ships_at_sea: The homeland is lost, but most of the merchant fleet is at sea. The enemy orders the ships to neutral or German ports.
event_desc.nor_svalbard_miners: Soviet coal companies work their own mines on Svalbard under the archipelago's treaty and send more men every year.
event_desc.nor_teachers_refuse: The occupation regime orders every teacher into its new union. Thousands write the same letter of refusal.
event_desc.nor_the_demands: The enemy envoy demands that the King appoint a government of the invader's choosing and order the army to stop fighting.
event_desc.nor_trotsky_asylum: An exiled Soviet revolutionary lives in a house outside Oslo. Moscow threatens to stop buying Norwegian fish unless he is silenced.
event_desc.nor_union_offer: Oslo proposes that our two countries join as one realm again, as in the old union days.
event_desc.nor_union_refused: Our neighbour has turned down the proposal for a union.
event_desc.phl_osmena_succeeds: President Quezon has died at Saranac Lake, New York, after a long illness. Vice President Sergio Osmeña takes the oath of office in Washington and pledges to bring the Commonwealth government home to Manila.
event_desc.pol_beck_speech: Replying to the German leader's speech of 28 April, the foreign minister tells the Sejm that Poland will give up neither Danzig nor a road across Pomerania. Talks remain possible, he says, but only between equals and by peaceful means. The deputies applaud him at length.
event_desc.pol_danzig_bargain: Berlin offers Warsaw a partnership: if Danzig returns to Germany and a German road crosses the corridor, Germany will guarantee Poland's frontiers and share its gains in the east. The offer comes with a smile and an army behind it.
event_desc.pol_danzig_demand: Germany demands the Free City of Danzig and an extraterritorial road and railway across the Polish corridor to East Prussia. Warsaw sees the corridor as its outlet to the sea, and the army has begun calling up reservists.
event_desc.pol_ev_bomb_built: The bureau's new machines can find the daily settings of the German cipher in a couple of hours. The mathematicians ask what to do next.
event_desc.pol_ev_castle_and_marshal: The President's friends and the Marshal's officers no longer dine together. Ministers ask which of the two men they answer to, and the newspapers have started to count the camp's factions.
event_desc.pol_ev_colonels_alone: The ruling camp now holds every office that matters. The opposition boycotts the elections, and the Sejm passes whatever the government sends it.
event_desc.pol_ev_danzig_customs: The Free City's Senate wants to stop Polish customs officers from working at its borders. Berlin says the Senate is right.
event_desc.pol_ev_eastern_amnesty: Now at war with Germany, the Soviet Union offers to free the Polish prisoners in its camps so they can form an army.
event_desc.pol_ev_falanga_brawls: Squads of national radicals have broken up a socialist meeting and attacked shops in the city centre. The universities are in uproar.
event_desc.pol_ev_first_steel: Where there was forest two years ago, the first steel has been poured. The workers came from the poorest villages of the region.
event_desc.pol_ev_gold_route: The gold reserve has crossed into Romania and waits at a Black Sea port. A ship must take it to a friendly country.
event_desc.pol_ev_hungarian_border: Hungarian troops now stand on the Carpathian passes. For the first time since the war Poland borders an old friend.
event_desc.pol_ev_kaunas_accepts: Lithuania has agreed to exchange envoys. Trains run across the line for the first time in twenty years.
event_desc.pol_ev_kaunas_note: Poland demands that Lithuania open diplomatic relations within two days, and its troops stand on the demarcation line. Lithuania has never accepted the loss of Vilnius.
event_desc.pol_ev_kaunas_refuses: Lithuania has rejected the note. The generals say the matter can be settled in a week.
event_desc.pol_ev_kpp_dissolved: Word comes from Moscow that the Comintern has dissolved the Communist Party of Poland as riddled with spies. Its leaders who went east have not come back.
event_desc.pol_ev_mobilisation_advice: German divisions gather on three sides. London and Paris urge Warsaw not to mobilise, so as not to give Berlin an excuse.
event_desc.pol_ev_morges_meeting: At the pianist's villa on Lake Geneva the opposition's leaders have agreed on a common programme. They must now decide who will speak for it at home.
event_desc.pol_ev_opposition_at_door: Mass meetings in every city call for free elections and an end to the colonels' rule. Even some officers have signed the petitions.
event_desc.pol_ev_peasant_strike: The People's Party has called a strike of the countryside. No milk, grain or meat reaches the towns, and the roads to the markets are watched by young men with sticks. The police ask for orders.
event_desc.pol_ev_union_offer: Warsaw proposes a union of the two nations under one state, with Lithuanian schools, a Lithuanian assembly and a shared army. Many in Kaunas remember the old union as a Polish one.
event_desc.pol_ev_union_refused: Kaunas has turned down the union. Some officers want to take by force what was offered by treaty.
event_desc.pol_ev_volhynia_unrest: Ukrainian nationalists have burned estates and attacked officials in the southeast. The army and the governor disagree on the answer.
event_desc.pol_exile_forces: France has asked for an armistice. The Polish government, and the soldiers and airmen who reach the ports of western and southern France, are carried to Britain. In London the army is rebuilt once more, this time beside the British.
event_desc.pol_pyry_meeting: In the Kabaty forest near Pyry, south of Warsaw, the Cipher Bureau receives British and French codebreakers. For years Polish mathematicians have been reading messages sent with the German cipher machine. Now they can hand their methods and replica machines to the allies who have promised to defend Poland.
event_desc.pol_warsaw_uprising: Soviet tanks are reported on the eastern approaches to Warsaw. The commander of the Home Army in the city asks our authorisation to rise against the German garrison and free the capital before the Red Army arrives.
event_desc.potsdam_conference: At Cecilienhof, outside ruined Berlin, the victorious powers fix Germany's eastern border on the Oder and the Neisse and divide East Prussia. Before they part, they will call on Japan to surrender.
event_desc.prt_alliance_invoked: The British ambassador cites the treaty of 1373 and asks for facilities in the Azores to hunt the submarines in mid-Atlantic. Arms are offered in return.
event_desc.prt_american_bases: With the British already on Terceira, Washington wants an airfield of its own on Santa Maria.
event_desc.prt_avante_press: The clandestine paper now reaches every factory floor in Lisbon and the Barreiro.
event_desc.prt_bordeaux_visas: As France collapses, our consul at Bordeaux signs visas for thousands of refugees against his explicit orders.
event_desc.prt_border_refugees: Spanish Republicans fleeing the Nationalist columns are crossing into Portugal. Burgos wants them back.
event_desc.prt_exiles_return: Republican exiles from Paris and Madrid come home to organise the opposition openly.
