event_desc.prt_german_protest: The German minister protests the bases in the Azores and hints at what his submarines could do to Portuguese shipping.
event_desc.prt_iberian_meeting: Salazar and the Spanish leader meet in Seville to discuss how to keep the peninsula out of the war.
event_desc.prt_iberian_union_offer: Lisbon proposes that Spain and Portugal become one state under one government. Do we accept?
event_desc.prt_iberian_union_refused: Madrid has rejected our offer of union.
event_desc.prt_integralist_revival: The old monarchist writers publish a manifesto calling for a Catholic, corporative kingdom.
event_desc.prt_king_returns: Dom Duarte Nuno lands in Lisbon to a crowd of monarchists, priests and curious onlookers.
event_desc.prt_preto_rally: Thousands of blue shirts march down the Avenida da Liberdade behind Rolão Preto.
event_desc.prt_sailors_revolt: Sailors of two sloops and a destroyer have seized their ships to sail for the Spanish Republic. The forts at the river mouth await orders.
event_desc.prt_salazar_bomb: A bomb has exploded beside Salazar's car as he went to Mass. He is unhurt and asks only that the service go on.
event_desc.prt_spain_joins_axis: Spain has bound itself to Berlin. Our only land frontier now faces an Axis power.
event_desc.prt_tarrafal: The police propose a penal camp on a dry plain of the Cape Verde islands, far from lawyers and newspapers.
event_desc.prt_timor_landing: Allied troops have landed on Portuguese Timor to deny it to Japan, without our consent.
event_desc.prt_wolfram_price: The price of wolfram has multiplied. Peasants dig by night, smugglers run ore to Spain, and both sides bid without limit.
event_desc.prt_wolfram_ultimatum: London and Washington demand that not one more ton of wolfram reach Germany, and hint at oil and food shipments.
event_desc.prt_world_exhibition: Pavilions of the discoveries and the empire rise at Belém while the rest of Europe goes to war. How grand should it be?
event_desc.quebec_agreement: Meeting in Quebec, the British and American leaders agree to pool their atomic research. British scientists join the American project; neither country will use the weapon against the other, nor against a third country without the other's consent.
event_desc.rou_antonescu: Blamed for the summer's losses of territory, King Carol II has abdicated in favour of his son Michael. The general he named prime minister now rules with full powers as Conducător of the state, backed by the Iron Guard. Parliament stays dissolved.
event_desc.rou_august_coup: Soviet armies have broken through in Moldavia. The young King and the opposition parties are ready to arrest the head of government at the palace, announce an armistice with the Allies on the radio and turn the army against Germany.
event_desc.rou_bessarabia_ultimatum: Moscow demands Bessarabia and northern Bukovina, with twenty-four hours to answer and four days to evacuate. Berlin advises Bucharest to give way, and no ally is ready to help. If we refuse, Soviet troops will cross the Dniester.
event_desc.rou_dobruja: Sofia asks for the return of Southern Dobruja, taken from Bulgaria after the Balkan wars. Berlin backs the claim, and after this summer's losses Bucharest has neither the will nor the friends to refuse. The agreement is to be signed at Craiova.
event_desc.rou_ev_bessarabia_grief: The provinces were given up without a shot. Crowds and officers ask who is to blame.
event_desc.rou_ev_cairo: In a neutral capital the envoys hear the other side's terms: an armistice, the army turned, and the border settled later.
event_desc.rou_ev_codreanu_rise: The Legion's marches fill the market towns, and students sing its songs in the lecture halls. Ministers ask whether the police should stop the next procession.
event_desc.rou_ev_codreanu_trial: The Legion's leader stands before a military court. The verdict will tell the country who rules it.
event_desc.rou_ev_court_scandal: Newspapers abroad print what Bucharest only whispers: the king's companion and his favourites decide who gets contracts and offices.
event_desc.rou_ev_earthquake: A deep earthquake has shaken Moldavia and Bucharest. A tower block has fallen in the capital and the walls of Doftana prison have collapsed on its inmates.
event_desc.rou_ev_entente_summit: The Little Entente's chiefs of staff meet to turn old promises into plans.
event_desc.rou_ev_german_mission: A German mission is ready to train our divisions. Officers welcome the methods; some ministers dislike foreign uniforms in Bucharest.
event_desc.rou_ev_hung_election: For the first time the government list has failed to reach the share that wins the majority bonus. The king must choose who governs.
event_desc.rou_ev_legion_rising: Legionaries hold ministries, newspapers and police stations across the country. The army waits for an order.
event_desc.rou_ev_minister_killed: Legionary gunmen have killed the head of government in the street and seized a radio station to announce it. The country waits for the answer.
event_desc.rou_ev_oil_saboteurs: Police have found explosives and foreign engineers with plans to block the Danube and wreck the wells.
event_desc.rou_ev_peasant_debts: The farm debts of the slump years crush the villages. The banks want them paid; the peasants want them cut.
event_desc.rou_ev_ploiesti_target: Both camps buy our oil, and both staffs have drawn circles around the refineries. Diplomats hint that exclusive contracts would be safer.
event_desc.rou_ev_polish_passage: Poland's government, its soldiers and its gold reserve are crossing into Romania. Berlin demands internment; Paris asks for free passage to the sea.
event_desc.rou_ev_railway_strike: The railway workshops stop over wages again. The police chief asks for orders.
event_desc.rou_ev_transylvania_refugees: Families from Cluj and Oradea arrive with what they can carry. The university of Cluj has moved south with them.
event_desc.rou_vienna_award_notice: Summoned to Vienna, our foreign minister has been handed a map: northern Transylvania, with Cluj and Oradea, goes to Hungary. Germany and Italy will guarantee what is left of Romania if we accept. At home, the news is met with fury.
event_desc.spa_aid_request: Envoys from Spain ask us for rifles, aircraft and men for their side in the civil war. Arms can travel through intermediaries; volunteers would make our part plain to everyone. Refusing costs nothing today, but Spain will remember it.
event_desc.spa_ebro_battle: On the night of 24 July boats and pontoon bridges carry the Republican army across the Ebro. The offensive is meant to ease the pressure on Valencia and to join the two halves of the Republic again. It becomes the longest and costliest battle of the war.
event_desc.spa_hendaye: At the railway station of Hendaye, just across the border in France, the Spanish head of state meets the German leader. As the price of entering the war Spain asks for Gibraltar, French Morocco and large deliveries of grain, fuel and arms. After hours of talks only a secret protocol without a date is signed.
event_desc.spa_madrid_holds: After two weeks of fighting in the University City and the Casa de Campo, the attack on the capital has stalled. The Nationalist command calls off the frontal assault and turns to a long siege. The front around Madrid will barely move for more than two years.
event_desc.sun_annex_east_poland: Assemblies convened in the occupied Polish east have asked to join the Ukrainian and Belorussian Soviet republics. The Supreme Soviet can accept the request and make the border final.
event_desc.sun_arsenal_fire: A fire destroys a great arsenal. The inquiry blames wreckers, but the losses are real either way.
event_desc.sun_barbarossa: At dawn, German armies cross the border along its whole length, from the Baltic to the Black Sea. Airfields are bombed before the planes can take off, and whole armies are cut off within days. Molotov speaks to the country by radio: "Our cause is just."
event_desc.sun_blyukher_arrest: Marshal Vasily Blyukher, a hero of the Civil War who had led the army in the Far East since 1929, is relieved after the fighting at Lake Khasan and arrested on 22 October. He dies in custody the following month.
event_desc.sun_bukharin_arrest: At the February–March plenum of the Central Committee, Nikolai Bukharin and Alexei Rykov are expelled from the party and arrested on 27 February. Bukharin edited Izvestia from 1934; Rykov had headed the government until 1930.
event_desc.sun_camp_uprising: Prisoners in a remote camp overpower the guards and march on the nearest town. The garrison asks for orders.
event_desc.sun_denunciation_cascade: One arrest brings ten denunciations, and each of those brings ten more. Managers spend their days defending themselves instead of working.
event_desc.sun_depot_explosion: A supply depot blows up in the night. Rifles and guns meant for the front are lost, and the guards are arrested.
event_desc.sun_factory_sabotage: A shift foreman is accused of wrecking machinery. Whether it was sabotage or exhaustion, the line stands idle while the investigators work.
event_desc.sun_false_reports: Plant directors report plans fulfilled for fear of being accused of failure. The staffs find out when the shells are not there.
event_desc.sun_first_moscow_trial: In Moscow, Grigory Zinoviev, Lev Kamenev and fourteen other defendants stand trial for an alleged plot against the party leadership. The case rests on their own confessions, printed in full in every newspaper. The court convicts all sixteen, and a wave of arrests follows.
event_desc.sun_foundry_halt: The chief engineer of a great foundry is taken away, and nobody dares to restart the furnaces without him.
event_desc.sun_hardliner_unrest: Party hardliners and the security organs refuse to accept the generals. Barracks and committees alike grumble, and loyal units are watched. A steady regime can break the movement by force; a shaky one risks a civil war.
event_desc.sun_hunger_riots: Shops are empty in the industrial towns, and workers gather at the gates of the grain stores.
event_desc.sun_japan_pact_lapses: Months after the notice, Moscow no longer treats the neutrality pact with Japan as binding. Since the spring, troops and equipment have rolled east along the Trans-Siberian without pause. The armies gathered in the Far East wait for their orders.
event_desc.sun_khalkhin_gol: Mongolian and Japanese-Manchukuo forces clash over the border along the Khalkhin Gol river. Under the 1936 protocol, Soviet troops move in to support Mongolia, and by late summer the skirmishes have grown into a full-scale battle.
event_desc.sun_lake_khasan: Japanese troops seize the hills west of Lake Khasan, on the border between the Soviet Union and Manchukuo. The Red Army retakes them after two weeks of hard fighting, and the ceasefire of 11 August leaves the border where Moscow drew it.
event_desc.sun_litvinov_dismissed: Maxim Litvinov, the face of collective security for nearly nine years, is removed as People's Commissar for Foreign Affairs. Premier Vyacheslav Molotov takes the post himself. In Berlin the change is read as a signal.
event_desc.sun_military_trial: A special session of the Supreme Court tries Marshal Mikhail Tukhachevsky, army commanders Iona Yakir and Ieronim Uborevich and five other senior officers for treason behind closed doors. The hearing lasts a single day, and all eight are convicted. Arrests spread through the officer corps.
event_desc.sun_mine_flooding: The pumps of a major mine were left unrepaired when their engineers were arrested. The galleries fill with water.
event_desc.sun_mr_pact_offer: The German Foreign Minister has arrived in Moscow with an offer: a ten-year non-aggression pact and a secret protocol dividing Eastern Europe into spheres of interest. Britain and France have offered nothing comparable. Signing would keep the Soviet Union out of the coming war, at least for now.
event_desc.sun_nationalities_petition: The leaders of the union republics ask the new government to keep their languages, schools and borders as they are. The generals prefer one army and one chain of command.
event_desc.sun_officers_flee: A group of officers and intelligence men slip across the border, afraid of the next list of names.
event_desc.sun_party_delegation: A delegation of veteran party members asks for seats in the councils of the state. They promise loyalty if they are heard, and make no promises if they are not.
event_desc.sun_peasant_petition: Village delegates arrive with petitions: the grain quotas are beyond what the fields can bear. The generals can ease them, or hold the line and keep the granaries full.
event_desc.sun_poland: Soviet troops cross the Polish border from the east, declaring that the Polish state has ceased to exist. Moscow presents the move as protecting the Ukrainians and Belarusians who live beyond the border. The two invading armies meet along the line drawn in the secret protocol.
event_desc.sun_rail_accident: A military train derails on a main line. Investigators look for wreckers, while the line stays blocked for days.
event_desc.sun_renounce_japan_pact: Foreign Commissar Molotov receives the Japanese ambassador and reads a statement: Japan, Germany's ally, is helping Germany in its war against the USSR, so the neutrality pact cannot be extended. Tokyo is left to guess at Moscow's intentions.
event_desc.sun_rokossovsky_arrest: Konstantin Rokossovsky, a cavalry commander with a distinguished record since the Civil War, is arrested on charges of spying for Poland and Japan. He will spend the next two and a half years in prison under investigation.
event_desc.sun_rokossovsky_release: After two and a half years under investigation, Konstantin Rokossovsky is released on 22 March 1940 and restored to his rank. He returns to command.
event_desc.sun_security_infighting: Two directorates of the security organs accuse each other of shielding enemies. Months of effort in the capital go to settling it.
event_desc.sun_shaposhnikov_returns: With the front giving way, Marshal Boris Shaposhnikov is recalled to head the General Staff in place of Georgy Zhukov. He had held the same post from 1937 to 1940. His calm and methodical staff work is needed more than ever.
event_desc.sun_shaposhnikov_steps_down: In failing health, Marshal Shaposhnikov leaves the post of Chief of the General Staff. His deputy, Aleksandr Vasilevsky, head of operations since August 1941, carries on the work and is confirmed in the post in June.
event_desc.sun_third_moscow_trial: Nikolai Bukharin, Alexei Rykov and nineteen other former leaders stand trial in Moscow for treason and sabotage. Foreign diplomats and journalists watch from the gallery as the defendants confess. On 13 March the court convicts all twenty-one.
event_desc.sun_tupolev_arrest: Aircraft designer Andrei Tupolev is arrested along with several of his engineers, among them Vladimir Petlyakov. From 1939 they design aircraft in a design bureau set up inside a prison.
event_desc.sun_tupolev_released: Andrei Tupolev and many of his engineers are released early to build aircraft for the war. The Tu-2 bomber they designed in prison is readied for production. Tupolev will not be fully rehabilitated until 1955.
event_desc.sun_vilnius_to_lithuania: Our troops hold Vilnius, which Lithuania has claimed as its capital since 1920. A mutual assistance treaty would hand the city to the government in Kaunas in return for Soviet garrisons on Lithuanian soil.
event_desc.sun_yegorov_replaced: Marshal Alexander Yegorov hands the General Staff over to Boris Shaposhnikov and becomes First Deputy People's Commissar of Defense. It is one move in a sweeping reshuffle of the high command that spring.
event_desc.svk_independence: With Bohemia and Moravia in our hands, Slovak politicians in Bratislava are ready to declare a state of their own under our protection. A separate Slovakia would guard our flank at little cost; ruling it directly would keep the land in our own hands.
event_desc.svk_national_uprising: Army units and partisans in the central Slovak mountains have risen against the government and its German protectors, with Banská Bystrica as their centre. German divisions are moving in to put the rising down and occupy the region.
event_desc.swe_adalen_march: On the anniversary of the shootings, the communists lead a march along the river to the graves. The Social Democrats want to lead it themselves.
event_desc.swe_allied_passage: Britain and France want to send an expedition to Finland through Narvik and the Swedish ore railway. Everyone in Stockholm knows the troops would stop at Kiruna's mines on the way.
event_desc.swe_anchorage_explosion: Three destroyers have blown up and burned at their anchorage near Stockholm, with dozens of sailors dead. Was it an accident with the torpedoes, or sabotage?
event_desc.swe_bofors_buyers: Delegations from a dozen armies wait in Karlskoga's hotel for 40 mm guns and anti-tank guns. The works cannot supply them all and the Swedish army at once.
event_desc.swe_british_purchase: At war with Germany, London proposes a war trade agreement: Swedish ships may sail west under British control, and Britain will buy what would otherwise go to Germany.
event_desc.swe_budapest_mission: The Americans ask whether Sweden would send a diplomat to Budapest to hand out protective passports to people facing deportation. A young businessman, Raoul Wallenberg, is willing to go.
event_desc.swe_crown_speech: Farmers and officers march to the palace once more, and the old king steps out to speak about the defence of the realm. The government asks him to keep to his role.
event_desc.swe_danish_rescue: The occupiers in Denmark are about to arrest the Danish Jews. Fishermen are ready to carry them across the Sound by night, if Sweden says publicly that it will take them all.
event_desc.swe_finland_appeal: The Red Army has crossed the Finnish border. Helsinki asks Stockholm for troops; the streets of Stockholm cry that Finland's cause is ours. The cabinet weighs volunteers and arms against war with the Soviet Union.
event_desc.swe_german_ore_demand: The German trade delegation asks for millions of tonnes more than last year's contract, and hints that coal deliveries depend on the answer.
event_desc.swe_holiday_cabinet: The defence vote has split the cabinet and the Prime Minister has resigned. The Farmers' League offers to mind the government over the summer until the election, after which a coalition could follow.
event_desc.swe_iron_pressure: With Norway occupied, Berlin demands that the ore from Kiruna and Gällivare keep flowing south. Narvik is wrecked, so the ore leaves through Luleå on the Baltic while the ice allows. The note also asks for rail transit to Norway. No one in Stockholm can say what a refusal would bring.
event_desc.swe_midsummer_crisis: Germany, now at war in the east, asks to move a full division with its guns from Norway to Finland on Swedish trains. The king is said to threaten abdication if the answer is no; the Social Democrats threaten to leave the cabinet if it is yes.
event_desc.swe_norwegian_refugees: Norway has fallen. Across the long mountain border come soldiers, resistance men and families on skis. Berlin asks that they be turned back.
event_desc.swe_ore_train_sabotage: Explosions on the line to Luleå and in German-bound ore ships: the police trace them to a communist sabotage network working for a foreign service.
event_desc.swe_saab_founding: The air force wants Swedish aircraft. Bofors and the bankers will put up the money for a new company in Trollhättan and Linköping, or the state can build its own works.
event_desc.swe_saltsjobaden_talks: After two years of talks the trade union confederation and the employers have a basic agreement on negotiations, strikes and lockouts. The government only has to stay out of the way, or it can write its own strike law.
event_desc.swe_torch_march: Lindholm's men want to march through the capital in uniform with torches. The uniform ban stands in their way, if the police enforce it.
event_desc.swe_union_offer: Stockholm proposes a union of the Nordic states: one foreign policy, one army and one crown over many parliaments. Joining means giving up independence; refusing means facing the giants alone.
event_desc.swe_union_refused: Our neighbour has turned down the union. Some in Stockholm shrug; others say that history was never made by asking politely.
event_desc.tehran_conference: For the first time the leaders of the Soviet Union, the United States and the United Kingdom sit at one table, at the Soviet embassy in Tehran. They agree that a second front will open in France in the spring of 1944.
event_desc.tha_border_war: With France defeated, crowds in Bangkok demand the return of the lands west of the Mekong that Siam ceded to French Indochina in 1904 and 1907. Border clashes have already begun, and the government must choose between war and patience.
event_desc.tha_tokyo_peace: Japan has offered to mediate the border war with Siam and expects an answer. Its terms would cede the lands west of the Mekong and around Battambang to Siam. Refusing would mean fighting on alone.
event_desc.treaty_escalation: A power outside the 1936 London naval treaty is building battleships beyond its limits. The treaty members agree to invoke the escalator clause: the displacement limit rises and heavier guns are allowed again.
event_desc.tur_aid_request: Under the treaty of mutual assistance Ankara asks for aircraft, rifles and credits to modernise its army. Turkey guards the Straits and the road to the Middle East. Yet every aircraft sent to Anatolia is one fewer for our own squadrons.
event_desc.tur_allied_arms_mission: Ankara asks for aircraft and rifles to defend the Straits and Thrace. Turkey has not joined the war, but it might.
event_desc.tur_assembly_elects: The Grand National Assembly meets to elect the second president of the Republic. The party has its candidate; the army has its own.
event_desc.tur_ataturk_dies: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, founder of the Republic, has died in Istanbul. The Grand National Assembly turns to İsmet İnönü, his long-serving prime minister and comrade from the War of Independence. The country goes into deep mourning.
event_desc.tur_balkan_ally_attacked: A partner of the Balkan Pact is at war and asks Ankara for help under the pact.
event_desc.tur_belligerents_ask_passage: The great powers are at war. Their ambassadors ask what Turkey will do with the Straits.
event_desc.tur_capital_levy_debate: The assessment commissions ask how hard to press. Merchants in Istanbul already speak of ruin.
event_desc.tur_chromium_offer: Turkey offers a year's output of its chromium mines, for gold, credit and goodwill.
event_desc.tur_dersim_rising: The tribes of Dersim have taken up arms against the new laws and the gendarmes. The army waits for orders.
event_desc.tur_erzincan_earthquake: A winter earthquake has levelled Erzincan and the towns around it. Tens of thousands are dead and the survivors are in the snow.
event_desc.tur_german_envoy: Germany's ambassador in Ankara offers a treaty of friendship and hints at more: arms, trade, perhaps land.
event_desc.tur_hatay_garrison: Turkey asks to station troops in the Sanjak of Alexandretta beside ours until the elections there are held.
event_desc.tur_hatay_state: The assembly of the sanjak of Alexandretta has met for the first time and proclaimed the State of Hatay. French and Turkish troops supervise the territory together. In Ankara the question is whether to press for union at once or to let the new state settle first.
event_desc.tur_kayseri_first_fighters: The first fighters built at Kayseri stand on the field. The air force asks what to do with the line.
event_desc.tur_montreux_signed: At Montreux the powers have agreed on a new regime for the Bosporus and the Dardanelles. Merchant ships keep free passage, but Turkey regains control of the Straits and may fortify them again. Warships of the Black Sea states and of outside navies face new limits.
event_desc.tur_mosul_note: Ankara says the Mosul verdict of the League is void and asks for the province back.
event_desc.tur_neutrality_pressure: In Cairo the British foreign secretary asks the Turkish foreign minister for air bases in Anatolia and for Turkey's entry into the war. Moscow is pressing London for the same. Ankara answers that its army lacks modern arms and that a German attack would follow at once.
event_desc.tur_opposition_petition: Four deputies ask for the constitution's freedoms in full and the right to found a party. The party group must answer.
event_desc.tur_poet_on_trial: A communist poet is accused of stirring up cadets with his verses. The court martial waits for a signal from Ankara.
event_desc.tur_soviet_demands: The Soviet Union denounces the old treaty of friendship and asks for bases on the Straits and a new frontier in the east.
event_desc.tur_turanist_trials: The racist and Turanist writers have attacked the government in print and in the street. The prosecutors are ready.
event_desc.tur_village_institutes_debate: Landowners call the Village Institutes nests of the left; teachers call them the best thing the Republic has done.
event_desc.usa_atlantic_charter: Meeting aboard warships off Newfoundland, the President and the British Prime Minister have set out common aims for the world after the war: no territorial gains, self-determination, open trade and freedom from fear and want.
event_desc.usa_democratic_uprising: Outside the capital the deposed party still holds the loyalty of millions. Governors refuse orders, guardsmen drift home and crowds fill the squares. The regime can break the movement by force if it is steady enough, or the country divides.
event_desc.usa_destroyers_for_bases: London asks for fifty old American destroyers to guard its convoys. In return Britain offers ninety-nine-year leases on bases from Newfoundland to British Guiana. The deal would bypass Congress and stretch neutrality to its limit.
event_desc.usa_election_1936: Americans choose between Franklin D. Roosevelt's New Deal and the Republican Alf Landon, who promises to balance the budget. Relief programmes, union rights and Social Security are on the ballot as much as the man in the White House.
event_desc.usa_election_1940: With war in Europe, Roosevelt breaks tradition and runs for a third term against Wendell Willkie. Both men promise to help Britain while keeping America out of the fighting; the voters must decide whom they trust in a crisis.
event_desc.usa_election_1944: For the first time since 1864 Americans vote in the middle of a great war. A visibly tired Roosevelt faces Thomas E. Dewey; his running mate this time is Senator Harry S. Truman of Missouri.
event_desc.usa_isolation_ends: Events abroad have overwhelmed the case for staying out. With the world at war, Congress and the public accept that the United States can no longer stand apart from it. The neutrality laws lose their force.
event_desc.usa_isolation_strained: As crisis follows crisis abroad, more Americans ask whether the oceans still keep the country safe. The neutrality laws stay on the books, but Congress has begun to argue over how far they should bind the President.
event_desc.usa_lend_lease_act: Congress has passed An Act to Promote the Defense of the United States. The President may now lend or lease war materials to any country whose defence he judges vital to America, and Britain's dollar shortage no longer limits its orders.
event_desc.usa_pearl_harbor: Japanese carrier aircraft have struck the Pacific Fleet at Pearl Harbor while Japanese forces attack across the Pacific. The President asks Congress to recognise that a state of war exists, and the isolationists fall silent.
event_desc.usa_quarantine_speech: In Chicago the President likens the spread of lawlessness in the world to an epidemic and calls on peace-loving nations to quarantine the aggressors. The press is divided, and isolationists in Congress are furious. No measures have yet been named.
event_desc.usa_recession_1937: Share prices have plunged and factory output is falling fast after Washington cut spending to balance the budget. Advisers urge the President to open the public purse again; the Treasury warns that the deficits will never end.
event_desc.usa_roosevelt_dies: Franklin D. Roosevelt has died at Warm Springs, Georgia, before the war's end. Vice President Harry S. Truman, little known abroad and barely briefed on the war, takes the oath of office.
event_desc.usa_united_nations: Representatives of the nations at war with the Axis gather in Washington to sign a joint declaration: each pledges its full resources to the common struggle and promises not to make a separate peace. It is the first document to use the name 'United Nations'.
event_desc.usa_uranium_committee: A letter warning that uranium could yield a bomb of enormous power has reached the President. He has asked a small committee of government scientists and officers of the army and navy to decide whether the research deserves federal money.
event_desc.vic_dakar: A British and Free French squadron appears off Dakar and calls on the colony to join General de Gaulle. The battleship in the harbour and the coastal batteries stand ready, and the governor-general must choose between the guns and the envoys.
event_desc.vic_fleet_ultimatum: The British admiral gives our squadron a few hours: sail to a British port or to the West Indies under guard, or be sunk where it lies. Yet the armistice forbids us to hand over a single ship.
event_desc.vic_full_powers: Meeting in the casino theatre at Vichy, deputies and senators vote 569 to 80 to grant full powers to write a new constitution. The next day the President of the Council becomes Head of the French State, and the Third Republic is over.
event_desc.vic_head_of_government: Under German pressure, a constitutional act creates the post of head of government. A minister dismissed at the end of 1940 returns to run domestic and foreign policy, while the head of state keeps his title.
event_desc.vic_japanese_demand: Japan demands airfields, garrisons and the right to move troops through northern Indochina, to cut the railway that supplies China. The governor-general has few soldiers and can expect no help from France.
event_desc.vic_levant_armistice: After five weeks of fighting, Damascus has fallen and British, Australian, Indian and Free French columns stand before Beirut. The high commissioner asks for terms: at Acre the Levant is handed over, and its garrison may sail home to France.
event_desc.vic_madagascar_armistice: Six months after British troops landed at Diego-Suarez, the last Vichy garrison in the south of the island has nowhere left to fall back to. The governor-general signs an armistice.
event_desc.vic_torch: American and British troops have landed at Casablanca, Oran and Algiers. After two days of fighting, the senior Vichy commanders in Algiers must decide whether to order a ceasefire or keep fighting the landings.
event_desc.vic_toulon: German troops are racing into the naval base at Toulon to seize the fleet. The admirals have standing orders that no ship may fall into foreign hands, and the scuttling charges are already in place.
event_desc.yalta_conference: The three Allied leaders meet at the Livadia Palace in the Crimea. They settle the zones of occupation in Germany, and the Soviet Union promises to enter the war against Japan within three months of Germany's defeat.
event_desc.yug_albania_falls: Italian troops have landed in Albania. Our southern border now faces Rome as well.
event_desc.yug_belgrade_coup: Air force officers move against the government that signed the pact. Crowds fill the streets of Belgrade, and the conspirators want to declare the seventeen-year-old Peter II of age and end the regency. Berlin will treat it as a betrayal.
event_desc.yug_chetniks_or_partisans: Two resistances fight in the homeland: the royal officers in the hills and the communist Partisans. Whom does the government back?
event_desc.yug_ciano_visit: Count Ciano signs the pact and promises that the Ustaše in Italy will be kept behind wire.
event_desc.yug_clearing_offer: Berlin offers to buy most of our exports through a clearing account. The prices are good, the marks are not.
event_desc.yug_concordat_crisis: Priests lead processions against the Concordat; the Patriarch dies during the debate and Belgrade riots.
event_desc.yug_election_results: Open voting, gendarmes at the polls, and still the opposition list takes over two-fifths of the votes.
event_desc.yug_eternal_friendship: Belgrade offers a pact of eternal friendship and says nothing about Macedonia.
event_desc.yug_federation_proposal: Belgrade proposes that our two peoples join one South Slav federation.
event_desc.yug_germany_on_the_karawanks: German troops now stand on the Slovene border. The northern frontier, quiet since the last war, has become a front.
event_desc.yug_maceks_terms: Maček wants a Croatia with its own Sabor, inside the kingdom but master of its own affairs.
event_desc.yug_occupation_partition: With the Yugoslav government in exile, the occupying powers draw their lines. We take northern Slovenia; Italy takes Ljubljana and the Dalmatian coast; Hungary takes Bačka and Baranja; Bulgaria takes Vardar Macedonia. What remains of Serbia stays under our military administration.
event_desc.yug_peasant_debts: Since the slump the villages cannot pay their loans. The state can take over the debts or leave them to the banks.
event_desc.yug_peter_comes_of_age: Crowds in Belgrade cheer the young king. Officers ask him to take the throne in his own right.
event_desc.yug_rump_serbia: The peace has left us only the Serbian heartland, bound to Germany. The name of a kingdom of the South Slavs no longer fits a state that rules from Belgrade alone, and the cabinet proposes to call the country Serbia.
event_desc.yug_serb_backlash: Serbian politicians and the Cultural Club protest that the Agreement has carved up Bosnia without them.
event_desc.yug_stojadinovic_falls: Five ministers resign at the regent's quiet request and the government falls. Stojadinović learns of it from the newspapers.
event_desc.yug_tito_returns: A metalworker from Kumrovec, back from Moscow, takes over what the purges left of the party.
event_desc.yug_tripartite: Berlin presses Belgrade to join the Tripartite Pact. Every neighbour but Greece has already signed, and the Regent has been promised that no Axis troops will cross Yugoslav soil. Many officers and Serbian politicians are bitterly opposed.
event_desc.yug_ustase_abroad: Pavelić's Ustaše train in Italian and Hungarian camps and smuggle pamphlets and bombs into Croatia.
event_desc.yug_zbor_clashes: Zbor students and leftists fight with sticks and stones outside the university.
event_desc.zaf_ev_centenary_trek: A hundred years after the Great Trek, replica ox-wagons cross the country to Pretoria. Men grow beards, women wear bonnets, and the crowds sing for a nation of their own.
event_desc.zaf_ev_delagoa_offer: Pretoria offers gold for Lourenço Marques and the railway to the Transvaal. The port lives on the Union's trade either way.
event_desc.zaf_ev_east_africa: The Italian empire in East Africa has fallen and our brigades were among the first into its cities. The country is proud of them.
event_desc.zaf_ev_fusion_strain: Europe drifts toward war and the two leaders of Fusion no longer agree what the Union would do. The caucus waits to see who gives way.
event_desc.zaf_ev_gold_premium: The price of gold is far above the old parity, and the mines are making profits nobody planned for. The treasury wants its share.
event_desc.zaf_ev_hct_request: South Africa formally asks for Basutoland, Bechuanaland and Swaziland. Their chiefs have told our officials they do not want to be ruled from Pretoria.
event_desc.zaf_ev_hertzog_leaves: Defeated on neutrality, the former Prime Minister walks out of the United Party with his followers. The question is where they will go.
event_desc.zaf_ev_japanese_submarines: Japanese submarines are sinking ships off the Natal coast. Shipping between Durban and the north is in danger.
event_desc.zaf_ev_mine_strike: Tens of thousands of African miners walk out for a wage they can live on. The Chamber of Mines asks the government to send the police into the compounds.
event_desc.zaf_ev_ob_founded: Out of the centenary trek grows a new movement, the Ossewabrandwag. It calls itself cultural, but it drills and swears oaths, and its members are counted in the hundreds of thousands.
event_desc.zaf_ev_purified_gains: Malan's party wins by-elections in the Cape and the Free State. Its newspapers say Fusion has sold the Afrikaner to the English.
event_desc.zaf_ev_red_oath: Clerks, farmers and miners queue to take the oath. Some of their neighbours call them traitors to the volk.
event_desc.zaf_ev_rhodesia_union: The Union offers Southern Rhodesia's settlers seats in Parliament and a share in its railways if London lets the colony join.
event_desc.zaf_ev_sixth_armoured: Our armoured division fights through the Apennines in rain and snow. The men signed on for Africa; most stay on anyway.
event_desc.zaf_ev_stormjaer_sabotage: Telegraph wires are cut and a power line is dynamited near Johannesburg. The police suspect the Sentinel's inner guard, and some policemen belong to it.
event_desc.zaf_ev_swa_germans: The territory's German settlers have their own clubs, schools and a branch of the Nazi party. Some of them want Berlin back.
event_desc.zaf_ev_tobruk_surrender: A whole South African division has gone into captivity with the fortress it was holding. Every town has a son behind the wire.
event_desc.zaf_parliament_vote: Britain's declaration of war on Germany splits the South African parliament. The Prime Minister wants to stay neutral; his deputy, Jan Smuts, wants to fight beside Britain. The vote will decide the country's course.

arg_ev_barracks_march.a: The government falls; the officers take power.

arg_ev_colonel_arrested.b: Hold him and clear the plaza.

arg_ev_maize_as_fuel.a: Burn the maize in the locomotives.

arg_ev_malvinas_note.b: A polite note and trade talks.

arg_ev_meat_inquiry.b: Open the books, whatever London says.

arg_ev_ortiz_illness.b: The president stays at his post.

arg_ev_palomar_scandal.b: Bury it to spare the army.

arg_ev_peace_prize.a: Take the lead at the League.

arg_ev_presidential_election.b: Let the votes be counted honestly.

aus_ev_brisbane_line.a: A royal commission finds no such plan

aus_ev_cowra.a: Round them up and bury the dead

aus_ev_dalfram.a: Enforce the law and load the ship
aus_ev_dalfram.b: Let the pig iron stay ashore

aus_ev_westminster.a: Leave it on the table for now

bel_ev_brussels_by_election.a: Every party behind the Prime Minister
bel_ev_brussels_by_election.b: Each party runs its own man

bel_ev_gold_reserve.b: Ship it to London and New York

bel_ev_kings_choice.a: The King stays with the army
bel_ev_kings_choice.b: The King goes with his government

bel_ev_march_on_brussels.a: Ban the march and arrest the leaders
bel_ev_march_on_brussels.b: Let them march and talk themselves hoarse

bel_ev_mechelen_incident.b: Call in the French and British now

bel_ev_rex_breakthrough.b: Govern with experts above the parties

bgr_ev_peshev_letter.b: Send them to the provinces instead.

bgr_ev_tsar_dies.a: A regency council of loyal men.

bra_ev_three_candidates.b: Let São Paulo's man run freely

can_bloc_populaire.b: Bring more Quebeckers into the cabinet

can_ccf_breakthrough.b: Call it socialism and fight it

can_gouzenko_affair.a: Protect him and expose the ring

can_on_to_ottawa.a: Pay them a wage on public works
can_on_to_ottawa.b: Send them home and keep order

can_ralston_crisis.a: Replace him; try for volunteers once more

ccp_ev_bethune.b: Keep him at the hospital in Yan'an

ccp_ev_first_harvest.a: Store it for the hard years

ccp_ev_korean_volunteers.a: Arm them and send them to the front
ccp_ev_korean_volunteers.b: Send them toward the Korean border

ccp_ev_northwest_council.a: Give the generals what they ask
ccp_ev_northwest_council.b: Keep the villages for the party

ccp_ev_plenum.b: Leave the question open for Moscow

ccp_ev_soviets_in_manchuria.b: Hold our positions in the south

ccp_ev_truce_breaks.b: Keep to the truce a while longer

ccp_ev_wang_ming_returns.a: Give him a seat in the Politburo
ccp_ev_wang_ming_returns.b: Keep him busy far from Yan'an

ccp_ev_western_route.b: Call them back across the river

ccp_new_fourth_clash.a: Rebuild the army north of the river

chn_ev_advisers_recalled.b: Keep their notes, burn the bridges

chn_ev_american_chief_of_staff.b: Give him the armies he asks for

chn_ev_henan_famine.b: Suspend the levy and send relief

chn_ev_inflation.b: Cut spending and take the anger

chn_ev_national_salvation.a: Let the courts take their time

chn_ev_no_more_concessions.b: Leave a door open for talks

chn_ev_one_army_offer.a: Accept and fold into the nation
chn_ev_one_army_offer.b: An army is not given away

chn_ev_provinces_submit.a: Seal it with a national conference
chn_ev_provinces_submit.b: Put their armies under one command

chn_ev_red_army_renamed.a: Take the badge, keep the army
chn_ev_red_army_renamed.b: Our army keeps its own star

chn_ev_south_anhui.b: Let it pass and blame the orders

chn_ev_soviet_credit.a: Ship the aircraft and the tanks

chn_ev_vice_chairman_leaves.b: Leave the door open for his return

chn_ev_victory_at_the_canal.b: Use it to steady the government

chn_ev_warlords_defiant.a: Buy them back with posts and silver

chn_ev_young_marshal.b: Send him back to his army

csk_after_munich.a: A firmer government for a smaller state.

csk_air_meeting.b: Study why the Germans were faster.

csk_ally_refusal.a: Then we must count on ourselves.

csk_danube_refused.b: Then the union will be made by force.

csk_fortress_tour.b: Show them little and learn from their questions.

csk_henlein_demands.c: Ask Paris what it will do.

csk_parachutists.b: Send them to build networks, not to kill.

csk_runciman_mission.b: Thank him and send him home.

csk_skoda_order.b: Keep the guns for our own army.

csk_tank_trials.b: Order more of the proven model.

deu_army_command.a: The head of state takes command

deu_compiegne_armistice.a: Leave the south to a French government

deu_croatian_state.b: Keep the occupation as it is

esn_carlist_defiance.b: Give the Requetés their own officers

esn_eastern_volunteers.b: Keep our young men at home

esn_hisma_offer.b: Keep the mines in Spanish hands

esn_hungry_years.b: Ask Buenos Aires for wheat on credit

esn_iberian_union.c: Refuse, and look to old allies

esn_oil_pressure.b: Keep selling and go without oil

esn_rock_offer.a: Ask for more before any answer
esn_rock_offer.b: Accept, and march on the Rock
esn_rock_offer.c: Refuse, and let London know it

esn_sierra_raids.b: Offer an amnesty to those who come down

esn_tangier_zone.b: Join it to the protectorate outright

esn_unification_crisis.b: Give the Falange the party machine
esn_unification_crisis.c: Give the Carlists the ministries of justice and worship

esn_world_turns_away.b: Soften the laws to win friends abroad

esr_after_victory.c: A people's republic led by the party.

esr_french_border.b: Ask for aircraft, whatever it costs.

focus_desc.alb_reforms: New law codes, schools and roads lay the groundwork of a young kingdom.
focus_desc.arg_abc_pact: The understanding becomes an alliance of the three great republics of the south.
focus_desc.arg_abc_understanding: Argentina, Brazil and Chile mediate together and settle their quarrels quietly, so that no one from outside does it for them.
focus_desc.arg_antarctic_sector: The weather station on the South Orkneys has been Argentine for decades. The navy maps a whole sector to the Pole.
focus_desc.arg_army_as_arbiter: The officers already removed one president. Every government in the Casa Rosada now governs with one eye on Campo de Mayo.
focus_desc.arg_army_reorganisation: New divisions, new depots and new regulations on the German model for an army that has not fought in sixty years.
focus_desc.arg_attack_wings: Northrop attack planes and the new trainers form wings to support the army.
focus_desc.arg_beef_and_wheat: The pampas feed half of Europe. The money from the cold stores and the grain elevators must start to build something at home.
focus_desc.arg_break_with_axis: The last embassies of the Axis close. The government says it chose; everyone knows it was pressed.
focus_desc.arg_british_capital: British firms already own the railways and tramways. Invite them to build factories too, and let them carry the risk.
focus_desc.arg_castillo_conservatism: The acting president trusts the landowners and the provincial machines. The reforms stop, and the opposition loses its patience.
focus_desc.arg_chaco_peace: Our foreign minister brings Bolivia and Paraguay to the table in Buenos Aires. Peace makes Argentina the arbiter of the south.
focus_desc.arg_clean_elections: The president promises honest counts and annuls the most shameless provincial results. The old allies are furious.
focus_desc.arg_com_general_strike: The ports, the railways and the packing plants stop at once. The party calls the workers to take power.
focus_desc.arg_com_meatpackers_unions: Twenty thousand workers kill and freeze the beef of Berisso and Avellaneda. The party means to lead them.
focus_desc.arg_com_nationalise_frigorificos: The British and American cold stores pass to the workers. London protests; the plants keep running.
focus_desc.arg_com_party_underground: Banned and hunted by the Special Section, the Communist Party organises in the unions and the immigrant quarters.
focus_desc.arg_com_popular_front: As in Spain and France, the Communists offer the Socialists and Radicals one front against fraud and fascism.
focus_desc.arg_com_workers_republic: Councils of workers and peasants rule from Buenos Aires. The estancias are next.
focus_desc.arg_comodoro_rivadavia: The oil found while drilling for water on the Patagonian coast now fills the tankers of YPF.
focus_desc.arg_concordancia_endures: The coalition has outlived its critics and its own president. It will choose the next one too.
focus_desc.arg_concordancia_pact: Conservatives, anti-personalist Radicals and independent Socialists share the offices among themselves. The pact must hold for another term.
focus_desc.arg_conscription_classes: Every class of twenty-year-olds serves a year. Calling up more of them fills the regiments.
focus_desc.arg_courting_washington: The Good Neighbor talks of friendship, while American farmers keep our beef out. Still, its machines and loans are worth a visit.
focus_desc.arg_cruiser_squadron: A new cruiser joins the fleet, to train cadets in peace and guard the trade routes in war.
focus_desc.arg_customs_union: One tariff for the river's republics: Argentine mills, Uruguayan wool and Paraguayan timber in one market.
focus_desc.arg_dem_alvear_returns: The old Radical president leads his party again. The Radical Civic Union still holds the majority of honest votes.
focus_desc.arg_dem_democratic_union: One list, one candidate and one demand: elections the government cannot count.
focus_desc.arg_dem_end_abstention: The Radicals stop boycotting rigged elections and fight for every seat, count by count.
focus_desc.arg_dem_hemisphere_democracy: Buenos Aires stands with the other republics of the Americas and with the democracies of Europe.
focus_desc.arg_dem_honest_ballot: The people demand the vote that the Sáenz Peña law promised them. If the government will not yield, the streets will decide.
focus_desc.arg_dem_radical_republic: An elected government sits in the Casa Rosada. It must prove that democracy can also keep order and pay its debts.
focus_desc.arg_dem_sabattini_cordoba: The Radical governor of Córdoba builds roads, schools and dams without the Concordancia. His province is the party's showcase.
focus_desc.arg_dem_socialist_allies: The Socialists of the capital and the Progressive Democrats of Santa Fe join the Radicals against fraud.
focus_desc.arg_destroyer_flotilla: More destroyers escort the fleet and watch the long coast down to Tierra del Fuego.
focus_desc.arg_estancieros_compact: The Rural Society and the cold-storage companies agree on prices with the government. London is pleased; the ranch hands are not asked.
focus_desc.arg_fabricaciones_militares: A directorate under an engineer general gathers the arsenals, the powder works and the mines into one plan.
focus_desc.arg_fas_axis_friendship: Rome and Berlin welcome a sister regime on the River Plate, with credits and instructors.
focus_desc.arg_fas_civic_legion: Uniformed volunteers drill in the parks with the government's blessing, ready to fight the reds in the street.
focus_desc.arg_fas_corporate_state: Parties and parliaments are a foreign invention, say the nationalists. Their legions move to replace them.
focus_desc.arg_fas_fresco_province: The governor of Buenos Aires Province admires Mussolini and runs his province like a corporate state in miniature.
focus_desc.arg_fas_liberating_alliance: The young nationalists march with raised arms and shout against the British railways and the Jewish bankers.
focus_desc.arg_fas_new_order: Guilds of employers and workers replace the unions. The state directs, and everyone obeys.
focus_desc.arg_fma_cordoba: The military aircraft factory builds engines and airframes in the middle of the country, far from any coast.
focus_desc.arg_foreign_concessions: Let the foreign companies drill faster than YPF can. The royalties and the fuel come sooner.
focus_desc.arg_fortify_the_plata: Batteries on the estuary and works on the borders protect the heart of the country.
focus_desc.arg_general_mobilisation: Every class is called to the colours and the factories turn to the war.
focus_desc.arg_german_arms_deal: An envoy sails for Berlin to buy the weapons Washington refuses us. If the British find out, the scandal will be loud.
focus_desc.arg_german_community: German schools, banks and clubs reach from Buenos Aires to Patagonia, and Berlin's embassy knows them all.
focus_desc.arg_gou_colonels_circulars: Typed circulars pass from garrison to garrison. They speak of a corrupt republic and an army that must save it.
focus_desc.arg_gou_descamisados: Pensions, paid holidays and collective contracts win the slums and the packing plants for the colonel.
focus_desc.arg_gou_labour_secretariat: A colonel takes the forgotten Labour Department and turns it into the workers' court of appeal.
focus_desc.arg_gou_lodge: Colonels and majors swear loyalty to each other in a secret lodge: no fraud, no communism, no British masters.
focus_desc.arg_gou_military_government: The generals dissolve Congress, intervene the provinces and promise to clean the republic.
focus_desc.arg_gou_national_economy: The military government plans its own steel, its own arms and its own merchant fleet.
focus_desc.arg_gou_revolution: The columns leave Campo de Mayo at dawn. By evening the officers mean to hold the Casa Rosada.
focus_desc.arg_gou_secret_arms_talks: No one in Washington will sell arms to a neutral. The lodge sends its own envoys to Berlin.
focus_desc.arg_gou_third_position: Neither Washington's capitalism nor Moscow's communism: Argentina will follow its own road between them.
focus_desc.arg_gou_war_ministry: The minister of war listens to the lodge. Promotions and postings now pass through its hands.
focus_desc.arg_grain_exports: Wheat and beef cross the Atlantic, and the payments fund the state's plans.
focus_desc.arg_hawk_licence: Curtiss sells its export fighter and the right to build it at Córdoba.
focus_desc.arg_hemisphere_defence: The war has reached us. Reservists are called up and the coastal batteries are manned.
focus_desc.arg_hemisphere_solidarity: Argentina joins the other republics in the common defence of the Americas, whatever its old pride says.
focus_desc.arg_iae_institute: Engineers at Córdoba design trainers of wood when metal is short, and dream of jets.
focus_desc.arg_import_substitution: When the depression closed the markets, workshops in Buenos Aires began to make what the ships no longer brought.
focus_desc.arg_industrial_promotion: Credit from the industrial bank, tariffs and state orders make factory work a career for the sons of farmers.
focus_desc.arg_infamous_decade: The Concordancia governs by managed elections and quiet deals with the estancieros. Order holds, but few believe the ballot boxes.
focus_desc.arg_join_the_victors: The war is all but decided. Declaring war now buys a seat at the peace and the goodwill of the victors.
focus_desc.arg_la_plata_refinery: The largest refinery in South America runs day and night to make the country's own fuel.
focus_desc.arg_malvinas_by_law: The claim will be pressed in conferences and courts, not with guns. Patience is also policy.
focus_desc.arg_malvinas_claim: Every schoolchild learns that the islands were taken by force. The government writes it into its maps and its notes to London.
focus_desc.arg_malvinas_landing: Marines and sailors rehearse the crossing from the Patagonian ports. The whole nation waits for the news.
focus_desc.arg_malvinas_ultimatum: Britain is fighting for its life in Europe. Its garrison on the islands is a handful of men; the moment will not return.
focus_desc.arg_mendoza_fields: Under the vineyards of Cuyo lies more oil. Wells rise among the vines.
focus_desc.arg_military_aviation_command: The army's squadrons get their own command, their own schools and their own bases.
focus_desc.arg_military_factories: A directorate under the army runs state factories for arms, steel and chemicals.
focus_desc.arg_motorised_cavalry: The regiments of the pampas trade some of their horses for trucks and armoured cars.
focus_desc.arg_mountain_troops: Detachments trained to cross the Andes passes guard the long border with Chile.
focus_desc.arg_nahuel_project: No one will sell us tanks, so the arsenal will build one: a heavy design with a Krupp field gun.
focus_desc.arg_nation_of_immigrants: Italians, Spaniards and Germans have filled Buenos Aires within two generations. Their sons are now conscripts and voters.
focus_desc.arg_national_defence_law: Industry, transport and manpower are put under one plan of national defence.
focus_desc.arg_naval_programme: Two dreadnoughts, two Italian cruisers and new destroyers make the strongest fleet in South America. It must stay so.
focus_desc.arg_neu_conservative_clubs: In the Jockey Club and the provincial capitals, the old families gather to take back the country they think is theirs.
focus_desc.arg_neu_landowners_rally: The ranchers bring their foremen and their votes to the plaza. Order, property and the old constitution are their words.
focus_desc.arg_neu_restoration: With the governors and part of the army behind them, the conservatives move to take the Casa Rosada back.
focus_desc.arg_neutral_trade: Both sides need meat, wheat and hides. Argentina sells, and the gold piles up in London and New York.
focus_desc.arg_neutrality: Buenos Aires keeps trading with both sides and resists every pressure to join a war.
focus_desc.arg_northern_fields: Geologists follow the Andes into Salta, where oil seeps from the foothills.
focus_desc.arg_ortiz_succession: A new president from the coalition takes the sash. His health is poor, and his vice-president is a man of the old school.
focus_desc.arg_paraguay_railway: A line to the Paraguayan border carries our goods north and their trade south through our ports.
focus_desc.arg_patagonian_bases: Roads, harbours and a naval base on the empty southern coast bring the islands within reach.
focus_desc.arg_patriotic_fraud: The provincial bosses know how to count. If the Radicals would win, the ballot boxes will say otherwise, for the good of the nation.
focus_desc.arg_plata_heritage: Once the River Plate was one viceroyalty, from Montevideo to Asunción and Potosí. Some in Buenos Aires have not forgotten.
focus_desc.arg_puerto_belgrano: The great naval base near Bahía Blanca gets new docks, batteries and depots.
focus_desc.arg_railway_nationalisation: Buy the British lines with the money London owes us for beef. The rails will run where Argentina needs them.
focus_desc.arg_rio_santiago_yard: A naval yard near La Plata will build at home what we order from Britain and Italy today.
focus_desc.arg_roca_runciman_renewal: Britain buys our beef on its own terms and keeps its railways. Renewing the treaty keeps the market, at a price.
focus_desc.arg_rosario_works: Argentina's second port grows mills and engine works along the Paraná.
focus_desc.arg_san_nicolas_steel: A great integrated steel plant on the Paraná will free the arsenals from imported plate.
focus_desc.arg_secretariat_of_aeronautics: An independent air force answers to its own secretary, equal to the army and the navy.
focus_desc.arg_state_arsenals: The army wants its own factories for powder, steel and rifles, owned by the nation and run by officers.
focus_desc.arg_state_merchant_fleet: With foreign ships gone to war, the state buys interned and laid-up hulls to carry our own harvest.
focus_desc.arg_state_of_siege: The constitution's emergency article suspends meetings and newspapers. The streets go quiet and the barracks start to talk.
focus_desc.arg_stubborn_neutrality: Europe's war is not ours. Argentina sells to whoever pays and signs nothing in Washington.
focus_desc.arg_submarine_service: The submarines from Taranto train a service that may one day close the Strait of Magellan.
focus_desc.arg_united_provinces: The old name returns. From the Andes to the Paraná, one flag flies over the River Plate.
focus_desc.arg_united_provinces_offer: Buenos Aires proposes one state again: the United Provinces of the River Plate, with a seat for every partner.
focus_desc.arg_unity_by_the_sword: Those who refused the hand will meet the army. The general staff draws up the plans.
focus_desc.arg_university_laboratories: Physicists and chemists in La Plata and Buenos Aires turn to the problems of industry and defence.
focus_desc.arg_uruguay_river_works: Ports, bridges and ferries tie both banks of the river closer to Buenos Aires.
focus_desc.arg_war_college: German instructors taught a generation of Argentine staff officers. The college now writes its own doctrine.
focus_desc.arg_ypf_monopoly: The state oil company gets the new fields and the right to fix prices. Standard Oil will have to wait.
focus_desc.arg_zapla_iron: In the hills of Jujuy, iron ore and charcoal from the forests feed the country's first blast furnace.
focus_desc.aus_advisory_war_council: Government and opposition sit at one table to run the war, without either giving up its seat.
focus_desc.aus_allied_base: American soldiers, airmen and a general from the Philippines arrive. Australia becomes the springboard for the counter-attack.
focus_desc.aus_also_at_war: Britain is at war, and as a result Australia is at war too. Few in 1939 think it needs saying any other way.
focus_desc.aus_anzac_pact: Canberra and Wellington agree to speak with one voice in the South Pacific, and to tell the great powers so.
focus_desc.aus_armoured_division: The 1st Armoured Division forms around a handful of tanks and a great deal of enthusiasm.
focus_desc.aus_australasia: The two dominions become one, from Perth to Invercargill.
focus_desc.aus_bardia: Engineers breach the wire at dawn, infantry pour through behind a barrage, and the Bren carriers follow.
focus_desc.aus_bathurst_corvettes: Small minesweeping sloops of local design, built in yards from Whyalla to Brisbane, escort the coastal convoys.
focus_desc.aus_beaufort: The Department of Aircraft Production builds the British torpedo bomber with American engines.
focus_desc.aus_bhp_newcastle: BHP's steelworks at Newcastle make some of the cheapest steel in the world. More furnaces, more rolling mills.
focus_desc.aus_boomerang: Wackett's team turns the Wirraway into a stubby fighter in weeks. It is not a Spitfire, but it is here.
focus_desc.aus_bring_them_home: Churchill wants the Australian divisions for Burma. Curtin insists they come home to defend their own country.
focus_desc.aus_brisbane_line: Planners ask whether the north can be held at all, or whether the vital south-east should be defended first.
focus_desc.aus_cac: BHP, GMH and their partners found a company at Fishermans Bend to build aircraft and engines in Australia.
focus_desc.aus_canungra: Every reinforcement passes through the rainforest camp in Queensland before going north.
focus_desc.aus_chullora_shops: Railway workshops in Sydney's west assemble the Sentinel, one cast hull at a time.
focus_desc.aus_coal_power: The Hunter and Illawarra coalfields feed the furnaces and the new power stations of the eastern states.
focus_desc.aus_coastwatchers: Planters, patrol officers and missionaries in the islands get teleradios and a code name, and report every ship and plane.
focus_desc.aus_cockatoo_island: The old convict island in Sydney Harbour becomes the navy's main shipyard.
focus_desc.aus_com_general_strike: The coalfields stop, then the wharves, then the railways. The cities go dark.
focus_desc.aus_com_legal_party: Banned or not, the party prints its paper, runs its candidates and fills the Domain on Sundays.
focus_desc.aus_com_militant_unions: Communists win office in the miners', seamen's and waterside workers' unions. The employers notice; so does the Comintern.
focus_desc.aus_com_waterfront: Wharfies refuse to load scrap iron for Japan's war in China. The strike is about more than wages.
focus_desc.aus_com_workers_commonwealth: Red flags fly over Trades Hall. The party proclaims a Commonwealth of the workers, and the army must choose.
focus_desc.aus_commonwealth_crossroads: Thirty-five years after federation the states still guard their purses, the Depression has not let go, and the Empire's guns are half a world away.
focus_desc.aus_crown_kingdom: A royal prince is proclaimed king in Canberra. The Commonwealth becomes a kingdom in its own right, bound to London by blood rather than by law.
focus_desc.aus_crown_loyal_leagues: Empire leagues and returned soldiers want the Crown closer, not further away: a king's man to rule, not a party.
focus_desc.aus_crown_royal_governor: Ask the King to send one of his own brothers to Yarralumla, and give him real power.
focus_desc.aus_crown_takes_charge: The Governor-General dissolves Parliament and governs in the King's name. Republicans and Labor men take to the streets.
focus_desc.aus_cruiser_tank: With no tanks coming from Britain, engineers design one around three Cadillac engines and a cast hull.
focus_desc.aus_csir: The Council for Scientific and Industrial Research has studied sheep, soil and prickly pear. Now it is asked for things that win a war.
focus_desc.aus_curtin_program: Full employment, a fair go for the worker, and a defence policy that starts with Australia's own air force.
focus_desc.aus_defence_talks: Our ministers sit with the Admiralty and ask the old question: if Japan moves, when will the fleet come?
focus_desc.aus_dem_free_press: Newspapers that were told what to print begin to print what they know.
focus_desc.aus_dem_restore_parliament: The chamber in Canberra stands empty. The people mean to fill it again, whatever it costs.
focus_desc.aus_dem_union_halls: Unionists, farmers and returned soldiers meet in the halls and draw up their demand: a Parliament the people elect.
focus_desc.aus_director_of_munitions: The head of BHP is given a department and almost unlimited power to make what the forces need.
focus_desc.aus_divisions_to_burma: The convoy turns toward Rangoon. Australia's soldiers will fight Japan in the Empire's line, far from home.
focus_desc.aus_dockyards: The yards on Sydney Harbour build destroyers and repair Allied warships.
focus_desc.aus_dutch_new_guinea: With the Netherlands overrun, its half of the island has no master. Australian soldiers are already there.
focus_desc.aus_eats: Australian schools train pilots, navigators and gunners by the thousand for the Empire's air forces.
focus_desc.aus_emergency_powers: Regulations under the National Security Act let the ministry govern by order. Elections can wait.
focus_desc.aus_empire_together: Whatever comes in the Pacific, Australia stands with Britain. The two fight one war.
focus_desc.aus_fas_australia_first: Stephensen's circle preaches an Australia free of London and of party politics, and finds readers among the disappointed.
focus_desc.aus_fas_march_on_canberra: Columns of Guardsmen and embittered veterans converge on the capital. The police step aside; the army does not.
focus_desc.aus_fas_new_guard: The men who cut the ribbon on the Harbour Bridge before the premier could are drilling again in the Sydney suburbs.
focus_desc.aus_fas_the_publicist: A monthly paper paid for by a rich admirer gives the movement a voice at every newsagent.
focus_desc.aus_fortress_darwin: Airfields, gun pits and fuel dumps turn the northern port into a base that can strike back.
focus_desc.aus_gmh_war_work: The Fishermans Bend plant turns out trucks, guns, aircraft engines and boats.
focus_desc.aus_graving_dock: A dry dock big enough for any battleship in the Pacific is dug out beside Garden Island.
focus_desc.aus_home_army: Every trained man stays in Australia. Let Britain fight in Europe; our war, if it comes, will come to us.
focus_desc.aus_hughes_returns: The wartime prime minister of 1916 is old, deaf and as fierce as ever. Soldiers still cheer him.
focus_desc.aus_imperial_partner: Australia speaks for itself at imperial conferences, but it speaks as a member of the family.
focus_desc.aus_imperial_preference: Wool, wheat and meat go to Britain on favoured terms; British machines come back the same way.
focus_desc.aus_independent_companies: Small commando units are trained by British instructors at Wilsons Promontory. One of them fights on in Timor for a year.
focus_desc.aus_independents_decide: Two independents hold the balance in the House. When they cross the floor, a government falls without an election.
focus_desc.aus_iron_ore_embargo: Japan wants to mine Yampi Sound. Canberra bans iron ore exports, saying the country needs every ton itself.
focus_desc.aus_island_bases: Moresby, Milne Bay and Manus become anchorages for the ships that guard the northern approaches.
focus_desc.aus_jungle_divisions: Infantry divisions shed their trucks and heavy guns for porters, mortars and pack artillery.
focus_desc.aus_jungle_lessons: On the Kokoda Track and at Milne Bay the army learns that the jungle is a weapon for whoever masters it.
focus_desc.aus_jungle_training: A jungle training centre teaches divisions to move, supply and fight under the canopy.
focus_desc.aus_labor_reunion: The split of the Depression years is healed: Lang's men come back, and Curtin leads a party that can win again.
focus_desc.aus_leander_cruisers: Sydney, Hobart and Perth, light cruisers of the Leander type, give the navy real teeth.
focus_desc.aus_lithgow_arsenal: The rifle factory in the Blue Mountains goes to three shifts and opens annexes in country towns.
focus_desc.aus_look_to_america: Free of any pangs about our traditional links with Britain, Australia looks to the United States for its safety in the Pacific.
focus_desc.aus_mandate_works: Roads, airstrips and a harbour at Rabaul for the territory the League entrusted to us after the last war.
focus_desc.aus_manpower_directorate: Every worker is directed to where the war needs them: the army, the munitions works or the farm.
focus_desc.aus_maribyrnong: Guns, shells and explosives come from the factories on the river west of Melbourne.
focus_desc.aus_militia_camps: Weekend parades and a fortnight under canvas each summer: the citizen soldiers of the Militia.
focus_desc.aus_militia_training: Long camps, regular officers and real ammunition for the home army.
focus_desc.aus_motor_industry: Bodies are built here, but engines still come from Detroit. Why not the whole car?
focus_desc.aus_munitions: The small-arms factory at Lithgow and the other government plants expand to arm the army.
focus_desc.aus_munitions_annexes: Railway workshops, car plants and country foundries take munitions contracts. Shell cases come out of tram depots.
focus_desc.aus_munitions_board: Lithgow, Footscray and Maribyrnong are a small family of government factories. The Board wants to make it a large one.
focus_desc.aus_national_emergency: Old Billy Hughes and his friends talk of an all-party ministry above the quarrels of Parliament. Many listen.
focus_desc.aus_national_register: Every man of military age is counted, his trade and his skills written down, before anyone is called.
focus_desc.aus_near_north: What Europe calls the Far East is, for Australia, the near north. The islands above us are our front gate.
focus_desc.aus_neu_country_movement: Graziers and wheat farmers, tired of the city parties, talk of a government of men who get things done.
focus_desc.aus_neu_national_authority: Parliament is suspended 'for the duration' and a council of national authority takes the reins.
focus_desc.aus_neu_strong_man: Lang in Sydney, Hughes in Canberra: the crowds want a leader who will stop the talking.
focus_desc.aus_north_south_road: Army engineers push a sealed road a thousand miles from Alice Springs to Darwin.
focus_desc.aus_northern_defence: Darwin has a small garrison, a few guns and a dirt road to nowhere. It needs more of each.
focus_desc.aus_noumea: France has fallen, and New Caledonia's nickel and harbour have no one to guard them. A warship in the roads can decide who governs.
focus_desc.aus_observer_unit: Horsemen and bushmen patrol the empty coast from the Kimberley to the Gulf, watching for landings.
focus_desc.aus_overseas_service: A new act lets conscripts serve in the islands north of Australia. Labor's old principle bends to the war.
focus_desc.aus_owen_gun: A Wollongong inventor's ugly little sub-machine gun works in mud and jungle when nothing else will. The army hesitates, then orders thousands.
focus_desc.aus_own_legations: For the first time Australia sends its own ministers abroad, to Washington, Tokyo and Chungking, instead of speaking through the Foreign Office.
focus_desc.aus_pacific_first: With Japan at war, Australian divisions are needed close to home rather than in the Middle East.
focus_desc.aus_pacific_power: Australia no longer waits for others to decide the fate of the islands around it.
focus_desc.aus_pacific_war_council: In Washington, Australia sits beside the President when the Pacific is discussed. A small voice, but its own.
focus_desc.aus_port_kembla: The rival steelworks south of Sydney passes to BHP and grows into a second great mill.
focus_desc.aus_raaf_expansion: The air force grows from a few squadrons of biplanes toward a force that can defend the continent.
focus_desc.aus_radiophysics: In a hut at Sydney University, scientists build Australia's own radar sets in secret.
focus_desc.aus_ran_squadron: A few cruisers and old destroyers, manned by Australians and trained in the ways of the Royal Navy.
focus_desc.aus_rats_of_tobruk: Dug in behind wire and minefields, a garrison holds out for months against tanks and dive bombers.
focus_desc.aus_reconstruction: Plans for housing, migration and industry are drawn up while the war is still being fought, so that peace does not bring the Depression back.
focus_desc.aus_second_aif: The Militia cannot serve abroad, so a new volunteer army is raised for the war overseas, as in 1914.
focus_desc.aus_self_reliance: Labor and a few colonels warn that the fleet may never come. Better aircraft and coast guns at home than promises from London.
focus_desc.aus_shale_oil: In a valley of the Blue Mountains a town is built to squeeze petrol out of oil shale. It is costly, but it is ours.
focus_desc.aus_sixth_division: Convoys leave Sydney and Fremantle for Egypt. The volunteers go to train where the war is.
focus_desc.aus_sound_finance: Balanced budgets and the Premiers' Plan brought the country back from the edge. Now the recovery must reach the dole queues.
focus_desc.aus_squadrons_overseas: Australian squadrons form within the RAF, from Coastal Command to the desert.
focus_desc.aus_staff_college: Australia's few regular officers are sent to the staff colleges at Quetta and Camberley, and come home to teach.
focus_desc.aus_steel_nation: Australia now makes its own plate, rails and shell steel. What it once bought it can now sell.
focus_desc.aus_tactical_air_force: Kittyhawks, Beaufighters and Spitfires move up the islands with the army.
focus_desc.aus_tasman_union: New Zealand was invited into the federation in 1901 and said no. A second invitation may be answered differently.
focus_desc.aus_timor_question: Portuguese Timor lies four hundred miles from Darwin and cannot defend itself. If Lisbon will not guard it, someone else will.
focus_desc.aus_total_mobilisation: Austerity, rationing and the direction of labour: the whole country is placed on a war footing.
focus_desc.aus_trade_diversion: Quotas meant to favour British cloth fall hardest on Japanese goods. Tokyo answers by buying its wool elsewhere.
focus_desc.aus_tribal_destroyers: Australia's own yard lays down big Tribal-class destroyers, the largest warships yet built in the country.
focus_desc.aus_trust_singapore: The great base at Singapore will hold and the Main Fleet will sail to it. Australia's money goes to cruisers for the Empire's sea lanes.
focus_desc.aus_tungsten: King Island and the Tasmanian hills hold tungsten, the metal that hardens armour-piercing shot.
focus_desc.aus_two_ocean_navy: From the Indian Ocean to the Coral Sea, the navy learns to fight off both coasts at once.
focus_desc.aus_uap_coalition: The United Australia Party and the Country Party share the ministry, as they have since 1934. Steady hands, few surprises.
focus_desc.aus_uniform_tax: The Commonwealth takes over income tax from the states. The premiers protest; the High Court lets it stand.
focus_desc.aus_up_the_islands: From New Guinea to Borneo, Australian divisions fight the long campaigns of the islands.
focus_desc.aus_war_book: A secret book lists every step to be taken on the day war comes, department by department.
focus_desc.aus_war_industry: Many times as many men and women make munitions as before the war. The country has become an arsenal.
focus_desc.aus_washington_legation: Casey leaves the Treasury for Washington, to make Americans think of Australia as more than kangaroos and cricket.
focus_desc.aus_westminster_debate: Canberra has never adopted the Statute of Westminster. Some call it a lawyer's matter; others say a nation should write its own laws.
focus_desc.aus_whyalla: A blast furnace and a shipyard rise beside the iron ore of the Middleback Ranges.
focus_desc.aus_wirraway: An American trainer, built under licence and armed, becomes the RAAF's aircraft for every job.
focus_desc.aus_women_at_war: The Women's Land Army, the auxiliary services and the munitions works take women by the hundred thousand.
focus_desc.bal_arms_imports: Buy abroad what our own arsenals cannot make, paying in credits and barter on easier terms.
focus_desc.bal_axis_tilt: Widen trade and military ties with Berlin and open the way into the Axis.
focus_desc.bal_border_forts: Bunkers and trench lines across the passes and valleys of our most threatened border.
focus_desc.bal_danube_rail: Lay railways from the river ports inland and widen the roads that feed them.
focus_desc.bal_land_reform: Break up the great estates, hand the land to smallholders and widen farm credit. A settled countryside fills the ranks.
focus_desc.bal_light_industry: Textile mills and food-processing plants turn the harvest into goods at home.
focus_desc.bal_mountain_troops: Raise mountain battalions from highland conscripts, with pack animals and mountain guns.
focus_desc.bal_neutral_bloc: Form a union of Balkan states that takes no great power's side.
focus_desc.bal_pact: Hold to the Balkan Pact of 1934: Greece, Yugoslavia, Romania and Turkey stand by each other's borders.
focus_desc.bal_partisans: The capital is lost, but the fight goes on in the mountains. Aid the resistance in the occupied lands.
focus_desc.bal_revisionism: Declare that the lands lost under the post-war treaties will be won back.
focus_desc.bal_royal_army: New officer schooling and more regimental exercises; the old establishment is trimmed and rebuilt.
focus_desc.bal_switch_sides: Our ally's defeat is at hand. Sign a separate armistice and join the side that is advancing.
focus_desc.bal_western_tilt: Reach out to London and Paris and ask them to guarantee our borders.
focus_desc.bel_aeronautique: The air arm is a part of the army, with biplanes from the last decade. It needs its own staff, airfields and a plan to fight.
focus_desc.bel_albert_canal: A great canal will join Liège to Antwerp, carrying coal and steel to the sea in big barges. It will also be a moat facing east.
focus_desc.bel_albert_canal_line: The main army will stand on the canal from Antwerp to Liège and leave the Ardennes to delaying troops. The forest is thought too thick for tanks.
focus_desc.bel_amnesty_law: The Flemings who worked with the occupier in the last war were condemned long ago. The nationalists demand an amnesty, and the government needs their quiet.
focus_desc.bel_antwerp_assembly: American car makers assemble trucks at Antwerp for the whole continent. A share of them could go to the army.
focus_desc.bel_ardennes_border: The staff will defend the forests on the frontier itself, with every road blocked and every bridge mined. The canal line is left to reserves.
focus_desc.bel_army_mobilised: Mobilised, Belgium can put more than half a million men behind its rivers and forts: a big army for a small country, if it is given time to gather.
focus_desc.bel_army_reorganised: The army of the Yser still has its pride and its old rifles. The staff wants new divisions, new guns and soldiers who serve long enough to learn to use them.
focus_desc.bel_authority_over_parliament: Some socialists and Catholics alike now say that parliaments talk while dictators act. They want a government that answers to the King and the nation, not to the party bosses.
focus_desc.bel_avions_fairey: The Belgian branch of a British firm builds its parent's designs under licence. Newer ones could follow the old biplanes down the line.
focus_desc.bel_black_brigade: The VNV gives its stewards black uniforms and a name. They guard meetings, break up others' and march through Flemish towns on Sundays.
focus_desc.bel_bleu: Luxembourg already shares Belgium's currency and customs. A closer union is only a few signatures away, if the Grand Duchess agrees.
focus_desc.bel_campine_mines: In the heathland of Limburg new pits reach a coalfield richer than the old ones of the south. Miners come from Poland and Italy to work them.
focus_desc.bel_canal_doctrine: The army will fight behind canals, rivers and forts, and give ground only line by line until the guarantors arrive.
focus_desc.bel_capital_air_defence: Anti-aircraft batteries ring Brussels and the Antwerp docks. The observers on the church towers get telephones.
focus_desc.bel_cavalry_corps: The cavalry trades its horses for trucks, motorcycles and armoured cars from France. The lancers keep their name.
focus_desc.bel_chasseurs_ardennais: Light infantry raised in the Ardennes, with the boar's head on their berets. They know every forest track between the Meuse and the German border.
focus_desc.bel_colony: A territory eighty times the size of Belgium is ruled from Brussels by a governor, the missions and the great companies. It is rich, and almost nobody in Belgium has seen it.
