focus_desc.bel_colony_at_war: If Belgium itself is overrun, the Congo remains: its copper, rubber and gold can still pay for the war and keep the flag in the field.
focus_desc.bel_constitution_defended: The oldest liberal constitution on the continent still binds king and parliament alike. Whoever tries to rule outside it will find the courts, the press and the old parties in the way.
focus_desc.bel_corps_de_marine: Belgium disbanded its little navy after the last war. A few patrol boats and a corps of sailors would at least watch the coast and the Scheldt.
focus_desc.bel_crossroads: Every army that marched between France and Germany crossed Belgian fields. The country must decide whether alliances protect it or drag it into the next war.
focus_desc.bel_cultural_councils: Two academies, one Flemish and one francophone, advise the government on the affairs of each culture. They have no power, but they do have a voice.
focus_desc.bel_dietsland_dream: The nationalists draw maps on which Flanders and the Netherlands are one people in one state. In The Hague the maps are met with polite silence.
focus_desc.bel_dinaso_militia: Van Severen's movement drills its men in green shirts and dreams of the old Burgundian Netherlands. It is small, disciplined and admired by officers who should know better.
focus_desc.bel_dutch_in_flanders: The language laws are enforced: Dutch alone in the schools, courts and offices of Flanders, French in Wallonia, both in the capital. The francophone bourgeoisie of Ghent and Antwerp protests.
focus_desc.bel_eben_emael: Cut into the cliff where the Albert Canal meets the Meuse, it is called the strongest fort in the world. Its guns cover the bridges to Maastricht.
focus_desc.bel_eighteen_days: The army falls back from canal to river to canal, fighting at each one. Every day it holds is a day for the Allies.
focus_desc.bel_flemish_new_order: In Flemish towns the nationalists take over the town halls and declare that Brussels no longer speaks for them. The state answers with the gendarmerie, and the country splits.
focus_desc.bel_fn_herstal: The national arms factory at Herstal makes Mausers and Brownings for half the world's armies. The Belgian army should come first.
focus_desc.bel_force_publique: The colonial army has Belgian officers and Congolese soldiers, and has been a police force more than an army. Trained and armed, it could fight beyond the colony's borders.
focus_desc.bel_foreign_fighters: Britain, Italy and America each sell a few modern fighters. Three types mean three kinds of spares, but there is no time to build our own.
focus_desc.bel_franc_recovered: The franc was cut loose from gold, and the factories of Liège and Ghent found buyers again. The recovery is real, but it was bought with the savings of the middle classes.
focus_desc.bel_frc_guns: The Royal Gun Foundry's 47 mm piece pierces any tank in service. Every infantry regiment wants a battery of them.
focus_desc.bel_french_accord: The military agreement with France stays in force. French officers will know where to stand, and Flemish voters will not forgive it.
focus_desc.bel_general_mobilisation: The reservists are called up and the army takes its war positions. The country holds its breath for months, and the economy suffers for it.
focus_desc.bel_gold_and_colony: The Congo's copper and the Belgian gold go to the Allied war effort. Belgium pays its way, even from exile.
focus_desc.bel_good_offices: The King and the Queen of the Netherlands offer to mediate between the warring powers. Nobody accepts, but nobody can say the Low Countries did not try.
focus_desc.bel_great_strike: The dockers of Antwerp walked out and the mines and mills followed. Employers and unions sit at one table under the government's eye: paid holidays and a shorter week are the price of peace.
focus_desc.bel_greater_netherlands: The new order offers The Hague a union of the Dutch-speaking peoples. Whether the Dutch want one is another question.
focus_desc.bel_guarantors_called: The guarantees of London and Paris are only worth what they will do on the day. Brussels asks them to say it again, and louder.
focus_desc.bel_hague_partnership: Old quarrels over the Scheldt and Limburg are set aside. The two kingdoms are the same size, the same fear and almost the same language in the north.
focus_desc.bel_hainaut_coal: The old pits of the Borinage and Charleroi are deep, wet and dangerous. Mechanising them would cost money and jobs, but leaving them would cost more.
focus_desc.bel_herstal_rifles: Herstal's short Mausers and the light automatic rifle replace the old weapons of the last war, one regiment at a time.
focus_desc.bel_independence: The King tells his ministers that Belgium must have free hands: no alliance that could drag it into a war, only an army strong enough to make any invader pay.
focus_desc.bel_industrial_mobilisation: Every large works receives sealed orders for the day of mobilisation. On that day, the furnaces will work for the army.
focus_desc.bel_kings_council: Leopold listens more to his military household and his secretary than to the party leaders. He believes the constitution gives the crown more than his ministers admit.
focus_desc.bel_kw_line: Steel gates and bunkers run from Koningshooikt to Wavre to cover the capital. The Allies are meant to take their place on it when they come.
focus_desc.bel_labour_plan: De Man's plan would put credit and the great industries under the state and spend the country out of the slump. Its friends call it a third way; its enemies call it the road to a planned dictatorship.
focus_desc.bel_lahaut_borinage: Julien Lahaut, scarred from a dozen strikes, tours the pit villages of Hainaut. The miners know him as one of their own.
focus_desc.bel_language_compromise: Neither side gets all it wants, so both can live with it. The quarrel does not end, but it moves from the street to the committee room.
focus_desc.bel_language_question: The north speaks Dutch, the south French, and the state, the army and the money have long spoken French. Flemish patience is wearing thin and Walloon unease is growing.
focus_desc.bel_language_regiments: Flemish recruits will be commanded in Dutch by officers who speak it. Many officers must go back to school.
focus_desc.bel_liege_position: The ring of forts that held the Germans for days in the last war is rebuilt with concrete, turrets and air shafts, and new forts are added to the east.
focus_desc.bel_liege_steel: Cockerill's furnaces at Seraing and the mills along the Meuse are some of the oldest in Europe. Modern blast furnaces would make them some of the best again.
focus_desc.bel_locarno_release: London and Paris agree to release Belgium from its obligations under the Rhine pact while keeping their own promise to defend it. It is the best of both worlds, on paper.
focus_desc.bel_london_government: If the homeland falls, the ministers carry the state abroad: the gold, the colony, the merchant fleet and the soldiers who escape.
focus_desc.bel_low_countries_defence: An attack on one of the three would be an attack on all. The promise is bold; the armies behind it are not large.
focus_desc.bel_low_countries_united: For the first time since the Burgundian dukes, the lands between France and Germany and the North Sea stand under one government.
focus_desc.bel_march_on_brussels: Degrelle calls his followers to converge on the capital, as another leader once did on Rome. The government must choose between a ban and a parade.
focus_desc.bel_matadi_railway: Only a railway round the rapids joins the river to the port of Matadi. Widening it would bring the colony's goods to the ships faster.
focus_desc.bel_merchant_fleet: The Belgian line to the Congo and the tramp steamers of Antwerp could sail under Allied escort if the homeland falls.
focus_desc.bel_militia_law: Uniforms, drills and marching columns of the parties are forbidden and the ban is enforced. The movements cry persecution, and some of their members go underground.
focus_desc.bel_ministers_above_parties: The King asks for ministers chosen for their competence, bankers and generals among them, rather than for their party cards.
focus_desc.bel_namur_forts: The Namur forts guard the meeting of the Sambre and the Meuse, the gate from the Ardennes into the plain.
focus_desc.bel_national_redoubt: If everything else falls, the army will hold Antwerp and its forts, as it did in the last war, with the sea at its back.
focus_desc.bel_national_union: The three old parties govern together, as they did in the Great War. None of them trusts the others, and each fears what would fill the street if they parted.
focus_desc.bel_one_belgium: The government holds that the unity of the state comes before the wishes of the regions. Flemish deputies walk out; the Walloon press applauds.
focus_desc.bel_one_candidate: When Degrelle forces a by-election in the capital, every democratic party, the communists too, stand aside for the Prime Minister. The Cardinal tells the faithful whom not to vote for.
focus_desc.bel_oslo_group: The small trading nations of the north agree to lower their tariffs toward each other and to consult in a crisis. Together they are not small.
focus_desc.bel_ouchy_convention: Belgium, Luxembourg and the Netherlands once signed a pact to lower their tariffs step by step. The great powers blocked it. It could be revived.
focus_desc.bel_party_truce: The party newspapers stop attacking the coalition partners for a season. Scandals are settled in committee rooms rather than on the front page.
focus_desc.bel_pays_reel: Rex's daily paper sells to those who feel the political class has stolen the country from them. Every scandal is a gift.
focus_desc.bel_popular_front: The communists offer the socialists a common list, as in France. The socialist leaders refuse, but many of their members do not.
focus_desc.bel_port_of_antwerp: Antwerp handles the trade of half a continent. New quays and cranes would make it a still bigger door to the sea.
focus_desc.bel_recovery_office: The banks are split from industry, credit is cheapened and public works are financed carefully. It is a banker's recovery: steady, sound and slow.
focus_desc.bel_red_borinage: The coal basin rises: pits are occupied, councils elected, the gendarmes driven out. Liège and Charleroi must choose a side.
focus_desc.bel_renard_designs: Alfred Renard designs fast monoplanes at Evere. His fighter is promising, but the order goes to cheaper machines from abroad.
focus_desc.bel_rex_rallies: Thousands come to hear a young man shout what they mutter. The police count the crowd and the ministers count the votes.
focus_desc.bel_rex_rising: Degrelle sweeps through the Catholic youth with a broom and a slogan against the corrupt. His rallies fill halls, and his paper names bankers and ministers by name.
focus_desc.bel_rex_vnv_accord: Rex, which wants a strong Belgium, signs a secret pact with the VNV, which wants to break it up. Both need the other's votes more than they dislike each other's dreams.
focus_desc.bel_rexist_state: The broom is raised against parliament itself. Rex's guards take to the streets, and the army must decide which Belgium it serves.
focus_desc.bel_royal_government: The chamber is sent home and the King names a cabinet of his own. The parties call it a coup; the palace calls it saving the state.
focus_desc.bel_royal_secretariat: The King's secretary becomes the most powerful unelected man in the country. Ministers learn to clear their speeches with the palace first.
focus_desc.bel_saio: Congolese soldiers march across half of Africa to fight the Italians in Ethiopia. Their victory is a long way from Brussels, and it is Belgian.
focus_desc.bel_scheldt_guard: The river to Antwerp runs through Dutch waters. Mines and shore guns on the Belgian bank would keep the port from being closed by surprise.
focus_desc.bel_secret_army: Officers of the beaten army organise in the cellars: arms caches, escape lines for airmen, and plans to rise when the Allies land.
focus_desc.bel_secret_contacts: Officially neutral, the staff passes word through attachés: where the Belgian army will stand, which bridges it will hold. Nothing is signed.
focus_desc.bel_service_law: Service is lengthened and the reserves reorganised. Flemish deputies vote for it only after the King promises that the army defends Belgium and nobody else.
focus_desc.bel_shinkolobwe: A Katanga mine gave the world most of its radium; its ore holds uranium too, a metal few have use for. A handful of physicists think that may change.
focus_desc.bel_social_pact: Employers and unions agree to meet in joint committees rather than on picket lines. Wages, hours and holidays become matters of negotiation, not of battle.
focus_desc.bel_societe_generale: One holding company owns a large share of Belgian coal, steel, banks and the Congo. What its governor wants, ministers usually come to want too.
focus_desc.bel_spaak_socialists: Spaak once marched with the far left; now he sits at the foreign ministry and talks of a socialism that serves the nation. The old guard of the party grumbles.
focus_desc.bel_staff_talks: The general staffs meet openly to plan where French divisions would enter Belgium. Berlin takes note.
focus_desc.bel_state_reform: A study centre drafts plans for a stronger executive and a weaker chamber. Its reports are learned and dull, and they are read closely at the palace.
focus_desc.bel_strategic_stocks: Belgium has coal but no oil and no rubber. Tanks are filled at Antwerp while the sea is still open.
focus_desc.bel_strike_committees: The summer strikes were started by rank-and-file committees, not by the union leaders. The communists mean to keep those committees alive.
focus_desc.bel_t13_hunters: A British tractor chassis with a Belgian anti-tank gun on top: not a tank, but a gun that can move. The cavalry and the Ardennes troops take them.
focus_desc.bel_union_miniere: The mines of Katanga pour out copper, cobalt and tin. The company answers to Brussels shareholders, and its profits pay a good part of the colony's bills.
focus_desc.bel_vnv_front: De Clercq gathers the scattered Flemish nationalist groups into one party. It speaks of Flanders' rights and of a new order, and it no longer hides the second.
focus_desc.bel_volunteers_spain: Young Belgians cross the Pyrenees to fight for the Spanish Republic. Those who come back know how to fight, and the police keep their names.
focus_desc.bel_young_king: Leopold III came to the throne after his father's fall in the Ardennes, and lost his queen in a car crash a year later. The country mourns with him and looks to him for a firm hand.
focus_desc.bgr_academy_laboratories: Sofia's physicists and chemists get money, instruments and students. Their work on electrets and materials finds military uses.
focus_desc.bgr_aegean_outlet: Neuilly took Western Thrace and with it the kingdom's only window on the Aegean. Without it Bulgarian trade passes through other men's ports.
focus_desc.bgr_armoured_brigade: A tank regiment, motorised riflemen and guns form one brigade. Bulgaria gets its own fast striking force.
focus_desc.bgr_army_beyond_neuilly: Twenty thousand volunteers cannot defend the kingdom. The general staff draws up plans for the army Bulgaria will need.
focus_desc.bgr_artillery_park: The old Schneider guns are overhauled and new howitzers are ordered. Gunners train with live shells again.
focus_desc.bgr_avia_licence: A modern Czech fighter is ordered with the right to build it at home. The first machines come from Prague, the rest will come from Lovech.
focus_desc.bgr_balkan_entente_seat: Once the outsider of the peninsula, Bulgaria sits down with the Entente's ministers to keep the great powers out of the Balkans.
focus_desc.bgr_balkan_redoubt: If the plains fall, the army will hold the Balkan range around the capital.
focus_desc.bgr_black_sea_flotilla: A handful of old torpedo boats and minesweepers are all Neuilly allowed. Their crews keep them ready and dream of more.
focus_desc.bgr_black_sea_ports: The quays of Burgas and Varna are lengthened for grain ships and colliers. A small yard can repair the flotilla.
focus_desc.bgr_black_sea_security: Soviet and Bulgarian sailors agree on the security of the western Black Sea. Varna becomes a friendly port for Sevastopol's ships.
focus_desc.bgr_bozhurishte_works: The state aircraft workshops outside Sofia have built biplanes in secret. They now build openly and learn to make modern machines.
focus_desc.bgr_break_imro: The revolutionary organisation ran Petrich like its own state and shot its rivals in the streets of Sofia. Its last cells must be broken so that Belgrade and Athens can be talked to.
focus_desc.bgr_bulgarian_designs: The engineers of Kazanlak and Bozhurishte draw their own reconnaissance and light bombers. They are modest machines, but Bulgarian ones.
focus_desc.bgr_cavalry_divisions: Horsemen still matter in the mountains and the Dobruja plain. Two cavalry divisions are kept at strength.
focus_desc.bgr_chaika_bombers: A Polish light bomber rebuilt to Bulgarian order arrives by rail. The crews call it the gull.
focus_desc.bgr_change_sides: The government breaks with its old allies and turns its army against them. The war goes on, on the other side.
focus_desc.bgr_clearing_with_germany: Germany pays for the crop in credits that can only be spent in Germany. The trade grows every year, and so does the dependence.
focus_desc.bgr_coastal_batteries: Guns are set on the headlands around Burgas bay. No enemy landing will come cheap.
focus_desc.bgr_com_balkan_federation: Bulgarians and Yugoslavs could share one federal state and settle the Macedonian question for good. Belgrade is invited to talk.
focus_desc.bgr_com_fatherland_front: Communists, Agrarians and Zveno officers act together: the partisans come down from the hills and the ministries are seized at night.
focus_desc.bgr_com_line_from_moscow: The hero of the Leipzig trial now leads the Comintern, and his instructions reach Sofia by courier. The party learns to build fronts with peasants and officers.
focus_desc.bgr_com_partisan_detachments: Young men take to the Balkan range and the Rhodopes with old rifles. They raid police posts and vanish into the forests.
focus_desc.bgr_com_peoples_republic: The monarchy is put to a vote and abolished, and the party governs through the Fatherland Front. Moscow sends advisers and friendship.
focus_desc.bgr_com_workers_party: The Communist Party is banned, so it works through a legal Workers' Party and the trade unions. Its strength in the towns surprises the police every year.
focus_desc.bgr_court_berlin: Germany buys most of the crop and offers credits for arms in return. The weapons come quickly; the debts last longer.
focus_desc.bgr_court_london_paris: The Western powers want Bulgaria out of Germany's pocket and offer modest loans. Sofia accepts politely and promises nothing.
focus_desc.bgr_court_rome: The Queen is a daughter of the King of Italy, and Rome treats Sofia as family. Italian aircraft and instructors follow the courtesy.
focus_desc.bgr_curb_the_legions: The Legions march in uniform and talk of a new order without the Tsar. Their rallies are banned and their leaders watched by the police.
focus_desc.bgr_danube_crossing: Pontoon bridges go up at Ruse and German columns roll south toward Greece. Bulgaria becomes the road of the Balkan campaign.
focus_desc.bgr_danube_flotilla: Patrol boats watch the long river border with Romania, and the river ports are fortified.
focus_desc.bgr_defend_the_rhodopes: The passes facing the enemy are blocked with bunkers and mines. Every ridge becomes a line.
focus_desc.bgr_dem_agrarian_union: Stamboliyski's movement once governed the countryside alone. Its village clubs reopen and its newspapers circulate from hand to hand.
focus_desc.bgr_dem_opposition_five: Democrats, two wings of the Agrarian Union, radicals and socialists sign a common platform. Together they demand the constitution back.
focus_desc.bgr_dem_peasant_democracy: Parliament sits freely again and the villages send their own deputies. Cooperatives and schools come before barracks.
focus_desc.bgr_dem_restore_tarnovo: The opposition calls the people into the streets and the garrisons waver. The constitution will be restored, by consent or by force.
focus_desc.bgr_dem_tarnovo_petition: Thousands sign a petition for the constitution of 1879, the oldest charter of Bulgarian liberty. The palace cannot pretend not to hear.
focus_desc.bgr_dem_village_cooperatives: Cheap credit through the cooperatives buys ploughs, mills and tobacco warehouses. The countryside begins to save instead of borrow.
focus_desc.bgr_divisional_areas: The kingdom is divided into divisional areas, each ready to raise its regiments on mobilisation day.
focus_desc.bgr_dobruja: Seek the return of Southern Dobruja, lost in 1913, at the negotiating table.
focus_desc.bgr_dobruja_at_the_table: Southern Dobruja is the one claim Bucharest might yield without a war. Sofia prepares its case and waits for Romania's moment of weakness.
focus_desc.bgr_eastern_volunteers: Berlin asks for soldiers against the Soviets and offers glory and arms in return. A Bulgarian corps entrains for the steppe.
focus_desc.bgr_eternal_friendship: A short pact of peace and eternal friendship with Yugoslavia breaks Bulgaria's isolation. The Macedonian question is left unspoken.
focus_desc.bgr_fas_legion_march: Columns of Legionaries converge on Sofia from every province. The government must crush them or give way.
focus_desc.bgr_fas_legionary_state: The Legions take the ministries and Lukov governs at their head. Discipline, marches and a war for the lost lands are promised.
focus_desc.bgr_fas_national_legions: A former war minister leads the Union of Bulgarian National Legions. Students and young officers join its ranks.
focus_desc.bgr_fas_officer_sympathisers: Lukov still has friends in the barracks from his years at the ministry of war. Some colonels promise not to fire on the Legions.
focus_desc.bgr_fas_ratnik_torches: The Ratniks march by torchlight in white shirts and threaten the "enemies of the nation". Their numbers grow faster than the police can count.
focus_desc.bgr_feelers_in_cairo: The war is lost for Bulgaria's allies. A quiet envoy travels through Turkey to meet the Allies and ask their terms.
focus_desc.bgr_first_tank_battalion: Eight Vickers tanks join the tankettes bought from Italy. A small battalion is the seed of Bulgarian armour.
focus_desc.bgr_frontier_railways: New lines and sidings toward the southern and western borders shorten the mobilisation by days.
focus_desc.bgr_fuel_reserves: Bulgaria has no oil of its own. Tanks dug near the capital hold a reserve for the first months of a war.
focus_desc.bgr_general_mobilisation: The reservists are called up and the factories go on war shifts. The kingdom stakes everything it has.
focus_desc.bgr_german_instructors: Officers from the Reich teach combined arms and radio procedure. The army learns quickly and borrows the German drill.
focus_desc.bgr_grain_for_arms: Wheat and tobacco are traded directly for rifles and guns. The army gets what the budget could never pay for.
focus_desc.bgr_harness_imro: The Macedonian bands know every pass across the border. Kept quiet but armed, they are a lever on Belgrade that no treaty can take away.
focus_desc.bgr_his_majestys_air_force: The hidden air arm comes into the open with its own name and ensign. Airfields are cleared and hangars rise near Sofia.
focus_desc.bgr_hold_the_new_lands: Garrisons and police are sent to the regained provinces to keep order behind the front.
focus_desc.bgr_industrial_concentration: The scattered workshops are merged into a few large plants around Sofia. For a small country it is a great effort.
focus_desc.bgr_iskar_power: Small hydroelectric plants on the mountain rivers bring electric light to the towns and power to the workshops.
focus_desc.bgr_join_tripartite: German divisions stand on the Danube and the lost lands are on offer. The prime minister signs in Vienna; the Tsar hopes to give as little as possible in return.
focus_desc.bgr_kazanlak_arsenal: The state military factory in the Valley of Roses makes ammunition, fuses and rifles' spare parts. It is enlarged for a real army.
focus_desc.bgr_kazanlak_flying_school: Pilots, observers and mechanics are trained in numbers at the school in the Valley of Roses.
focus_desc.bgr_krali_marko_line: Bunkers and anti-tank ditches are built along the southern frontier facing Turkey and Greece. The line is named after a hero of the old songs.
focus_desc.bgr_kyoseivanov_cabinet: A career diplomat who owes everything to the Tsar heads the government and keeps the foreign ministry for himself. Pacts with the neighbours become the business of the day.
focus_desc.bgr_labour_service: Every young man owes the state a year of labour on roads and railways. The labour battalions march, drill and dig like soldiers.
focus_desc.bgr_last_levies: Old men and schoolboys are called to the colours. The kingdom has nothing left to send.
focus_desc.bgr_lovech_works: A new factory at Lovech is built to make Czech-designed fighters under licence. The kingdom will build its own front-line aircraft.
focus_desc.bgr_macedonian_question: Skopje and Ohrid were promised to Bulgaria once and lost twice. The question cannot be dropped, only postponed.
focus_desc.bgr_military_league: The secret league of officers has made and unmade governments before. Its members in the garrisons are counted again, one regiment at a time.
focus_desc.bgr_motorised_units: Trucks bought abroad carry rifles and guns behind the tanks. The armoured brigade can now move as one.
focus_desc.bgr_mountain_warfare: The Balkan range and the Rhodopes cover half the kingdom. Infantry learns to fight on the ridges and in the passes.
focus_desc.bgr_new_provinces: Teachers, priests and officials follow the army into the regained lands. Roads and schools must win what the soldiers took.
focus_desc.bgr_no_eastern_front: Bulgarians remember the Russians who freed them from the Ottomans. Sofia keeps its embassy in Moscow and sends no division east.
focus_desc.bgr_no_party_regime: The parties stay banned and ministers answer to the palace. Order returns to the ministries, though the old politicians grumble in the cafés of Sofia.
focus_desc.bgr_officer_corps: Officers retired by the treaty are recalled and the Military School takes larger classes. Experience from the Balkan wars is not yet lost.
focus_desc.bgr_officers_take_sofia: Before dawn the league's regiments occupy the post office, the ministries and the radio. Whoever governs now must fight to keep the capital.
focus_desc.bgr_partyless_elections: Candidates stand as individuals, the lists are watched and women vote for the first time. The palace wins its majority, but some sixty opponents still find their way into the chamber.
focus_desc.bgr_pernik_coal: The state mines at Pernik feed the railways and the few factories of the kingdom. New shafts double the output.
focus_desc.bgr_polish_fighters: Fourteen gull-winged fighters are bought from the Polish works. They are the first modern aircraft of the new air force.
focus_desc.bgr_prepare_the_regency: The heir is a small boy and the Tsar's heart is weak. Naming the regents now spares the kingdom a scramble for power at the worst moment.
focus_desc.bgr_professor_at_the_head: An archaeologist who heads the Academy of Sciences and has never sat in a party leads the government. The Tsar expects learning and loyalty in equal measure.
focus_desc.bgr_rearmament: Shake off the arms limits of the Treaty of Neuilly and widen conscription.
focus_desc.bgr_reserve_divisions: Every trained man up to forty is listed for a reserve division. On paper the army doubles.
focus_desc.bgr_revision_committees: Refugee associations from Macedonia, Thrace and Dobruja are brought under one patronage. Their lectures, maps and songs keep the claims alive.
focus_desc.bgr_salonika_accord: The Balkan Entente agrees to set aside the military clauses of Neuilly if Bulgaria renounces force against its neighbours. The army can grow in the open.
focus_desc.bgr_san_stefano_bulgaria: The map of the treaty that lasted only months in 1878 is whole again, from the Danube to the Aegean and the lakes of Ohrid. The dream of three generations is fulfilled.
focus_desc.bgr_secret_rearmament: No neighbour will give Bulgaria its army back for nothing. Labour battalions drill with rifles and depots fill under false names.
focus_desc.bgr_seek_an_award: What Bulgaria cannot take alone a great power can award. Envoys go to the capitals that redraw maps.
focus_desc.bgr_sixth_fighter_regiment: The best pilots are gathered into one regiment to guard the capital. Its young aces become national heroes.
focus_desc.bgr_sofia_air_defence: Anti-aircraft batteries and listening posts ring the capital. The fighters get a warning before the bombers arrive.
focus_desc.bgr_sofia_shelters: Cellars are reinforced, trenches dug in the parks and families sent to the villages. The capital prepares for bombs.
focus_desc.bgr_sofia_workshops: Machine shops and textile mills around the capital take on more workers. The town grows into a city.
focus_desc.bgr_soviet_arms: Fighters arrive from Odessa by sea, with mechanics and manuals in Russian. The pilots learn quickly.
focus_desc.bgr_soviet_pact: A Soviet envoy offers mutual assistance against any attacker. Sofia, against all advice from Berlin, says yes.
focus_desc.bgr_state_above_parties: The officers' government abolishes the old party machines and runs the country by decree and plan. Kimon Georgiev takes the chair again.
focus_desc.bgr_strict_neutrality: The Tsar refuses every pact and every army's passage. Bulgaria will defend its borders and wait for the war to decide the map.
focus_desc.bgr_the_lost_lands: Two national catastrophes took Southern Dobruja, Macedonia and the road to the Aegean. Every schoolchild knows the map of what was lost, and every government is judged by it.
focus_desc.bgr_throne_above_factions: Neither the Legions nor the old parties can claim the Tsar. The crown stands above them all and the people learn to look to it alone.
focus_desc.bgr_tobacco_and_roses: Oriental tobacco and attar of roses are the kingdom's gold. The crop must buy what the country cannot make.
focus_desc.bgr_torpedo_boats: Fast boats are ordered abroad to guard the coast between Varna and Burgas.
focus_desc.bgr_tsar_and_the_kingdom: The officers who seized Sofia in 1934 are gone and Boris III governs through men he picks himself. A small, proud and wounded kingdom waits to see what he will make of it.
focus_desc.bgr_tsar_unifier: Lands lost a generation ago fly the white, green and red again. The crowds that greet Boris now call him the unifier.
focus_desc.bgr_tsars_balancing: Boris trusts no power completely: he takes Berlin's credits, keeps London's goodwill and never closes the door to Moscow. A small country survives by never choosing too early.
focus_desc.bgr_tsars_men: Officials chosen at the palace replace the party men in every ministry. Decisions come faster when every desk answers to one man.
focus_desc.bgr_tsk_corporate_bulgaria: Guilds of peasants, workers and employers replace the parties, and the state arbitrates between them. Tsankov leads the new order.
focus_desc.bgr_tsk_ministers_of_order: The movement offers the palace ministers who promise to keep both the communists and the Legions in check. One of them is a hard man for the interior ministry.
focus_desc.bgr_tsk_national_social_movement: The former prime minister who crushed the uprisings of the 1920s founds a movement on the Italian model. Lawyers, teachers and officers listen.
focus_desc.bgr_tsk_new_order_cabinet: Tsankov demands the government and his men in the police and army take the key posts overnight. Those who refuse will have to fight.
focus_desc.bgr_tsk_seats_in_the_chamber: Tsankov's men win seats as individuals in the partyless chamber and speak for order and corporations. They are polite, patient and well organised.
focus_desc.bgr_turkish_declaration: A joint declaration of non-aggression with Turkey quiets the southern frontier. The divisions in Thrace can stand down.
focus_desc.bgr_varna_naval_school: The naval school trains officers and petty officers for a fleet that does not yet exist.
focus_desc.bgr_war_academy: Staff officers are trained at home instead of abroad. Plans and maps for every frontier fill the academy's cabinets.
focus_desc.bgr_war_industry: Workshops become arsenals and the ministry of war takes over the order books. The country makes more of its own shells and less of its own shoes.
focus_desc.bgr_western_markets: Sofia sells its tobacco to London and Paris for hard currency, at lower prices but without strings.
focus_desc.bgr_zveno_circle: The intellectuals and officers of the Link have not forgiven the palace for pushing them aside. They meet again and talk of a state run by experts rather than kings or parties.
focus_desc.bra_abc_pact: Argentina, Brazil and Chile once signed a pact of friendship. Rio proposes to make it an alliance.
focus_desc.bra_abc_staff_talks: Staff officers of the three countries share maps and plans for the defence of the southern cone.
focus_desc.bra_air_ministry: Army and navy aviation merge into one air force under a civilian minister.
focus_desc.bra_american_steel_loan: The Export-Import Bank lends the money and American engineers draw the plans.
focus_desc.bra_anl_remnants: The National Liberation Alliance was crushed with the rising, but its cells survive in the ports and the barracks.
focus_desc.bra_aranha_mission: The Foreign Minister sails to Washington with a list: loans, a steel mill and modern arms.
focus_desc.bra_armed_neutrality: Brazil sells to all and fights for no one. The coast and the bulge must be defended by Brazilians.
focus_desc.bra_army_reorganisation: The army that fought São Paulo in 1932 is reorganised into proper divisions with a general staff.
focus_desc.bra_aviation_schools: New schools turn out pilots by the hundred, many trained on American aircraft.
focus_desc.bra_axis_friendship: Several generals admire the German army, and trade with Germany is growing. Rio leans toward the Axis.
focus_desc.bra_ban_the_parties: Every party is closed, the green shirts included. The Integralists expected seats in the new regime and got a decree instead.
focus_desc.bra_break_with_the_axis: The ambassadors of Germany, Italy and Japan are handed their passports.
focus_desc.bra_brigadier_campaign: Eduardo Gomes, survivor of the Copacabana revolt, becomes the opposition's candidate. Washington likes what it hears.
focus_desc.bra_burn_the_state_flags: In a ceremony in Rio the flags of the states go into the fire. There is one flag now, and one government.
focus_desc.bra_central_railways: New lines and repaired track tie the coast to the interior.
focus_desc.bra_chaco_mediation: Paraguay and Bolivia have bled each other in the Chaco. Brazilian diplomats help write the peace.
focus_desc.bra_chamber_of_400: The movement builds its own state in miniature: councils, a militia, schools and a chamber of four hundred.
focus_desc.bra_cisplatine_claim: Uruguay was a Brazilian province for a few years after independence. Some in Rio say it should be again.
focus_desc.bra_coastal_artillery: New batteries guard the bays of Rio and Santos.
focus_desc.bra_coastal_convoys: Coastal shipping sails in escorted convoys from Belém to Porto Alegre.
focus_desc.bra_coastal_patrol_wings: Patrol aircraft watch the shipping lanes along eight thousand kilometres of coast.
focus_desc.bra_coffee_institute: The coffee department buys the surplus and burns it, sack by sack, to keep the price up.
focus_desc.bra_cohen_plan: Army intelligence produces a document describing a communist plot. True or not, it is exactly what the palace needs before the election.
focus_desc.bra_compensation_trade: Germany pays in marks that can only be spent in Germany. They buy machines, rails and arms.
focus_desc.bra_compulsory_service: The draft law is finally enforced in the interior, not only in the capitals.
focus_desc.bra_condor_airline: The German-run airline already flies the coast. Its pilots and mechanics can serve more than mail.
focus_desc.bra_constitutional_rising: The garrisons of São Paulo and Minas declare for a constitutional government. The capital must choose.
focus_desc.bra_continental_leadership: Half of South America's people and land are Brazilian. It is time the continent heard it.
focus_desc.bra_crown_and_altar: The movement courts the bishops: an emperor, it says, would give the nation back its faith and its order.
focus_desc.bra_dasp: Examinations replace patronage in the federal offices. The state starts to know what it owns and what it spends.
focus_desc.bra_democratic_union: Liberals, old republicans and dissident officers agree on one thing: the next government must be elected.
focus_desc.bra_dip: One department censors the press, runs the radio and builds the cult of the president. Newspapers print what they are given.
focus_desc.bra_estado_novo_coup: Troops surround Congress, the election is cancelled and a new charter is read on the radio. Vargas now rules by decree-law.
focus_desc.bra_expeditionary: Brazil raises infantry divisions, trains them on the American model and prepares to ship them to Europe.
focus_desc.bra_expeditionary_force: People said a snake would smoke a pipe before Brazil sent troops to Europe. The division sails for Italy.
focus_desc.bra_father_of_the_poor: The censored press calls him the father of the poor, and in the factory towns many believe it.
focus_desc.bra_federal_intervention: Governors who defy Rio are replaced by interveners loyal to the president. The states learn who holds the purse.
focus_desc.bra_free_coffee_market: Stop burning money: let the price fall, let the weakest planters fail and move the capital to the cities.
focus_desc.bra_free_prestes: The Knight of Hope sits in a cell in Rio. His name is chalked on walls from Porto Alegre to Belém.
focus_desc.bra_french_school: The French military mission has trained the staff for two decades. Its methods stay.
focus_desc.bra_galeao_factory: The navy's aircraft factory on Governador Island builds German designs under licence.
focus_desc.bra_gaucho_cavalry: The cavalry divisions of Rio Grande do Sul ride the open pampa of the southern border.
focus_desc.bra_general_mobilisation: Reservists are called up across the states, from the pampa to the Amazon.
focus_desc.bra_german_mission: German officers replace the French instructors at the staff college.
focus_desc.bra_getulio_returns: Loyal officers and union men move together. The old president is carried back to the Catete on their shoulders.
focus_desc.bra_getulist_clubs: In the suburbs and the union halls people keep his portrait on the wall and talk of his return.
focus_desc.bra_goes_monteiro_doctrine: Góis Monteiro's rule: the army as a whole may act in politics, but no officer acts on his own.
focus_desc.bra_good_neighbour: Roosevelt's policy promises no more marines in Latin America. Rio tests how much goodwill is worth.
focus_desc.bra_green_shirts: Integralist Action marches in green with the sigma on its armbands. It is the largest movement the country has ever seen.
focus_desc.bra_hemisphere_solidarity: Brazil chooses the United States: loans, arms and a share of the hemisphere's defence.
focus_desc.bra_hold_the_election: The constitution calls for a new president. Vargas could step aside and let the candidates fight it out at the ballot box.
focus_desc.bra_hora_do_brasil: Every evening every radio station carries the same government programme. The president's voice reaches the backlands.
focus_desc.bra_hydroelectric_works: Dams on the rivers of Minas feed the new mills with electricity.
focus_desc.bra_ilha_das_cobras_yard: The navy yard in Rio is enlarged to build destroyers at home.
focus_desc.bra_imperial_house: Prince Pedro Henrique of Orléans-Braganza lives quietly abroad. Letters begin to reach him from Rio.
focus_desc.bra_imperial_officers: A few officers of old families listen. They would rather serve an emperor than a party.
focus_desc.bra_imperial_rising: The garrison of Petrópolis raises the imperial flag and calls the country back to the monarchy.
focus_desc.bra_import_substitution: What the war in Europe stops selling, Brazilian factories learn to make.
focus_desc.bra_integral_state: Family, nation and God: corporations replace parties and the chief rules in the name of the sigma.
focus_desc.bra_integralist_militia: Gustavo Barroso drills the militia in the parks. Its members swear an oath to the chief, not to the republic.
focus_desc.bra_integralist_partnership: Salgado's movement keeps its uniforms and gets a ministry. The regime gains a mass following and a rival it must watch.
focus_desc.bra_italian_submarines: Three coastal submarines are ordered from Italian yards.
focus_desc.bra_krupp_contract: The army orders a whole park of artillery from Essen, to be paid in coffee and cotton over many years.
focus_desc.bra_krupp_steel_works: German engineers offer the steelworks on the same terms as the guns: coffee and cotton, delivered over years.
focus_desc.bra_labour_code: Minimum wage, the eight-hour day, paid holidays and labour courts gathered in one code. It will outlive the man who signed it.
focus_desc.bra_labour_ministry: Unions are recognised as long as the ministry registers them. Workers gain rights and lose the right to strike.
focus_desc.bra_labour_party: His followers organise a party of the workers he protected, a machine that will win elections without him.
focus_desc.bra_lend_lease_agreement: Rifles, trucks and aircraft arrive at the docks of Rio and Recife.
focus_desc.bra_lobato_oil: Near Salvador the drill finally strikes oil, the first well in the country.
focus_desc.bra_march_on_guanabara: Militia and sympathetic officers attack the president's residence by night. The rest depends on the army.
focus_desc.bra_march_to_the_west: Roads, colonies and new towns push into Goiás and Mato Grosso, the empty heart of the country.
focus_desc.bra_minas_geraes_refit: The two old battleships get oil-fired boilers and new fire control at the Rio yard.
focus_desc.bra_mineiro_manifesto: Lawyers and bankers of Minas Gerais sign an open letter for democracy. Some lose their posts; the letter is copied by hand.
focus_desc.bra_moderating_power: As under the old constitution, the emperor stands above the ministers and settles their quarrels.
focus_desc.bra_monte_castello: After failed assaults in the snow, the division takes the mountain that held up the advance.
focus_desc.bra_motorised_column: Trucks bought abroad give the army its first motorised units.
focus_desc.bra_national_economy: Coffee alone cannot carry the country. The state will plan what the market has not built.
focus_desc.bra_national_motor_factory: A plant near Rio is built to make aircraft engines and, later, trucks.
focus_desc.bra_national_security_law: After the barracks rose in Natal, Recife and Rio, the law gives the police wide powers and a special tribunal to judge the plotters.
focus_desc.bra_naval_renewal: The navy's ships are older than most of its sailors. A building programme is drawn up.
focus_desc.bra_new_state: A new constitution concentrates power in the presidency and the federal government.
focus_desc.bra_northeast_bases: Natal is the closest point of the Americas to Africa. American engineers lengthen the runways.
focus_desc.bra_northeast_command: Natal and Recife face Africa across the narrowest part of the Atlantic. They get forts and guns.
focus_desc.bra_open_campaign: Rallies fill the squares of São Paulo and Recife, and the newspapers take sides openly for the first time in years.
focus_desc.bra_pan_american_host: The foreign ministers of the continent meet in Rio, and Brazil speaks for the hemisphere.
focus_desc.bra_patria_nova: A small circle of Catholic monarchists argues that the republic of 1889 was a mistake to be undone.
focus_desc.bra_paulista_constitutionalists: São Paulo fought Vargas for a constitution once and lost the war but won the charter. Its liberals have not forgotten.
focus_desc.bra_peaceful_succession: For once the sash passes from one president to the next without a revolt. The state of siege can end.
focus_desc.bra_peoples_republic: Land and factories pass to committees, and the new government looks to Moscow for recognition.
focus_desc.bra_petroleum_council: Oil is declared the nation's property, and a council sets out to find it.
focus_desc.bra_polaca_constitution: Francisco Campos's constitution, borrowed in parts from Poland, gives the president nearly every power and promises a plebiscite that never comes.
focus_desc.bra_port_strikes: Dockers in Santos and Rio stop the coffee ships. The police cannot arrest a whole waterfront.
focus_desc.bra_pragmatic_equidistance: Washington buys the coffee; Berlin buys the cotton and sells the guns. Brazil means to keep both customers.
focus_desc.bra_queremismo: Crowds march with one slogan. Whoever governs in Rio can hear them from the palace windows.
focus_desc.bra_red_barracks: Sergeants and young officers who remember the tenentes' marches are recruited one by one.
focus_desc.bra_red_rising: This time the barracks and the ports move together. The party calls for a people's government.
focus_desc.bra_republic_restored: Parties are legal again, Congress sits and the press prints what it likes. The decree-laws are reviewed one by one.
focus_desc.bra_restore_the_empire: Pedro Henrique is proclaimed emperor in Rio. The republic of the colonels and the coffee barons is over.
focus_desc.bra_river_plate_question: Argentina is the old rival in the south. Rio weighs talks against a race in cruisers.
focus_desc.bra_rubber_battle: With Malaya lost to the world, the old Amazon groves are tapped again by migrants from the northeast.
focus_desc.bra_salgado_candidacy: The chief stands for the presidency. If the vote is held, the green shirts will be counted.
focus_desc.bra_sao_paulo_industry: Textile mills, foundries and assembly plants spread along the railways of São Paulo.
focus_desc.bra_sell_to_both: Rubber, cotton and minerals go to whoever pays in gold. Neutrality is good business.
focus_desc.bra_senta_a_pua: The 1st Fighter Group flies Thunderbolts over the Po valley under its battle cry.
focus_desc.bra_south_atlantic_patrol: Brazilian ships escort the convoys between Trinidad and Rio.
focus_desc.bra_special_plan: A five-year plan of public works and arms, paid from a fund outside the normal budget.
focus_desc.bra_state_of_belligerence: The country is at war. Factories, ports and newspapers are put on a war footing.
focus_desc.bra_steel_bargain: Rio lets each capital know that the other has made an offer. Whoever builds the steelworks will win Brazil.
focus_desc.bra_steel_commission: Minas Gerais holds mountains of iron ore and the country still imports every rail. A commission studies a national steelworks.
focus_desc.bra_steel_mill: An American loan builds an integrated steelworks at Volta Redonda, in the Paraíba valley.
focus_desc.bra_technical_schools: The education ministry founds schools for engineers, chemists and skilled workers.
focus_desc.bra_tenentes_and_oligarchs: The young officers of the revolution want a strong centre; the old state machines want their offices back. Vargas plays one against the other.
focus_desc.bra_tripartite_overture: Rio quietly asks what membership in the Axis would bring. The question alone alarms Washington.
focus_desc.bra_vale_do_rio_doce: The state takes over the iron mines of Itabira and the railway that carries the ore to the sea.
focus_desc.bra_vargas_era: Getúlio Vargas came to power with the revolution of 1930 and has outlasted every rival since. The country waits to see what he will make of it.
focus_desc.bra_volta_redonda: In a bend of the Paraíba river rises the largest steelworks in Latin America.
focus_desc.can_air_training_plan: Wide skies, safe from the enemy, close to American factories: Canada offers to train the aircrews of the whole Commonwealth.
focus_desc.can_angus_valentines: The railway's Montreal shops build British infantry tanks. Most of them will sail for Murmansk.
focus_desc.can_armoured_divisions: Two armoured divisions take shape in England around the Ram and the training it allows.
focus_desc.can_arsenal: Canadian factories turn out vehicles, guns and ships for the Allied fronts.
focus_desc.can_arvida_aluminium: Cheap Saguenay power makes the smelter at Arvida one of the largest in the world. Every bomber in the Empire wants its metal.
focus_desc.can_bank_of_canada: The young Bank of Canada passes wholly into public hands. Its governor will run the war's money as carefully as the peace's.
focus_desc.can_beauharnois_power: The great canal at Beauharnois turns the river into electricity for Montreal's factories.
focus_desc.can_blue_shirt_legion: Uniformed squads guard the rallies and break up the meetings of their enemies. The police look the other way more often than they should.
focus_desc.can_borden_camp: The tank school at Borden trains its crews on a handful of old machines and a great deal of patience.
focus_desc.can_canadian_citizenship: Canadians are British subjects in law. A citizenship act would make them Canadians first.
focus_desc.can_canadianization: Canadian airmen serve in Canadian squadrons under Canadian officers, not scattered through the Royal Air Force.
focus_desc.can_ccf_government: Social democrats take office in Ottawa. Where another regime rules, the movement rises to restore elected government; under the ballot it simply governs.
focus_desc.can_ccf_hurricanes: Canadian Car and Foundry builds the British fighter on the shore of Lake Superior, with its chief engineer, Elsie MacGill, running the line.
focus_desc.can_cmp_trucks: Ford and General Motors of Canada build one common pattern of army truck. It will carry the Eighth Army across the desert as well as the Canadians through Holland.
focus_desc.can_commonwealth_arsenal: Canada makes more war material than it can use. Shells, trucks, ships and aircraft go out to every Allied front.
focus_desc.can_conscription_if_necessary: Not necessarily conscription, but conscription if necessary. The Prime Minister's formula buys time and keeps both halves of the country inside the tent.
focus_desc.can_consumer_factories: American firms build branch plants behind the tariff wall in Ontario and Quebec. The jobs are Canadian even if the head offices are not.
focus_desc.can_continental_alliance: Geography is destiny: Canada's security lies with the continent, not with an empire across the ocean.
focus_desc.can_continental_partners: A highway to Alaska, a pipeline from Norman Wells, airfields across the North: the neighbours build the northern defences together.
focus_desc.can_cooperative_commonwealth: Wheat pools, credit unions and public power: the prairie habit of doing things together becomes a national plan.
focus_desc.can_corvette_yards: Shipyards on the Great Lakes and the St. Lawrence build a whaler's design into a small escort by the dozen.
focus_desc.can_crown_plants: Where private industry cannot or will not build, the Crown builds the factory itself and hires a company to run it.
focus_desc.can_defence_scheme_three: The staff's plan for an expeditionary force: two divisions ready to sail if Parliament decides.
focus_desc.can_dollar_a_year_men: Business executives come to Ottawa for a token salary to run the war's controls and companies.
focus_desc.can_dominion_of_order: Parliament gives way to a corporate chamber and the leader's word. The new regime promises work, discipline and a place beside the new powers of Europe.
focus_desc.can_eastern_air_command: Flying boats and bombers out of Dartmouth and Gander close the air gap over the convoys a little more each year.
focus_desc.can_eldorado_radium: The mine on Great Bear Lake was dug for radium. Its waste heaps of uranium ore may soon be worth more than the radium ever was.
focus_desc.can_end_privy_appeals: Appeals to the Privy Council in London end; the Supreme Court in Ottawa has the final word on Canadian law.
focus_desc.can_escort_navy: Small warships from Canadian yards take over the escort of convoys across the North Atlantic.
focus_desc.can_external_affairs: A handful of brilliant officials in the East Block become a foreign service, and the Under-Secretary its conscience.
focus_desc.can_family_allowances: A monthly cheque for every child under sixteen. Critics call it a bribe to Quebec's large families; mothers in every province cash it.
focus_desc.can_first_canadian_army: Two corps, five divisions and two armoured brigades under Canadian command: the largest field force the country has raised.
focus_desc.can_first_division_sails: Volunteers fill the regiments in weeks. The first contingent crosses to England to train and wait.
focus_desc.can_fleet_to_halifax: What the Royal Navy saved from home waters anchors in Halifax and Bermuda and fights on from there.
focus_desc.can_general_strike: Winnipeg was crushed once. This time the strike spreads from the steel mills to the railways, and the strike committees arm themselves.
focus_desc.can_gold_to_ottawa: Britain ships its gold and securities across the Atlantic in warships, to vaults under a Montreal insurance building.
focus_desc.can_good_neighbours: The President comes to Kingston and promises that the United States will not stand idly by if Canada is threatened.
focus_desc.can_grizzly_and_sexton: Montreal Locomotive builds the American medium tank under its own name, and a self-propelled gun on the Ram's chassis.
focus_desc.can_halifax_station: The great harbour of Halifax becomes the convoy port of the Atlantic, with booms, batteries and dockyard.
focus_desc.can_hamilton_steel: The mills at Hamilton and the Sault run three shifts again. Steel is the first thing a war economy runs short of.
focus_desc.can_home_defence_divisions: Divisions kept at home for the coasts and for the country's peace of mind, filled by men who did not choose to go overseas.
focus_desc.can_home_war_squadrons: Squadrons on both coasts to hunt submarines and guard the convoy ports.
focus_desc.can_hyde_park_deal: The war drains Canada's American dollars. The answer is to sell Washington as many munitions as Canada buys from it.
focus_desc.can_imperial_conference: In London the Prime Minister promises nothing in advance: Parliament will decide. The British are reassured and annoyed at once.
focus_desc.can_imperial_partnership: Canada stands first with Britain: one foreign policy for the Empire, settled together, and a Canadian voice in it.
focus_desc.can_industrial_unions: The new industrial unions organise whole plants, not trades. Party members are the best organisers in the steel towns, and everyone knows it.
focus_desc.can_infantry_reinforcements: The battles eat riflemen faster than volunteers arrive. Somewhere in Canada there are trained men; the question is whether they can be sent.
focus_desc.can_kingdom_of_canada: The founders once wanted that name. A Canada that shares only its King with Britain takes it at last.
focus_desc.can_labor_progressive_party: Banned again, the party returns under a new name and wins a Montreal seat in Parliament. Its members sit on union executives across the country.
focus_desc.can_lancaster_x: Victory Aircraft rolls out Lancasters that fly the Atlantic to join No. 6 Group.
focus_desc.can_lead_the_commonwealth: Australia, New Zealand and South Africa look to Ottawa now. Canada takes up the leadership of what is left of the Commonwealth's war.
focus_desc.can_liberal_mandate: A Liberal Canada that has kept its balance only grows steadier. If another regime holds Ottawa, the parliamentarians call the country back to the ballot box, by force if they must.
focus_desc.can_long_branch_arsenal: A small arms plant outside Toronto, and a Bren gun line at the Inglis works, so the army need not wait for British rifles.
focus_desc.can_mackenzie_papineau: Over a thousand Canadians cross to Spain to fight for the Republic, against their own government's law. Those who come home come back as cadres.
focus_desc.can_maple_leaf_flag: The Red Ensign or something new? A maple leaf is the one symbol both languages already share.
focus_desc.can_march_on_ottawa: The blue shirts march on Parliament Hill. Part of the militia follows them, the rest stands by the elected government, and the country splits.
focus_desc.can_mid_ocean_escort: Canadian groups take convoys from Newfoundland to the meeting point off Iceland, in the worst water of the Atlantic.
focus_desc.can_middle_power: Not a great power, not a small one: Canada claims a voice wherever it carries a real share of the load.
focus_desc.can_militia_reorganization: A militia of paper regiments is cut down to units that can actually be mobilised, with modern establishments on paper at least.
focus_desc.can_montreal_laboratory: British and French atomic scientists move to Montreal, and a heavy-water pile begins to rise at Chalk River.
focus_desc.can_mosquito_works: De Havilland's Canadian plant builds the wooden wonder with Packard engines and Canadian spruce.
focus_desc.can_munitions_and_supply: One department, one minister and powers no peacetime cabinet would grant: it buys, builds and orders whatever the war needs.
focus_desc.can_mutual_aid_board: Britain cannot pay. Canada gives: first a billion dollars outright, then a Mutual Aid Board that hands out war material by need.
focus_desc.can_national_registration: Every adult registers. The government learns who it could call up, and promises again it will not send them overseas.
focus_desc.can_national_research_council: A small council with a new laboratory on Sussex Drive becomes the country's war science office.
focus_desc.can_national_unity_party: Adrien Arcand's blue shirts drill in Montreal halls and preach a corporate state. A small movement, but a hard and loud one.
focus_desc.can_newfoundland_confederation: Why wait? Ottawa offers to take Newfoundland and Labrador into Confederation as the tenth province, debts and all.
focus_desc.can_newfoundland_garrison: Britain's oldest colony is bankrupt and run by a commission. Canada sends troops and airmen to guard Gander and St. John's, and asks for nothing more.
focus_desc.can_north_atlantic_triangle: Canada's place is between London and Washington, interpreting each to the other and never choosing one against the other.
focus_desc.can_northern_mining: Gold carried the Shield through the Depression. Nickel from Sudbury, copper and zinc follow it out of the rock.
focus_desc.can_northwest_atlantic: The only Allied theatre ever commanded by a Canadian: the convoy lanes west of the meeting point.
focus_desc.can_ogdensburg_board: Prime Minister and President meet in a railway car at Ogdensburg and agree to plan the continent's defence together.
focus_desc.can_order_and_parish: Unions give way to Catholic syndicates and chambers of trade; the parish, the family and the province are the pillars of the new order.
focus_desc.can_ottawa_war_cabinet: The Empire's war is run from Parliament Hill now. The senior Dominion takes the decisions the mother country no longer can.
focus_desc.can_own_declaration: When Britain goes to war, Canada waits a week and declares war on its own, by a vote of its own Parliament.
focus_desc.can_pacific_coast_defence: Batteries at Esquimalt and Vancouver, and a watch on a coast that Ottawa has long forgotten.
focus_desc.can_padlock_act: Any house used to spread 'communism or bolshevism' can be locked by the attorney general. The law never defines either word.
focus_desc.can_park_steamships: A Crown company orders cargo ships by the hundred and names them for Canada's parks.
focus_desc.can_provinces_inquiry: The provinces are broke and the Dominion holds the taxes. A royal commission travels the country to ask who should pay for relief, roads and schools.
focus_desc.can_provinces_league: Quebec City and Edmonton join hands against Ottawa. Their premiers speak of a Canada of strong provinces under a government that answers to no party.
focus_desc.can_provincial_rights: Quebec's premier and Alberta's preacher agree on one thing: Ottawa takes too much. A league of the provinces' strong men offers order without the old parties.
focus_desc.can_public_ownership: Banks, utilities and the war plants pass to Crown corporations answerable to Parliament, not to shareholders in Montreal and New York.
focus_desc.can_public_works: Roads, harbours and post offices give the jobless a wage instead of a relief voucher.
focus_desc.can_quebec_lieutenant: No government holds without French Canada. The Minister of Justice speaks for Quebec in cabinet and for the cabinet in Quebec.
focus_desc.can_quebec_reassured: A respected Quebec lawyer takes the Justice portfolio and tells his province that the government keeps its word as far as the war allows.
focus_desc.can_radio_section: British scientists bring their secrets across the Atlantic; Canadian physicists turn them into working sets for ships and coasts.
focus_desc.can_ram_programme: An American chassis, a Canadian hull and a British gun: the country's own cruiser tank, built at Montreal Locomotive.
focus_desc.can_rcaf_independent: The RCAF stops being a branch of the militia and flies under its own Chief of the Air Staff.
focus_desc.can_reciprocity_treaty: The first trade agreement with the United States in decades cuts the tariffs that the Depression piled up along the border.
focus_desc.can_regina_manifesto: Farmers' cooperatives and labour parties promise to eradicate capitalism by the ballot. The Co-operative Commonwealth Federation asks the country to give it a chance.
focus_desc.can_relief_camps_closed: The Depression's work camps for single jobless men are a scandal since the trek to Ottawa ended in a riot. The new government shuts them and looks for work that pays a wage.
focus_desc.can_research_enterprises: A Crown company in Leaside builds optical glass, radar and fire-control sets by the thousand.
focus_desc.can_river_destroyers: The Royal Navy sells Canada modern destroyers, named for Canadian rivers.
focus_desc.can_river_frigates: Longer legs and more depth charges than the corvettes: the frigates can hunt a submarine to the end.
focus_desc.can_save_the_navy: Treasury men once proposed scrapping the navy to save money. A few destroyers and a stubborn Chief of the Naval Staff keep it alive.
focus_desc.can_section_98_repealed: The law that jailed the Communist leaders is gone. Tim Buck's party organises in the open, in the mines, the camps and the auto plants.
focus_desc.can_set_piece_battles: Plan every step, mass the guns, and let the artillery carry the infantry forward. It is slow, and it works.
focus_desc.can_shelter_the_crown: If the islands fall, the fleet, the gold and the royal family will come here. Ottawa prepares to be the capital of an Empire at war.
focus_desc.can_six_group: Canada's bomber squadrons in Yorkshire join into one group of their own, paid for and led by Canadians.
focus_desc.can_social_credit: Prosperity certificates, a dividend for every citizen and a war on the bankers: the radio preacher's Alberta is the movement's laboratory.
focus_desc.can_sorel_guns: A shipbuilding family's works at Sorel turn to field guns and naval mounts.
focus_desc.can_special_service_force: Canadians and Americans train together in Montana as one commando force: ski troops, paratroopers and mountain fighters at once.
focus_desc.can_stay_out: Ireland stays out; why not Canada? A Dominion that is equal in law may also be neutral in fact.
focus_desc.can_strongmen_take_ottawa: The provincial police and the leagues will not wait for another election. Their followers seize Ottawa, and the loyal half of the country takes up arms.
focus_desc.can_tribal_class: The navy wants real fighting destroyers too, and orders the big Tribal class, some built in Britain and some at Halifax.
focus_desc.can_turner_valley_oil: A deep well south of Calgary strikes crude, not just gas. Alberta becomes the Empire's only oil field on this continent.
focus_desc.can_unemployment_insurance: The courts struck down the last attempt as a provincial matter. A constitutional amendment, agreed with every province, lets Ottawa insure the jobless.
focus_desc.can_unity_first: The Prime Minister's art is to do nothing that splits the country. Every policy is weighed first by how Quebec and Ontario will take it, then by what it does.
focus_desc.can_uranium: The radium mine on Great Bear Lake reopens to ship uranium ore south.
focus_desc.can_veterans_charter: Land, education and a start in life for everyone who served: the country means to do better than after the last war.
focus_desc.can_victory_aircraft: The government takes over the Malton plant and turns it to four-engined bombers built in Canada.
focus_desc.can_vimy_memory: The Canadian Corps of the last war fought together under its own commander and took the ridge. The new army means to do the same.
focus_desc.can_volunteers_only: The pledge stands without conditions. Canada fights with whoever chooses to go, and with no one else.
focus_desc.can_war_measures: Parliament hands the cabinet powers to govern by order: prices, wages, censorship and internment.
focus_desc.can_welcome_the_king: The King and Queen will cross the country by train, the first reigning monarch to set foot in Canada.
focus_desc.can_western_nationalists: The Winnipeg nationalists and the Ontario clubs fold into Arcand's party. For the first time the movement speaks in both languages.
focus_desc.can_westminster_powers: The Statute of Westminster made Canada's Parliament equal to Britain's in law. Ottawa now learns to use what it was given: its own treaties, its own envoys, its own word on war.
focus_desc.can_which_canada: English and French, East and West, farmer and worker: the country holds together by compromise. Which road it takes from here decides whether the compromise lasts.
focus_desc.can_workers_dominion: Councils of workers and farmers run the plants and the wheat pools. The new government looks to Moscow for advice and to its own people for patience.
focus_desc.ccp_agents_in_the_rear: A general's private secretary, a staff officer, a cipher clerk: the party's people serve in the other camp and report.
focus_desc.ccp_ample_food_and_clothing: For the first time the Border Region feeds and clothes itself. The poorest corner of China no longer starves.
focus_desc.ccp_annihilation_battles: Do not rout ten divisions; destroy one. Every battle must end with the enemy unit gone and its weapons ours.
focus_desc.ccp_anti_fascist_front: We are part of a war fought from Stalingrad to the Pacific. The allies of China are our allies too.
focus_desc.ccp_arms_from_the_enemy: Our arsenal is the enemy's supply column. Every ambush is planned around the rifles, bullets and mortars it will bring us.
focus_desc.ccp_artillery_school: A handful of captured guns become a school. Gunners trained here will command the batteries we do not have yet.
focus_desc.ccp_aviation_school: Captured aircraft, Japanese instructors who stayed and students who have never driven a car: the party's air force starts here.
focus_desc.ccp_base_areas: Widen the base areas in the countryside behind Japanese lines and set up local governments.
focus_desc.ccp_bethune_hospitals: Surgery a few miles behind the line saves men who would die on the long road to the rear. Village nurses learn on the job.
focus_desc.ccp_border_elections: Villagers who cannot read vote by dropping beans into bowls behind each candidate. The party learns that it can win votes as well as battles.
focus_desc.ccp_border_region_bank: The Border Region prints its own notes and keeps the Nationalist currency out. Whether people trust them is another matter.
focus_desc.ccp_cadres: Train military and administrative cadres and send them to the units and base areas.
focus_desc.ccp_captured_arms: Repair and reissue weapons and ammunition taken from the enemy as a main source of supply.
focus_desc.ccp_careful_screening: Suspects are examined case by case, and nobody is condemned on a forced confession. Slower, but the young volunteers keep their faith.
focus_desc.ccp_cave_arsenals: Set up small arsenals in hillside caves to make rifles and grenades.
focus_desc.ccp_cave_workshops: Lathes carried over the mountains on mule-back turn out rifle parts and grenades in caves the bombers cannot find.
focus_desc.ccp_central_party_school: Cadres from every base come to Yan'an to study for months. They go back with one vocabulary and one chain of command.
focus_desc.ccp_chongqing_talks: The two leaders sit at one table for weeks and sign an agreement on peace. Each side counts its troops while it signs.
focus_desc.ccp_coalition_programme: A programme for a government of all parties: free speech, elected assemblies and land rents cut, not land seized. Some old comrades frown.
focus_desc.ccp_comintern_line: The delegates back from Moscow carry Stalin's blessing. The party will follow the International's advice and keep its eyes on the world front.
focus_desc.ccp_commanders_council: The army commanders meet without the political commissars. They talk of order, discipline and a state that soldiers run.
focus_desc.ccp_commanders_take_power: The council declares the party's leaders deposed and rules by the army's word. The party's loyalists will not give up without a war.
focus_desc.ccp_constituent_assembly: An assembly elected by all writes the constitution, and the party becomes one party among several. Not everyone in the party accepts it.
focus_desc.ccp_cooperatives: Village co-operatives buy salt and cloth together and sell grain together. The traders lose their margins; the peasants keep them.
focus_desc.ccp_counteroffensive: The enemy is stretched thin across the Pacific. Our armies come out of the hills and take the towns.
focus_desc.ccp_crack_troops: Too many mouths in offices, too few in the field. Staffs are cut, and the cadres go to the villages and the front.
focus_desc.ccp_dixie_mission: An American army mission flies to Yan'an to see what the Communists can do. They see a lot and promise little.
focus_desc.ccp_eighth_route: Reorganise the main Red Army as the Eighth Route Army and move into the enemy's rear in North China.
focus_desc.ccp_eighth_route_army: The Red Army takes the national army's name and caps. Three divisions march toward the front in Shanxi under their own commanders.
focus_desc.ccp_engineer_companies: Men who blow bridges for the guerrillas learn to build them for the field armies.
focus_desc.ccp_field_armies: Combine the scattered guerrilla units into regular field armies with artillery.
focus_desc.ccp_field_armies_formed: The regiments become columns, the columns become field armies. The guerrilla war is turning into a regular war.
focus_desc.ccp_first_tank_unit: A few Japanese tanks dragged out of a Manchurian depot are repaired and crewed. The army has armour of its own.
focus_desc.ccp_fourth_front_loyalty: The largest of the Red armies obeys its own commanders first. Its men are told the party's quarrels cost them half their comrades.
focus_desc.ccp_go_north: Manchuria has the industry, the coal and the Soviet border. Whoever holds it first will hold China's future.
focus_desc.ccp_great_production: The blockade leaves only one answer: soldiers, cadres and students farm, spin and build for themselves.
focus_desc.ccp_guerrilla_war: Small units in the mountains, behind the enemy, under the party's own command. We do not throw our few divisions into set battles.
focus_desc.ccp_hexi_corridor: The road to the Soviet border runs through the Ma family's lands. The commanders mean to break through by force this time.
focus_desc.ccp_huangyadong_arsenal: In a ravine of the Taihang mountains the party builds its largest arsenal, and its own rifle.
focus_desc.ccp_hui_detachment: Muslim villagers of the Hebei plain form their own cavalry detachment under a Hui commander. They ride for the bases.
focus_desc.ccp_hundred_regiments: Strike the railways, roads and blockhouses of North China at once to cut Japanese communications.
focus_desc.ccp_hundred_regiments_offensive: Over a hundred regiments strike the railways, bridges and blockhouses of North China at once. The enemy will remember it.
focus_desc.ccp_independent: Refuse to work with the Nationalists and continue the armed struggle alone.
focus_desc.ccp_into_the_mountains: Behind the Japanese spearheads lie mountains, villages and no government. The army goes in and stays.
focus_desc.ccp_journalists_visit: Foreign correspondents are let through the blockade to Yan'an. Their reports do not match what Chongqing tells them.
focus_desc.ccp_kangda: Officers study in caves and fields: tactics in the morning, politics in the afternoon, the front after six months.
focus_desc.ccp_korean_volunteers: Korean exiles who fled to the Taihang mountains fight beside us against the same empire.
focus_desc.ccp_land_to_the_tiller: The land is taken from the landlords and divided among the peasants now, not after the war. The villages rise; the gentry flee to the Nationalists.
focus_desc.ccp_league_talks: Professors, small parties and liberal gentry want a constitution more than a revolution. They listen when we speak of elections.
focus_desc.ccp_liaison_offices: Offices of the Eighth Route Army open in the great cities of free China. They buy medicine, recruit students and listen.
focus_desc.ccp_main_force_regiments: The best men of the guerrilla bands are gathered into regular regiments that can fight in the open when the time comes.
focus_desc.ccp_mao_line: The man who was right at Zunyi leads. The revolution will be made from the villages, by Chinese judgement, not by instructions from abroad.
focus_desc.ccp_mass_line: Send cadres among the peasants to gather their views and turn them into policy.
focus_desc.ccp_militia: Organise militia in every village for sentry duty and supply, and as a reserve for the regular units.
focus_desc.ccp_militia_everywhere: The militia guards the harvest, carries the wounded and fills the regular army's gaps. No village is undefended.
focus_desc.ccp_mine_warfare: Stone mines, jar mines and mines made from shells the enemy fired: every road into the bases becomes dangerous.
focus_desc.ccp_mobile_war: Guerrillas cannot beat an army. We concentrate our divisions, strike columns on the march and fight battles we can win.
focus_desc.ccp_moscow_link: Restore contact with the Comintern and the Soviet Union and ask for aid.
focus_desc.ccp_moscow_men_rule: The International's people sit at the head of the table. If the country has strayed from the party, they bring it back.
focus_desc.ccp_nanniwan: A brigade is sent into an empty valley with spades instead of rifles. In three years the wasteland feeds the brigade and more.
focus_desc.ccp_natural_sciences: Chemists and engineers who left the coastal universities teach in caves and work on glass, soap, paper and explosives.
focus_desc.ccp_new_china: Prepare for the war to bring down the National Government and take power over the whole country.
focus_desc.ccp_new_china_daily: A legal Communist newspaper prints in the wartime capital. The censors cut it; the readers fill in the gaps.
focus_desc.ccp_new_fourth: Gather the guerrilla units left in the south into the New Fourth Army for Central China.
focus_desc.ccp_new_fourth_army: The guerrillas left behind in the south come down from the hills and form a new army between the Yangtze and the Huai.
focus_desc.ccp_no_truce: Chiang hunted us for ten years and will do so again. The revolution cannot hand its army to its executioner.
focus_desc.ccp_northeast: As Japanese rule in Manchuria falters, send units into the Northeast.
focus_desc.ccp_northeastern_army_pact: Front lines go quiet, prisoners go home, and officers of the two armies drink together. The Manchurian exiles want to fight Japan.
focus_desc.ccp_northwest_council: The generals and the party sit in one council and govern the northwest together, against Japan and apart from Nanking.
focus_desc.ccp_northwest_government: The council becomes a government led by the generals. The party is its partner, not its master, and its hardliners will fight that.
focus_desc.ccp_northwestern_army: The Shaanxi general's Seventeenth Route Army has guns and no love for Nanking. It shares both with us.
focus_desc.ccp_party_commands_the_gun: Whatever happened in between, the army answers to the party. If others hold the government, the party takes it back.
focus_desc.ccp_party_congress: Hold a party congress to settle the leadership and the line, and plan for after the war.
focus_desc.ccp_party_school: Open a party school in Yan'an to teach cadres theory and administration.
focus_desc.ccp_peoples_war: Instead of pitched battles, cut the enemy's supply and communications with movement, raids and ambushes.
focus_desc.ccp_pingxing_pass: A division waits on the ridges above a narrow pass and destroys a Japanese supply column. The first victory of the war is ours.
focus_desc.ccp_prisoners_school: Captured Japanese soldiers are taught, not shot. Some of them go back across the lines to talk to their comrades.
focus_desc.ccp_production: Under blockade, let units and offices farm and run workshops to supply themselves.
focus_desc.ccp_protracted_war: Japan cannot win quickly and China cannot lose quickly. Defence, stalemate, then the counter-offensive: the war will be long, and we must last.
focus_desc.ccp_radio_codes: Hand-built transmitters link Yan'an to every base. The codes are changed often and the operators trained hard.
focus_desc.ccp_radio_to_moscow: After years of silence on the march, the party talks to the International again, and the International talks back.
focus_desc.ccp_rear_intel: Bind the contacts in occupied territory into an intelligence network that watches the Japanese army.
focus_desc.ccp_rectification: Every cadre writes his self-criticism and hears the group's verdict. Old factions are broken up, and the party learns to think with one head.
focus_desc.ccp_red_army_strikes: No more waiting to be encircled. The army breaks out where the enemy is weakest and lives on what it takes.
focus_desc.ccp_red_star: An American journalist spends months with the Red Army and writes what he saw. The outside world learns we exist.
focus_desc.ccp_regional_forces: Between the village militia and the main force stand the county and district companies, who know every path.
focus_desc.ccp_rent_reduction: Make landlords lower rents and interest to win the support of the peasants.
focus_desc.ccp_rent_reduction_policy: Landlords keep their land but must cut rents and debts. Tenants gain bread, and the landlords stay in the front.
focus_desc.ccp_rescue_campaign: The security men claim the Nationalists have planted agents among the students who came to Yan'an. Confessions pile up, and so does fear.
focus_desc.ccp_salt_lakes: The salt lakes on the Inner Mongolian edge are the Border Region's best export. Caravans carry it out and bring cloth back.
focus_desc.ccp_second_centre: Zhang Guotao once set up his own central committee and called Mao's a fraud. Some of his officers never accepted its dissolution.
focus_desc.ccp_second_united_front: Ten years after the first front ended in massacre, the two parties agree again to fight one enemy. Neither forgets the last time.
focus_desc.ccp_self_defence_corps: Every able man and woman of a village joins the self-defence corps: sentries, stretcher-bearers, messengers and reserves.
focus_desc.ccp_self_reliance_line: Nobody is coming to help. What we eat, wear and fire, we make or take ourselves.
