focus_desc.esr_european_bet: The same powers that arm the rising threaten the democracies. When war comes, Spain will not be alone.
focus_desc.esr_farewell_brigades: The foreign volunteers are withdrawn under international supervision, in the hope that London and Paris will press the other side to do the same.
focus_desc.esr_fifth_column: Agents in the ministries and the staffs wait for the signal to rise behind the front.
focus_desc.esr_fifth_column_rises: The hidden network seizes buildings and barracks in the Republic's own capital.
focus_desc.esr_free_communes: Spain becomes a federation of free communes and unions. No state, the anarchists say; the militias say it must still be defended.
focus_desc.esr_french_frontier: Across the Pyrenees lies a friendly people and a cautious government. Ask Paris to open the border.
focus_desc.esr_front_governs: The left won the election by a narrow margin. Govern firmly enough to hold the coalition together and keep the street from the barracks.
focus_desc.esr_general_staff: A professional chief of staff plans the great offensives instead of the parties and the committees.
focus_desc.esr_gold_in_mexico: What is left of the Republic's money keeps the exiles, their newspapers and their organisation alive.
focus_desc.esr_gold_to_moscow: The Bank of Spain's reserve is shipped from Cartagena to the Soviet Union. It buys tanks, aircraft and advisers, and a debt that is never only money.
focus_desc.esr_gold_to_paris: The gold goes to the Bank of France instead, to buy whatever the market will sell past the embargo. Less comes, but no one master comes with it.
focus_desc.esr_government_in_exile: The Republic still has ministers, diplomats and a legal claim. From abroad it asks the world not to recognise the victors.
focus_desc.esr_guerrilla_corps: Special units cross the lines to blow up bridges and trains and come back with prisoners and news.
focus_desc.esr_guerrilla_networks: Men who would not surrender hold out in the mountains, fed by villages and messengers from across the border.
focus_desc.esr_herrera_laboratory: The air force's engineer and inventor of a pressure suit takes charge of aeronautical research.
focus_desc.esr_hidden_falange: In the Republic's cities the Falange survives underground, in embassies, cellars and offices.
focus_desc.esr_hispano_suiza: The car and aero-engine works of Barcelona build engines, armoured cars and aircraft parts for the war.
focus_desc.esr_iberian_federation: The old republican dream of a federation of the peninsula's peoples, now that Lisbon's dictatorship stands alone.
focus_desc.esr_iberian_republic: Spain and Portugal under one federal constitution, each people with its own parliament.
focus_desc.esr_industrial_plan: New factories in the regions that had none: the Republic's plan to end Spain's backwardness.
focus_desc.esr_katiuskas: Fast twin-engined bombers that the enemy's fighters can hardly catch.
focus_desc.esr_keep_brigades: The volunteers came to fight and they are the best shock troops the Republic has. Diplomacy can wait.
focus_desc.esr_kirovabad: Hundreds of young Spaniards are sent to the Soviet Union to learn to fly at a school in the Caucasus.
focus_desc.esr_league_appeal: The foreign minister denounces the foreign intervention in Geneva and asks for the right to buy arms.
focus_desc.esr_levante_railways: The lines between Valencia, Cartagena and the front are doubled and protected.
focus_desc.esr_libertarian_rising: The unions call a general strike and take the telephone exchanges, the barracks and the ministries. The state will defend itself.
focus_desc.esr_madrid_ring: Belts of trenches, bunkers and barricades make the capital a fortress the enemy can no longer storm.
focus_desc.esr_mexican_friendship: Mexico stood by the Republic from the start and will take in its refugees if the worst comes.
focus_desc.esr_mexican_rifles: Mexico is the one government that sells openly to the Republic. Its rifles and cartridges cross the Atlantic.
focus_desc.esr_moroccan_offer: Promise the Moroccans their freedom and the enemy's best troops may have to go home. Paris will not like it.
focus_desc.esr_naranjero_workshops: Small workshops in the Levante copy foreign submachine guns and turn out rifles from salvaged parts.
focus_desc.esr_new_cortes: The first elections in peacetime return a parliament. The Republic governs by votes again, not by decrees.
focus_desc.esr_nyon_patrols: After ships are sunk by submarines that no one admits to owning, the powers agree to patrol the Mediterranean.
focus_desc.esr_officer_postings: The generals who talk of a rising are sent to the islands and the provinces, and loyal men are given the garrisons that matter.
focus_desc.esr_officers_council: The commanders of the central armies meet in secret. They are sure they can make a better peace between soldiers.
focus_desc.esr_pce_course: The party argues for order, a regular army and victory before revolution, and its ranks swell with officers, peasants and clerks.
focus_desc.esr_pce_takeover: The ministers who resist are pushed out and the party's men take the army and the police. Those who refuse will fight.
focus_desc.esr_peace_army: The wartime brigades become a smaller professional army, loyal to the constitution and not to a party.
focus_desc.esr_peace_party: Socialists, republicans and officers who no longer believe in victory start to speak of an honourable end.
focus_desc.esr_peoples_democracy: A new kind of republic, led by the party and built on the army it created. Its friends are in Moscow.
focus_desc.esr_popular_army: The columns of the parties and unions are merged into mixed brigades under one chain of command, with ranks, uniforms and political commissars.
focus_desc.esr_public_schools: Thousands of new schools and teachers, paid by the state and free of the Church. The Republic's oldest promise.
focus_desc.esr_reconstruction: Bridges, railways and towns ruined by the war are rebuilt by a Republic at peace.
focus_desc.esr_regional_governments: Catalonia keeps its Generalitat and the Basque Country receives its statute at last. Their own armies fight under the Republic's flag.
focus_desc.esr_research_board: The scientists of the Republic's research institutes are put to work on the war's problems.
focus_desc.esr_reserve_army: New divisions are raised from the classes called up and trained behind the lines.
focus_desc.esr_resist_to_win: If the Republic holds long enough, the war in Europe will come and the democracies will have to take its side. Every month gained counts.
focus_desc.esr_restore_order: Patrols, committees and private prisons give way to courts and police. The state takes back the streets the revolution took.
focus_desc.esr_restored_command: Loyal officers return to the bridges and the committees give way to a chain of command.
focus_desc.esr_retreat_to_catalonia: With the capital lost, the government and the army fall back on Catalonia and its frontier with France.
focus_desc.esr_return_over_pyrenees: Veterans of the war cross back into Spain under arms, hoping that the country will rise with them.
focus_desc.esr_reus_chatos: With Soviet drawings and engines, Catalan workshops begin to build the snub-nosed fighter the pilots call the Chato.
focus_desc.esr_revolutionary_militias: The militias elect their delegates and fight for the revolution, not for a general staff. Keep them as they are and trust their fervour.
focus_desc.esr_sailors_committees: The crews refused to join the rising and took the ships from their officers. Now the fleet must be made to fight.
focus_desc.esr_sim_service: One security service for the whole Republic, in the party's hands. Spies are caught, and so are rivals.
focus_desc.esr_soviet_advisers: Soviet officers and specialists sit beside every commander who matters. Their advice is good, and their reports go to Moscow.
focus_desc.esr_soviet_friendship: The Soviet Union is the only great power that helps. Its embassy is the busiest in the capital.
focus_desc.esr_soviet_squadrons: Soviet volunteer pilots fly the new fighters and bombers until Spanish crews can take them over.
focus_desc.esr_state_factories: The war factories are taken under the state's control, with managers, quotas and one plan.
focus_desc.esr_submarine_flotilla: The submarines are repaired and given loyal crews to hunt the enemy's shipping.
focus_desc.esr_syndicalist_state: The new rulers promise one nation, one syndicate and an end to the war.
focus_desc.esr_teruel: In snow and frost the army takes a provincial capital for the first time. Holding it will be harder than taking it.
focus_desc.esr_thirteen_points: The government publishes its war aims: independence, a free vote, an amnesty. A programme for peace that the other side must answer.
focus_desc.esr_trubia_works: The old state gun factory in Asturias casts howitzers and armoured cars for the cut-off north.
focus_desc.esr_unified_command: Every front answers to the war ministry and one general staff. The parties keep their newspapers, not their armies.
focus_desc.esr_unity_government: Republicans, socialists, Communists and even anarchist ministers sit in one cabinet. The war first; the arguments about the revolution can wait.
focus_desc.esr_victorious_republic: The war is won. The Republic must now show that it can govern a ruined country in peace, under its own constitution.
focus_desc.esr_war_industries: Barcelona's metal and textile works are turned to shells, rifles and lorries under one commission of the Catalan government.
focus_desc.esr_war_schools: Most of the officers went over to the rising. Short courses turn sergeants, students and militia leaders into lieutenants.
focus_desc.esr_xyz_line: A deep line of trenches in the hills guards Valencia from the north.
focus_desc.fin_air_force: A few dozen aircraft of a dozen types: the air force needs one plan and one fighter.
focus_desc.fin_aland_plan: The demilitarised islands lie at the mouth of the Gulf of Bothnia. Fortified by Finland and Sweden together, they would close it to any invader.
focus_desc.fin_american_credit: Finland is the one country that keeps paying its war debt to America. Washington remembers, and lends.
focus_desc.fin_anti_tank_arm: Satchel charges, bottles of petrol and courage: infantry learns to stop tanks it cannot outgun.
focus_desc.fin_armoured_ships: Väinämöinen and Ilmarinen carry big guns in small hulls and break ice as they go.
focus_desc.fin_ask_london_paris: Envoys ask what help the great democracies would send if the Isthmus were attacked. The answers are warm and vague.
focus_desc.fin_blenheim_licence: A fast British bomber, built at Tampere, gives the air force a long arm.
focus_desc.fin_blue_black_youth: A youth league marches in uniform and sings of a Finland from the Baltic to the White Sea.
focus_desc.fin_bofors_licences: The Swedish works sell drawings as well as guns. Tampella builds their 37-millimetre anti-tank gun at home.
focus_desc.fin_border_roads: The wilderness along the eastern border has few roads. An army that cannot move there cannot defend it.
focus_desc.fin_brothers_in_arms: Not an ally, a co-belligerent: Finland would fight its own war beside Germany's and sign nothing more.
focus_desc.fin_buy_american_fighters: The US Navy has no use for its Brewsters. In Finnish hands, on skis over the lakes, they may do better.
focus_desc.fin_civil_guard: Bind the volunteer Civil Guard into the mobilisation plans to deepen the reserves.
focus_desc.fin_civil_guard_corps: The Suojeluskunta was born as the White army of 1918. Now its parish companies are the reserve of the nation.
focus_desc.fin_coastal_batteries: The forts of Koivisto and the islands off Helsinki guard both ends of the line from the sea.
focus_desc.fin_coastal_navy: The archipelago is a maze no battleship can enter. A navy built for it needs guns, mines and patience.
focus_desc.fin_concrete_bunkers: Old bunkers from the twenties are cracked and few. New ones need cement the budget has never paid for.
focus_desc.fin_continuation: Germany and the Soviet Union are at war. The time has come to recover the Karelia lost in 1940.
focus_desc.fin_cooperative_finland: Dairies, shops and banks owned by their members reach every parish. The cooperatives tie the farmer and the town worker to the republic.
focus_desc.fin_court_the_guards: A hundred thousand armed volunteers belong to no party. Whoever wins their officers wins the streets.
focus_desc.fin_cross_the_old_border: East Karelia never belonged to Finland, but its villages speak a kindred tongue. Going further makes a defensive war into another kind.
focus_desc.fin_crown_question: In 1918 parliament elected a king who never came. The monarchists of that year are old, but they have not changed their minds.
focus_desc.fin_defence_cabinet: Ministers who answer to the army's needs before the parties' make the budget a war chest.
focus_desc.fin_defence_in_depth: Lose ground slowly, strike the flanks, never let the enemy rest: the lessons of the forest are written down for the whole army.
focus_desc.fin_dem_free_press: Under a government that silenced the parliament, liberal and labour papers still circulate from hand to hand.
focus_desc.fin_dem_legal_front: Lawyers, union men and Agrarian deputies sign one appeal: the constitution of 1919 is still the law of the land.
focus_desc.fin_dem_restore_parliament: The deputies gather again in the house on Mannerheimintie. Those who sent them home will not leave quietly.
focus_desc.fin_east_karelian_rule: Schools, churches and camps follow the army into Olonets and Petrozavodsk. Some villages welcome it, others empty.
focus_desc.fin_end_shell_hunger: Gunners have been told to count every shell. Factories and purchases abroad must fill the stores before they are needed.
focus_desc.fin_evacuate_karelia: Whole parishes load their cattle onto trains and leave their homes before the front reaches them.
focus_desc.fin_fight_on: Ribbentrop wants a promise that Finland will not make peace alone. Giving it ties Finland's fate to Berlin's.
focus_desc.fin_fokker_licence: The Dutch fighter is simple, sturdy and takes skis. The State Aircraft Factory can build it under licence.
focus_desc.fin_forest_war_school: Small units, long marches and fighting without roads: the army trains for the war its terrain allows.
focus_desc.fin_friendship_treaty: Finland promises never to let its soil be used against the Soviet Union; Moscow promises to leave Finland to itself. Both will be tested.
focus_desc.fin_german_trade: Germany buys Finnish timber, pulp and butter, and sells machines. Many officers remember that German Jägers helped win 1918.
focus_desc.fin_granite_obstacles: Rows of granite boulders and barbed wire run between the bunkers. Volunteers from the universities dig all summer.
focus_desc.fin_greater_finland: The dream of the Academic Karelia Society made law: the frontier on the White Sea and the Svir.
focus_desc.fin_green_gold: Forests cover most of the land and pay most of the exports. Every sawmill is a small bank.
focus_desc.fin_guard_the_southern_shore: If Tallinn falls, Helsinki is a day's sail from the enemy. A guarantee says so out loud.
focus_desc.fin_gulf_cooperation: The coastal batteries of Finland and Estonia could cross their fire over the Gulf of Finland and keep the Red Fleet in Kronstadt.
focus_desc.fin_gulf_minefields: Together with the Estonian shore, Finnish mines can close the Gulf of Finland from coast to coast.
focus_desc.fin_guns_for_the_army: The field artillery still fires Russian guns of the Tsar's time. New guns must be bought or made.
focus_desc.fin_heal_the_divide: Whites and Reds still remember the prison camps and the executions. Amnesties, schools and shared work may close the old wound.
focus_desc.fin_home_front: Rationing cards, blackout curtains and women in the factories keep the front supplied.
focus_desc.fin_ikl_new_order: Parties are dissolved into one movement and the guards into the army. The new order must now choose who will lead it.
focus_desc.fin_ikl_rising: At Mäntsälä the guards once took up arms and waited for the country to follow. This time the movement believes it will.
focus_desc.fin_imatra_power: The state's great power station on the Vuoksi lights the south. More turbines mean more factories.
focus_desc.fin_industrial_south: Tampere, Turku and the Helsinki region grow into one industrial belt that could arm the country.
focus_desc.fin_isthmus_survey: Between the gulf and Lake Ladoga lies the only road for a great army. Engineers walk it with maps and measuring chains.
focus_desc.fin_january_engagement: The employers at last recognise the trade unions as their partners at the table. A small paper, a large peace between the classes.
focus_desc.fin_keep_the_pact: The pact with the Soviet Union is on paper. Keeping it in good repair costs little and may buy years.
focus_desc.fin_kindred_estonia: Estonians and Finns speak sister languages and fought each other's wars of independence. Some talk of one state.
focus_desc.fin_kingdom_of_finland: A regency council rules until a king is found. The name on the stamps changes; the frontier does not.
focus_desc.fin_kingdom_proclaimed: The constitution of the republic is set aside in the name of an older plan. The republicans will fight for theirs.
focus_desc.fin_ladoga_line: Everyone expects the blow on the Isthmus. North of the lake, in the forests, there is almost nothing to stop it.
focus_desc.fin_lahti_workshop: The self-taught designer at the state arsenal turns out a twenty-millimetre rifle for the infantry to stop tanks.
focus_desc.fin_lapua_march: Once twelve thousand farmers marched on the capital and the government bent. The movement means to show its strength again.
focus_desc.fin_league_faith: Finland won the Åland dispute at Geneva once. Its foreign ministry still believes that law protects the small.
focus_desc.fin_lease_the_islands: Suursaari and the small islands are rock and lighthouse. Leasing them could satisfy Leningrad's fear without touching the mainland.
focus_desc.fin_lex_kekkonen: The young interior minister wants the Patriotic People's Movement dissolved as a threat to the republic. The courts may not agree.
focus_desc.fin_light_detachments: Ski battalions grouped into light detachments can be sent wherever the enemy comes through the wilderness.
focus_desc.fin_lotta_svard: A hundred thousand women run field kitchens, aircraft watch posts, hospitals and supply depots.
focus_desc.fin_mannerheim_line: Strengthen the concrete bunkers and trench lines across the Karelian Isthmus.
focus_desc.fin_marshal_call: The chairman of the Defence Council warns that the country is not ready. Many would rather trust him than the parties.
focus_desc.fin_marshal_rises: Mannerheim was regent once before. If parliament will not give him the power to prepare, others will give it to him.
focus_desc.fin_mobilisation_plan: Each guard company knows the station where its men will form a battalion. Mobilisation can be done in days.
focus_desc.fin_monarchist_league: Bankers, landowners and old Jäger officers argue that a crown would stand above the quarrels of 1918.
focus_desc.fin_moscow_back_channel: A junior diplomat of the Soviet embassy asks for private talks with a minister. What Moscow wants is not yet said.
focus_desc.fin_moscow_trade_treaty: Paper and timber go east, grain and oil come west. Trade makes a neighbour less eager to quarrel.
focus_desc.fin_motti: Cut road-bound enemy columns in the forest into pieces and surround each one.
focus_desc.fin_motti_doctrine: A road-bound column is cut into pieces, each piece surrounded like a pile of logs and left to freeze.
focus_desc.fin_myrsky: When no one will sell fighters, the factory designs its own, in wood and steel tube, around an American engine.
focus_desc.fin_nine_divisions: On paper the reserves fill nine divisions. Rifles, boots and guns must make the paper true.
focus_desc.fin_nordic_arms_pool: Bofors in Sweden, Tampella and the state arsenals in Finland: one calibre and one drawing for all.
focus_desc.fin_nordic_defence_union: Alone each Nordic state is small. Together they are a power no neighbour can ignore, if only they agree to act together.
focus_desc.fin_nordic_orientation: Parliament has declared that Finland's neutrality stands with the Scandinavian states. It remains to be seen whether Stockholm will stand with Finland.
focus_desc.fin_nordic_talks: Officers of the Nordic armies compare plans quietly. No treaty, but every map now shows the others' roads.
focus_desc.fin_outokumpu_copper: The copper ore of North Karelia feeds a smelter and a new class of engineers.
focus_desc.fin_paper_mills: The mills on the Kymi and at Kuusankoski turn logs into newsprint for half of Europe.
focus_desc.fin_parish_ranges: The guards buy their own rifles and shoot every Sunday. Finland's marksmen are made in the villages.
focus_desc.fin_parvi_tactics: Fighters fly in loose pairs and fours instead of tight vics, and every pilot is taught to shoot from close in.
focus_desc.fin_patriotic_front: The Lapua Movement was banned after its rising, but its people sit in parliament in black shirts and blue ties. They want a stronger state than this one.
focus_desc.fin_petsamo_nickel: A Canadian-British company holds the concession on one of Europe's richest nickel ores. Every great power wants its output.
focus_desc.fin_port_towns: The export harbours need deeper quays and new cranes. In war they will need to build ships too.
focus_desc.fin_presidential_electors: The people choose three hundred electors and the electors choose the president. Svinhufvud's term runs out and the parties count their votes.
focus_desc.fin_red_earth_coalition: The Agrarians and the Social Democrats, the countryside and the workers, could govern together for the first time since the civil war.
focus_desc.fin_refuse_the_bases: Leningrad wants islands in the gulf and a border moved back on the Isthmus. To give way once is to be asked again.
focus_desc.fin_regent_mannerheim: One man answers for the army, the frontier and the state. The parties wait, the fortifications grow.
focus_desc.fin_reparations_industry: Paying for the war in ships, cables and machines forces the country to build a metal industry it never had.
focus_desc.fin_republic_for_all: When the old Reds and the old Whites defend the same constitution, the country has won a war it once fought against itself.
focus_desc.fin_rural_power: Electric lines reach farms that knew only oil lamps. Workshops follow the wires.
focus_desc.fin_salla_railway: A line from Kemijärvi towards Salla would carry men and timber north, and could carry others south.
focus_desc.fin_separate_peace: The war is lost for Germany and may be lost for Finland. Leaving it in time could save the country's independence.
focus_desc.fin_sissi_raids: Long-range patrols strike field kitchens and supply columns far behind the front, then vanish into the forest.
focus_desc.fin_sisu: A word with no translation: stubbornness beyond reason, the will to go on after strength is gone.
focus_desc.fin_ski_jaegers: Every conscript can ski. Battalions that move twenty kilometres a day through snow need no roads at all.
focus_desc.fin_skp_free_prisoners: Antikainen's life sentence made him a hero to the left. Campaigns for amnesty win sympathy far beyond the party.
focus_desc.fin_skp_front_groups: Sports clubs, reading circles and tenants' leagues carry the party's message under other names.
focus_desc.fin_skp_rising: The workers' guards of 1918 were beaten. Their sons believe the next rising will not be.
focus_desc.fin_skp_underground: The Communist Party is banned and its leaders sit in Moscow or in prison. Its cells still meet in the factories of Tampere and Turku.
focus_desc.fin_skp_union_left: In the trade unions the left opposition outvotes Tanner's men in the big branches.
focus_desc.fin_skp_workers_republic: Banks and sawmills pass to the state and the councils. Moscow watches its new neighbour closely.
focus_desc.fin_small_tank_arm: Vickers six-tonners arrive from Britain without their guns. A handful of tanks is still a school for more.
focus_desc.fin_state_aircraft_factory: The factory moves from the shore to Tampere, out of reach of a naval raid, and grows.
focus_desc.fin_state_arsenal: Expand the state rifle and ammunition factories.
focus_desc.fin_state_arsenals: The rifle factory at Jyväskylä, the aircraft factory at Tampere and the shipyards make what a small country can make itself.
focus_desc.fin_stop_at_the_old_border: The lost land is won back; not one step further. London and Washington take note that Finland fights only for its own.
focus_desc.fin_submarine_flotilla: The Turku yard builds boats to German drawings. In the shallow gulf they lay mines as often as they fire torpedoes.
focus_desc.fin_suomi_gun: Aimo Lahti's gun with its drum of seventy rounds turns a ski patrol into a firing line.
focus_desc.fin_swedish_volunteer_corps: Swedish officers promise that if war comes their volunteers will cross the Torne. Plans are made for their arrival.
focus_desc.fin_tampella_guns: The Tampere engineering works learn to make mortars and gun barrels as well as paper machines.
focus_desc.fin_timber_exports: British buyers take sawn timber by the shipload. Good prices, and good friends in the City.
focus_desc.fin_total_defence: Every factory, farm and family is part of the front. The government asks for everything, and gets it.
focus_desc.fin_transit_agreement: German soldiers on leave from Norway ask to travel through Lapland. A railway timetable can become an alliance.
focus_desc.fin_war_booty: Every destroyed column leaves guns, tanks and shells in the snow. The enemy becomes the army's best supplier.
focus_desc.fin_war_industry: The arsenals run three shifts and private works take army orders. Peace production waits.
focus_desc.fin_western_hope: Rather than lean on Berlin, Finland ties its future to the Western democracies, though their armies are far away.
focus_desc.fin_win_back_karelia: Viipuri, the second city, and the shores of Ladoga were Finland's. The army's first aim is to stand on the old frontier again.
focus_desc.fin_wood_gas: A country without oil wells has birch logs. A stove on the back of a lorry keeps it running when the tankers stop.
focus_desc.fin_young_republic: Independence is still young and the state that won it has kept order since. Its institutions must now prove they belong to the whole people.
focus_desc.fra_action_francaise: The royalist movement's papers and students campaign openly for the return of the King.
focus_desc.fra_air_force_plan: A new air plan sets a target of thousands of front-line aircraft and adds the factories and airfields to match.
focus_desc.fra_air_force_unified: The air force at last has a single command that answers to the General Staff, instead of squadrons attached to army corps. Operations become far easier to coordinate.
focus_desc.fra_algeria_settlers: Phosphates, iron ore and wheat are developed on a larger scale, and new roads and railways open up the interior. The settlers get most of the profit.
focus_desc.fra_alpine_troops: Mountain battalions are trained and equipped to fight on the passes facing Italy.
focus_desc.fra_anti_tank_guns: The 25 mm and 47 mm guns are ordered by the thousand and handed out to infantry divisions and to the fortified sectors of the north.
focus_desc.fra_armistice_path: Marshal Pétain asks the Germans for terms. The armistice divides the country into an occupied north and a free south, and the old republic gives way to a new regime at Vichy.
focus_desc.fra_armoured_corps: Heavy tanks are gathered into armoured divisions instead of being spread among the infantry. Colonel Charles de Gaulle, who argued for it, gets a command.
focus_desc.fra_arms_nationalisation: The state takes over the main private arms works, so that weapons are made for the nation rather than for profit.
focus_desc.fra_army_of_africa: The North African corps gets workshops and depots of its own, so that it can fight without waiting for convoys from France.
focus_desc.fra_army_reorganisation: Infantry divisions receive more anti-tank guns and engineers, and new manuals draw on the lessons of recent exercises.
focus_desc.fra_arsenal_dispersal_2: Another round of factories moves from the north-eastern border to the Loire and the south-west, away from the reach of the German bombers.
focus_desc.fra_aviation_reorganisation: Scattered aircraft firms are merged into large national companies by region, with new plants and modern tooling.
focus_desc.fra_bloch_bombers: Amiot and Lioré et Olivier bombers replace the lumbering types of the 1920s. The factories nationalised in 1936 finally deliver.
focus_desc.fra_bomber_force: Light and medium bomber squadrons are formed to strike enemy columns and supply lines behind the front.
focus_desc.fra_cagoule: A secret committee stockpiles arms and plans a seizure of power, with friends on the army staff.
focus_desc.fra_central_africa_rally: Chad, Cameroon and the Congo declare for Free France. Their rubber and cotton are modest, but Brazzaville gives de Gaulle a territory to rule.
focus_desc.fra_channel_flotilla: French and British staffs agree to share the watch on the Channel and to open each other's ports to their ships in case of war.
focus_desc.fra_char_b: The army puts its faith in the Char B1 bis: a heavily armoured tank with a hull gun and a turret gun, nearly impervious to anything the Germans field. It is slow, thirsty and expensive.
focus_desc.fra_collaboration_policy: At Montoire the Marshal shakes hands with the Führer and speaks of collaboration. Vichy hopes for easier terms; Berlin hopes for French workers, goods and bases.
focus_desc.fra_colonial_divisions: Recruiting in North and West Africa is widened, and the new regiments are formed into full divisions.
focus_desc.fra_colonial_minerals: Rubber plantations in Indochina and mines across the colonies are expanded to keep the factories at home supplied.
focus_desc.fra_colonial_rubber: Plantations in Cochinchina and bauxite from the Midi are bought under state contracts for the new aircraft and tyre factories.
focus_desc.fra_constitution_reform: The cabinet proposes to revise the constitutional laws: a stronger executive and elections put off while the country is in danger.
focus_desc.fra_count_of_paris: The pretender sends manifestos from exile and receives the generals and deputies who come to see him.
focus_desc.fra_early_rearmament: Arms orders come before consumer spending, and the factories turn to war work years earlier than planned.
focus_desc.fra_eastern_alliances: France confirms its promises to Prague and Warsaw and seeks a real military understanding with Moscow.
focus_desc.fra_economic_recovery: Decree laws lengthen the working week and loosen the controls of 1936 to bring capital home and restart production.
focus_desc.fra_empire_defence: Garrisons in Africa and Asia receive new forts and fresh recruits raised in the colonies themselves.
focus_desc.fra_factory_occupations: Workers occupy the factories, as in June 1936, and this time they refuse to leave when the agreements are signed.
focus_desc.fra_fast_battleships: Fast battleships with heavy guns are laid down to answer the new German and Italian ships.
focus_desc.fra_fighter_dewoitine: The D.520 is the nearest French match to the Bf 109. It is ordered late and delivered slowly, but it shows what the factories can do when the government finally gives clear orders.
focus_desc.fra_forty_hours_relief: Under pressure to arm, the government allows overtime in the war factories. Output climbs, and the unions grumble.
focus_desc.fra_fourth_republic: The provisional government gives women the vote, writes a new constitution and submits it to the people. The Third Republic, which fell in 1940, is not restored, and where Vichy's men still hold out it comes to fighting.
focus_desc.fra_free_french_forces: Soldiers who reached Britain from Dunkirk and Norway, and volunteers from the colonies, are formed into new divisions.
focus_desc.fra_free_french_navy: Sailors who refused to follow Vichy gather under the cross of Lorraine. Their destroyers and corvettes escort the convoys of the Atlantic beside the Royal Navy.
focus_desc.fra_french_union: The new constitution replaces the empire with a union of France and its overseas territories, with seats in the Assembly for the colonies. Whether the colonies are satisfied is another matter.
focus_desc.fra_front_commune: Communists, Socialists and the unions agree on a common programme. Moscow takes note, and the right begins to speak of a red menace.
focus_desc.fra_gamelin_plan: General Gamelin proposes that the best French and British armies swing forward into Belgium as soon as the Germans attack, to meet them on the line of the River Dyle. The plan is bold, and it leaves the reserve thin.
focus_desc.fra_giraud_de_gaulle: After months of rivalry, the generals who lead the French in Algiers and in London agree to share the chairmanship of one committee. Washington and London finally deal with a single French authority.
focus_desc.fra_heavy_water: Military intelligence borrows Norway's whole stock of heavy water and brings it to the physicists of the Collège de France.
focus_desc.fra_heavy_water_2: Joliot-Curie's laboratory secures more heavy water and uranium from Norway and the Belgian Congo, and keeps its research in step with the best in the world.
focus_desc.fra_indochina_decolonise: Paris offers the peoples of Indochina a share in their own government. Stability improves in the colonies, and the cost of the garrison falls.
focus_desc.fra_indochina_defence: Coastal batteries, border posts and an airfield strengthen the colony against an attack from the north or the sea.
focus_desc.fra_indochina_hold: The governor-general asks for more garrisons and fortifications on the frontier. Tonkin and the Mekong delta are turned into strongpoints.
focus_desc.fra_industrial_survey: Engineers list every plant, machine and skilled worker that could be turned to defence work.
focus_desc.fra_industrial_unions: Unions and employers sign a pact on arbitration and production. For a short while, the factory floor is calmer than it has been since the strikes.
focus_desc.fra_june_appeal: From a London studio, General Charles de Gaulle tells the French that the war is not lost and calls on them to fight on.
focus_desc.fra_latin_bloc: Paris turns to Rome, Burgos and Lisbon for a bloc of Latin states standing between Germany and the Soviet Union.
focus_desc.fra_leagues_ban: The government bans the armed leagues of the right, including the Croix-de-Feu. Order in the streets improves, and the right accuses it of attacking liberty.
focus_desc.fra_leagues_in_government: Leaders of the right-wing leagues are given ministries, and the left warns that the Republic itself is now at stake.
focus_desc.fra_leagues_united: The Croix-de-Feu, the Francistes and the other leagues agree on one leader and one programme.
focus_desc.fra_leclerc_division: Colonel Leclerc marches his column across the Sahara from Lake Chad to Kufra. The force he later builds in North Africa becomes the 2nd Armoured Division.
focus_desc.fra_levant_bases: Harbours in Syria and Lebanon are deepened and their airfields enlarged to guard the sea lanes of the eastern Mediterranean.
focus_desc.fra_levant_front: Free French and British columns march into Syria and Lebanon, where Vichy troops guard the mandate. A short, bitter fight is the first campaign of Free France.
focus_desc.fra_liberation_government: Free France becomes the Provisional Government of the French Republic, ready to take charge of the liberated country.
focus_desc.fra_liberation_of_paris: The police strike, barricades rise, and the 2nd Armoured Division enters the capital on the heels of the insurgents. The Germans surrender the city without destroying it.
focus_desc.fra_little_entente: Paris tries to hold Czechoslovakia, Yugoslavia and Romania together, with loans and arms orders, against the pull of Berlin and Rome.
focus_desc.fra_maghreb_loyalty: Promises of schools, land and recognition for veterans draw many more Algerian, Moroccan and Tunisian volunteers to the colours.
focus_desc.fra_maginot_extension: Concrete casemates and anti-tank obstacles are carried along the Belgian frontier towards the sea.
focus_desc.fra_maquis: Young men who flee the compulsory labour service hide in the hills and forests. Armed and supplied by air drops, they cut rails, ambush convoys and wait for the day of landing.
focus_desc.fra_march_on_paris: As on 6 February 1934 the leagues march on the Chamber, but this time they take it. The Republic's defenders take up arms, and France goes to civil war.
focus_desc.fra_matignon_accords: In the Hôtel Matignon, employers and unions settle the great strikes: wage rises, paid holidays and the forty-hour week. Factories reopen, but costs rise.
focus_desc.fra_med_squadron: Cruisers and destroyers are assigned to the new base at Mers-el-Kébir. Together with the British at Gibraltar, they can close the western Mediterranean.
focus_desc.fra_mers_el_kebir_base: A deep-water base is built near Oran to shelter the battle squadron on the African shore.
focus_desc.fra_ministry_of_armament: A single ministry takes charge of all arms production, from raw materials to the finished shell.
focus_desc.fra_mobile_reserve: Rather than pour more concrete, the army keeps motorised reserves behind the front to strike wherever the enemy breaks through.
focus_desc.fra_mobilisation_readiness: Call-up lists, depots and railway timetables are brought up to date so that the reserves can be called at short notice.
focus_desc.fra_modern_fighters: Designers are pressed to bring faster monoplane fighters from prototype to squadron service.
focus_desc.fra_motorised_divisions: Several infantry divisions trade their horses for lorries so that they can keep pace with the tanks.
focus_desc.fra_national_council: Jean Moulin brings the movements of the north and south, the unions and the political parties together in one council that recognises General de Gaulle as its leader.
focus_desc.fra_national_revolution: The new regime promises a moral renewal of France: land, craft guilds and the family above parties and unions. Many old republicans are dismissed from office.
focus_desc.fra_national_union: Instead of a left-wing coalition, Paul Reynaud gathers the centre and the moderate right around rearmament and a firm foreign policy.
focus_desc.fra_neutral_france: France leaves its old alliances and declares that it will defend its own soil and empire and nothing more.
focus_desc.fra_neutral_vichy: Vichy keeps its fleet in port and its colonies under its own flag, and refuses to commit to either side. Washington keeps an embassy open; London does not trust it.
focus_desc.fra_new_commune: Paris rises as it did in 1871 and proclaims a workers' republic. The government withdraws to the provinces, and France goes to civil war.
focus_desc.fra_no_munich: The cabinet decides that it will not hand Czechoslovak territory to Germany, whatever London chooses.
focus_desc.fra_non_intervention: Paris proposes that no power send arms to either side in Spain, keeping London close and France out of the war.
focus_desc.fra_north_africa_move: The ministers board ships for Algiers. From the other side of the Mediterranean, with the fleet and the empire behind them, they intend to keep France in the war.
focus_desc.fra_northern_industry: The coal and steel of the mines and mills of the Nord and Lorraine go first to military contracts.
focus_desc.fra_paratrooper_fr: Small groups of volunteers train to jump from transport aircraft. The idea is borrowed from the Soviet exercises, and the army is not sure what to do with it.
focus_desc.fra_polish_alliance_renew: Marshal Rydz-Śmigły visits Paris. France renews its alliance and promises credits for Polish arms, in return for pledges of mobilisation in case of war.
focus_desc.fra_popular_front: The left-wing alliance that won the election forms a cabinet and ends the wave of strikes through talks between employers and unions.
focus_desc.fra_popular_front_spain: Blum cannot bring himself to abandon the sister republic. Rifles and aircraft cross the Pyrenees in secret, and London warns that this may spread the war.
focus_desc.fra_radar_france: French engineers, working on short waves and decimetre tubes, build their first sets for the coast and the fleet.
focus_desc.fra_radio_everywhere: Most French tanks have no radio and talk with flags. A crash programme fits sets to every command vehicle and trains crews to fight as formations.
focus_desc.fra_rally_the_empire: Envoys of Free France fly to Africa to win over governors and garrisons.
focus_desc.fra_rapid_mobilisation: Reserve rolls are rewritten and the call-up tables simplified, so that the reservists can reach their depots within days instead of weeks.
focus_desc.fra_rearmament_plan: A programme of billions of francs spread over four years pays for new tanks, guns and fortifications.
focus_desc.fra_red_belt: The working suburbs around Paris elect communist mayors and become the party's strongholds.
focus_desc.fra_redoubt_breton: Rather than ask for terms, the government decides to hold a last redoubt in Brittany and keep fighting from the sea. Every port and every cliff road is turned into a strongpoint.
focus_desc.fra_research_centre: State laboratories are brought together under one national centre that hands out funds and sets research priorities.
focus_desc.fra_resistance_council: The resistance movements, parties and unions of occupied France unite in one council that recognises London.
focus_desc.fra_resistance_sabotage: Before the landings, the resistance receives the order to cut every rail and telephone line behind the German front. Thousands of acts of sabotage slow the reserves.
focus_desc.fra_royal_restoration: The royalists proclaim the monarchy and call the pretender home. The Republic will not give way, and France goes to civil war.
focus_desc.fra_royalist_officers: Officers from the old families promise their regiments to the restoration.
focus_desc.fra_science_council: A council of scientists and ministers plans the state laboratories' work as one programme and funds a second line of research.
focus_desc.fra_somua_light: Cavalry officers want a fast tank with a good gun and cast armour. The S35 is among the best tanks in Europe in 1940, if it is used in mass and with radios.
focus_desc.fra_southwest_dispersal: Factories within reach of German bombers move to Toulouse, Bordeaux and the valleys of the southwest.
focus_desc.fra_strong_executive: Weary of short-lived cabinets, the government asks for the power to rule by decree and sets a deadlocked parliament aside.
focus_desc.fra_strong_state_path: Decree powers, a stronger president and fewer debates in parliament. Supporters call it efficiency and opponents call it the end of the republic.
focus_desc.fra_submarine_fleet: Large submarines able to cross oceans are ordered to strike enemy sea lanes in the Atlantic and the Mediterranean.
focus_desc.fra_syria_treaty: Negotiators draft a treaty that would end the mandate in return for bases. The Assembly in Paris is slow to ratify it, but the talks calm the country.
focus_desc.fra_tank_programme: Firm orders and a delivery schedule let the makers of heavy and cavalry tanks build in larger batches.
focus_desc.fra_tunisia_front: Against a possible Italian advance from Libya, engineers fortify the Tunisian frontier with concrete positions, mines and anti-tank ditches.
focus_desc.fra_veterans_columns: Leagues of old soldiers parade through Paris in their thousands, and the police no longer stop them.
focus_desc.fra_vichy_state: The National Assembly at Vichy hands full powers to the Marshal. The slogan "Liberty, Equality, Fraternity" is replaced by "Work, Family, Fatherland".
focus_desc.fra_war_government: With German troops at the frontier, the parties set their quarrels aside and serve together in one wartime cabinet.
focus_desc.fra_weygand_reorg: With the front in crisis, General Weygand takes over the supreme command. He tries to knit the broken armies into a hedgehog line along the Somme and the Aisne.
focus_desc.fra_workers_militia: Party militias drill in the suburbs. Some soldiers bring their rifles with them.
focus_desc.gbr_air_training_plan: Tens of thousands of pilots and aircrew from across the Commonwealth learn to fly under Canada's wide skies.
focus_desc.gbr_airborne_division: Parachute battalions and glider infantry are raised into an airborne division.
focus_desc.gbr_aircraft_production: New plants roll out Hurricane and Spitfire fighters in growing numbers.
focus_desc.gbr_appeasement: To spare Europe another great war, London meets some German and Italian demands at the conference table and buys time to rearm.
focus_desc.gbr_arctic_convoys: Convoys run the gauntlet past Norway to Murmansk, carrying tanks and aircraft to the Soviet front.
focus_desc.gbr_area_bombing: Bomber Command turns to night raids on enemy cities and industry in a long strategic offensive.
focus_desc.gbr_armoured_division: Tank brigades and motorised infantry are combined into armoured divisions able to fight on their own.
focus_desc.gbr_army_command_2: Aged commanders make way for younger field leaders such as Montgomery and Alexander.
focus_desc.gbr_asdic_escort: Sonar-equipped escort groups hunt the U-boats rather than merely shadow the convoys.
focus_desc.gbr_atlantic_bridge: Closer ties with the United States open the way to borrowing American weapons and ships.
focus_desc.gbr_aus_annex: The Commonwealth is annexed to the Crown. Its states become provinces of the realm, its divisions and warships join the home forces, and its wool and wheat are counted in London.
focus_desc.gbr_aus_governor: A governor with wide reserve powers is sent out from London. The Commonwealth cabinet is told that the Palace will decide which of its measures stand.
focus_desc.gbr_aus_parliament: The federal and state houses are adjourned together. Elections are put off for the duration of the emergency, and the governor signs the budget alone.
focus_desc.gbr_battleship_class: Five modern battleships are rushed to completion to meet the German and Italian fleets in a decisive action.
focus_desc.gbr_bef: The force meant for the Continent is reorganised on new lines and its officer training overhauled.
focus_desc.gbr_berlin_accord: The integrated Empire and the Reich agree to leave each other's spheres alone. London keeps the seas and the colonies, Berlin keeps the continent, and each promises not to cross the line.
focus_desc.gbr_beveridge: Sir William Beveridge sketches a cradle-to-grave welfare state to give the war a purpose beyond victory.
focus_desc.gbr_bevin_boys: Ernest Bevin steers workers into mines and arms plants wherever the war needs them.
focus_desc.gbr_bletchley: Mathematicians and chess masters gather in a country house to break the enemy's ciphers.
focus_desc.gbr_bomber_command: Long-range bomber squadrons come under one command, ready to strike the enemy's industrial districts.
focus_desc.gbr_british_soviet: The strike committees declare themselves the government of the working class. Whitehall calls out the army, and Britain goes to civil war.
focus_desc.gbr_burma_campaign: Divisions in Assam and Burma learn to fight, live and supply themselves in the jungle.
focus_desc.gbr_burma_road: Trucks wind through the hills of Burma to carry British supplies to Chongqing.
focus_desc.gbr_can_annex: The Dominion of Canada is annexed to the Crown. Its provinces, its army and its factories pass to the realm in a single proclamation, and the border south of it is guarded with new care.
focus_desc.gbr_can_governor: A governor-general with the Crown's full confidence is sent to Ottawa. The ministers are reminded that the Statute of Westminster was a favour and not a right.
focus_desc.gbr_can_parliament: The House of Commons at Ottawa is prorogued without a date. Provincial premiers are summoned to the capital and told how things will be done.
focus_desc.gbr_canada_lend: Canada ships steel, munitions and food to Britain without asking for payment.
focus_desc.gbr_carriers: New carriers with armoured flight decks are planned and laid down.
focus_desc.gbr_chamberlain_remain: The Prime Minister keeps his seat and his methods, steady but no longer trusted to win.
focus_desc.gbr_churchill_cabinet: Winston Churchill forms a government of all talents and promises nothing but blood, toil, tears and sweat.
focus_desc.gbr_clyde: The yards on Glasgow's River Clyde fill up with warship orders again.
focus_desc.gbr_coalition_domestic: Labour and Liberal ministers sit beside the Conservatives, and party strife is set aside for the duration.
focus_desc.gbr_collective_security: In the spirit of the League, Britain will stand with any victim of aggression and is willing to work even with Moscow.
focus_desc.gbr_colonial_troops: African and Asian colonies raise battalions to serve beside the regular army.
focus_desc.gbr_combined_ops: Lord Louis Mountbatten's headquarters unites the three services to plan raids and landings.
focus_desc.gbr_commandos: Small raiding forces for enemy coasts and the first parachute troops are trained.
focus_desc.gbr_commonwealth_air: Flying schools across Canada, Australia and Rhodesia multiply, turning out crews faster than the front consumes them.
focus_desc.gbr_convoy_system: Merchant ships will sail in escorted groups, and the system is prepared before the first shot.
focus_desc.gbr_county_lords: Lords lieutenant and landowners open their estates to the cause and lend their tenants, their horses and their names. The shires begin to answer to the Palace.
focus_desc.gbr_crown_and_cabinet: Under the new King, Palace and government speak with one voice again and win back the confidence the abdication shook.
focus_desc.gbr_crown_loyalists: Patriotic leagues of veterans and gentry swear to stand by the King, whatever Parliament says.
focus_desc.gbr_crown_movement: Friends of the King in the press and the Commons rally to him against the cabinet. They want the Crown, not the parties, to lead.
focus_desc.gbr_crown_order: A council of the King's own appointees takes over the work of the cabinet. Orders now flow from one table, and the departments learn to expect them.
focus_desc.gbr_cruiser_tank: Fast cruiser tanks like the Crusader are built to exploit a breakthrough and strike deep into the enemy rear.
focus_desc.gbr_defence_white_paper: The 1936 Defence White Paper admits how far the three services have fallen behind and lays out a rearmament budget for the years ahead.
focus_desc.gbr_desert_rats: Seasoned units of the Western Desert Force become the spearhead of the army.
focus_desc.gbr_desert_training: Units in Egypt's Western Desert practise movement, supply and navigation on open sand.
focus_desc.gbr_destroyer_deal: Fifty old American destroyers are traded for leases on British bases in the Atlantic.
focus_desc.gbr_dominion_call: Canada, Australia, New Zealand, South Africa and India send men and open their factories to the Empire's war.
focus_desc.gbr_emergency_decree: The Crown claims its old right to act in an emergency. Orders in council now cover banks, prices and public meetings, and each one is called temporary.
focus_desc.gbr_emergency_powers: Parliament hands the government sweeping control of labour, property and industry.
focus_desc.gbr_empire_arsenal: Orders go out to every works from Montreal to Bombay. The forges of the Empire are tied to a single plan, and the arms that come out of them are counted in the thousands.
focus_desc.gbr_empire_resources: Malayan rubber and mines across the Empire are tied into the home war economy.
focus_desc.gbr_empire_stand: With the Dominions made one with the Crown, London turns to face the Reich as the head of a single realm. War aims are drawn up and the whole Empire is told to be ready.
focus_desc.gbr_escort_carriers: Merchant hulls are converted into small carriers to close the mid-Atlantic air gap.
focus_desc.gbr_fighter_command: Fighter Command takes charge of home air defence and directs its squadrons from the ground.
focus_desc.gbr_fleet_air_arm: The Navy takes its shipborne aircraft back from the RAF and runs them itself.
focus_desc.gbr_fuel_pipeline: Pipes laid across the Channel and through the ports keep an advancing army fuelled.
focus_desc.gbr_general_strike: The unions are called out again, as in 1926, but this time the strike committees do not go back.
focus_desc.gbr_guarantees: Britain pledges to defend the countries Germany is likely to threaten next. An aggressor must now reckon with war against Britain.
focus_desc.gbr_guards_regiments: The Guards and some cavalry regiments let it be known that they serve the King in person.
focus_desc.gbr_home_fleet: New ships join the Home Fleet, which guards the North Sea from Scapa Flow.
focus_desc.gbr_hunger_marches: Unemployed men from the north march on London. Each march leaves new branches of the movement behind it.
focus_desc.gbr_imperial_conference: The Dominion prime ministers meet in London to settle the Empire's trade and defence together.
focus_desc.gbr_imperial_defence_council: The Dominions sign a joint defence plan to make arms together and enlarge their own forces.
focus_desc.gbr_imperial_federation: A council of equals binds the Commonwealth into a single strategic whole, at the price of London's sole command.
focus_desc.gbr_imperial_levy: The Crown's subjects overseas are called to the colours under one law. Men from the farms of the south and the villages of the east fill the depots.
focus_desc.gbr_imperial_preference: Low tariffs on trade inside the Empire bind the industries of Britain and the Dominions together.
focus_desc.gbr_imperial_unity: The Crown declares that one throne means one government. The Dominions are told to prepare for a closer union, and the Colonial Office draws up the order in which it will come.
focus_desc.gbr_imperial_war_cabinet: Dominion premiers sit in London and share in the great decisions of the war.
focus_desc.gbr_india_defence: The Indian Army is modernised, and Indian factories begin making its weapons.
focus_desc.gbr_india_hold: The Viceroy keeps order by force and the Indian Army grows under direct British command.
focus_desc.gbr_india_reform: Sir Stafford Cripps flies to Delhi with a promise of dominion status after the war.
focus_desc.gbr_indian_question: Congress demands a say in India's war, and London must decide how far to bend.
focus_desc.gbr_industrial_reorganisation: Depression-worn industrial districts are rationalised and investment is steered into modern plants.
focus_desc.gbr_infantry_tank: Heavily armoured tanks such as the Matilda II accompany the infantry and break the enemy line in set-piece attacks.
focus_desc.gbr_jet_engine: Frank Whittle's long-neglected turbojet finally receives money and factories.
focus_desc.gbr_kings_friends: Peers, editors and country squires who stood by the King when the cabinet turned on him gather round the Palace. They are few, but they know every door in London.
focus_desc.gbr_labour_landslide: The wartime coalition ends; voters choose Attlee and a promise of a new Britain.
focus_desc.gbr_labour_partnership: Bringing Labour into government wins over the trade unions and sets the state on the road to a planned economy.
focus_desc.gbr_lend_lease_acceptance: American arms and trucks arrive under the Lend-Lease Act, to be repaid after the war.
focus_desc.gbr_loyalty_oath: Civil servants, magistrates and officers are asked to swear to the Crown rather than to the Government of the day. Those who hesitate find their posts quietly refilled.
focus_desc.gbr_mechanisation: Horses give way to lorries and carriers until the whole Army moves on wheels and tracks.
focus_desc.gbr_mediterranean: Stronger defences at Gibraltar, Malta and in Egypt guard the sea road to the Suez Canal.
focus_desc.gbr_merchant_building: Prefabricated standard hulls come off the slips faster than the U-boats can sink them.
focus_desc.gbr_midlands: The engineering works of Birmingham and Coventry take on arms contracts.
focus_desc.gbr_ministry_of_supply: A single ministry takes over buying the Army's weapons and equipment, so contracts and production are handled in one place.
focus_desc.gbr_mulberry: Prefabricated harbours are towed across the Channel so an invasion need not seize a port.
focus_desc.gbr_national_service: Every able man owes the Crown a term of service. Recruiting stops being a matter of persuasion, and the age limits are pushed out on both sides.
focus_desc.gbr_nationalisation: The state takes over coal, steel and the railways and directs their output to rearmament, to the fury of the owners.
focus_desc.gbr_naval_bases_med: Malta, Gibraltar and Alexandria are enlarged as bases for the Mediterranean Fleet.
focus_desc.gbr_nzl_annex: The Dominion is annexed to the Crown. Its ministers become officials, its small army joins the King's, and its ports fly the same flag as Portsmouth.
focus_desc.gbr_nzl_governor: A new governor-general arrives with orders to read every bill before it is tabled. The Dominion's ministers learn that the Crown is no longer a figure on a stamp.
focus_desc.gbr_nzl_parliament: The Dominion's House is adjourned until further notice. Its ministers govern by the governor's warrant and the press is asked to be patient.
focus_desc.gbr_old_soldiers: Retired officers and veterans of the trenches form a guard of honour around the cause. They bring drill, discipline and a stock of grievances against Westminster.
focus_desc.gbr_one_empire: Britain and the Dominions resolve to fight as one nation, and men from every corner of the Empire join the forces.
focus_desc.gbr_pacific_fleet: A modern squadron is sent east to Singapore and Ceylon to give the Pacific colonies a shield.
focus_desc.gbr_palace_dismissal: In one night the ministers are dismissed and the Palace names its own. No following is needed, only a guard at the right doors, but the old parties and the loyal regiments take up arms, and Britain goes to civil war.
focus_desc.gbr_peace_party: Halifax and his circle urge a settlement with Berlin while the Empire is still intact.
focus_desc.gbr_peacetime_conscription: The Military Training Act calls up twenty-year-old men in time of peace, something Britain has never done before.
focus_desc.gbr_peoples_rearmament: Working people throw their weight behind rearmament, and the factories and recruiting offices fill up together.
focus_desc.gbr_postwar_planning: Ministers draw up the housing, schools and health service of the peace to come.
focus_desc.gbr_press_barons: The owners of the great dailies decide that the throne makes better copy than the House. Front pages turn warm to the King's cause, and money follows.
focus_desc.gbr_prorogue_parliament: With the streets organised and the oath sworn, the King prorogues Parliament by his own authority and names no date for its return. Britain is governed by decree, and the old parties take up arms in the country to answer.
focus_desc.gbr_quebec_agreement: Churchill and Roosevelt agree to pool their atomic work and share its fruits.
focus_desc.gbr_radar_chain: Tall masts along the east coast pick up approaching aircraft long before they arrive.
focus_desc.gbr_radar_h2s: Centimetric radar lets bombers find cities and hunters find bombers through darkness and cloud.
focus_desc.gbr_raf_expansion: The Royal Air Force issues one expansion scheme after another, adding squadron after squadron.
focus_desc.gbr_raj_annex: India is annexed to the Crown. Hundreds of millions of subjects, a vast coast and the richest provinces of the East become the realm's land, and the Indian Army is disbanded rather than trusted. No other step costs the Crown as much.
focus_desc.gbr_raj_governor: The Viceroy's reserve powers are extended to every province, and officials of the Crown take the chairs of the provincial councils. Delhi is told that the age of consultation is over.
focus_desc.gbr_raj_parliament: The central legislature and the provincial assemblies are suspended in a single week. Parties are told to stay out of public life, and the districts are run by commissioners.
focus_desc.gbr_rationing: Food, fuel and clothing are rationed, and every shipping ton goes further.
focus_desc.gbr_realm_reconciliation: With the opposition beaten or bought off, the Crown declares the realm whole again. Order returns to the streets and the strain of the split begins to fade.
focus_desc.gbr_rearm_now: The rule that rearmament must not disturb normal trade is dropped, and industry puts war orders first.
focus_desc.gbr_red_clydeside: The shipyards of Glasgow and the valleys of South Wales elect communist shop stewards and councillors.
focus_desc.gbr_reich_exchange: Designers and engineers cross the North Sea in both directions. German armour and air research flows to British works, and British production methods flow back.
focus_desc.gbr_royal_cabinet: The King calls the movement's leader to form a government of his friends. Ministers who would not serve are dismissed, and the Commons is told to approve the list.
focus_desc.gbr_royal_dockyards: A standing programme funds the yards on every coast with orders that outlast any budget fight. The Navy is told it will be the Crown's long arm.
focus_desc.gbr_royal_government: The King dismisses the cabinet and rules through ministers of his own choosing. Parliament refuses, and Britain goes to civil war.
focus_desc.gbr_royal_staff: The old general staff is reshaped into a body that answers to the King. Promotion follows loyalty and results, and lessons from the last war are put into drill at once.
focus_desc.gbr_scientific_committee: A committee of scientists under Henry Tizard looks for new ways to defend Britain from the air.
focus_desc.gbr_second_front: The Allies prepare the great invasion of the Continent from southern England.
focus_desc.gbr_security_service: The police special branches and the intelligence offices are brought under one head. Plots are found early, and rumours are found even earlier.
focus_desc.gbr_shadow_factories: Motor manufacturers run state-funded twin plants in the Midlands, ready to turn out aero engines and airframes the moment war comes.
focus_desc.gbr_singapore: More batteries and forts go up around the Singapore naval base, the key to the Empire's defence in the Far East.
focus_desc.gbr_south_wales: Investment in the pits and steelworks of South Wales raises steel output.
focus_desc.gbr_soviet_agreement: Facing Germany as a common enemy, London sets ideology aside and agrees with Moscow that each will help the other.
focus_desc.gbr_special_ops_exec: "Set Europe ablaze": agents are trained to arm and organise resistance in occupied lands.
focus_desc.gbr_state_industry: Factories are put on orders from a central board. Output, prices and wages are set from above, and the works that made motorcars build what the Crown requires.
focus_desc.gbr_statute_commonwealth: The Dominions are treated as equal partners in the Commonwealth, and their governments answer with warmer goodwill.
focus_desc.gbr_suez_defence: Fortified lines and a ready garrison guard Egypt and the canal, the artery of the Empire.
focus_desc.gbr_tactical_air: Air power is tied to the army: fighter-bombers and close support ride with every advance.
focus_desc.gbr_tank_programme: Development and production of infantry tanks and cruiser tanks are pushed forward.
focus_desc.gbr_territorial_army: In spring 1939 the government decides to double the Territorial Army and calls for volunteers.
focus_desc.gbr_tizard_mission: A black box of British inventions crosses the Atlantic in exchange for American industry.
focus_desc.gbr_total_production: Every factory switches to war work, running shifts around the clock.
focus_desc.gbr_tube_alloys: Physicists in Birmingham and Cambridge find that a bomb may be possible, and the project begins.
focus_desc.gbr_union_rallies: Uniformed columns fill the halls of the East End and the Midlands under the Crown's banner. Order and a strong hand are promised to men who have waited years for work.
focus_desc.gbr_university_research: Laboratories at Cambridge, Oxford and Birmingham take on work for the armed services.
focus_desc.gbr_war_cabinet: Every party joins a wartime coalition, and the general election is put off until the war is won.
focus_desc.gbr_women_service: Women fill the lathes, the fields and the auxiliary services as men leave for the front.
focus_desc.gbr_world_partition: The accord is widened to the other revisionist powers. Rome and Tokyo are given their own zones and promise to respect the Crown's, and the old naval rivalries are put aside.
focus_desc.gbr_zaf_annex: The Union is annexed to the Crown. Pretoria becomes a seat of the realm's government, the mines and the army pass to the King, and the old quarrels over the republic are left to the police.
focus_desc.gbr_zaf_governor: A strong governor-general is posted to the Cape with troops at his back. The ministers in Pretoria find their budgets queried and their appointments vetoed.
focus_desc.gbr_zaf_parliament: The Union Parliament is sent home and the provincial councils with it. The governor-general rules by proclamation, and the opposition meets in private houses.
focus_desc.gen_air_bases: Paved runways, hangars and repair shops spread across the country, ready for a larger air force.
focus_desc.gen_air_force: The flying corps becomes a service of its own and buys its first modern fighters.
focus_desc.gen_army_artillery: New guns and modern fire control are ordered for the artillery, and gunners train more often.
focus_desc.gen_army_doctrine: Officers weigh the lessons of the last war against the new weapons and write down how to fight the next one.
focus_desc.gen_army_fort: Bunkers, ditches and obstacles rise where the most dangerous neighbour would strike first.
focus_desc.gen_army_infantry: Worn-out rifles and field gear give way to modern equipment for the next war, and the support units get new kit too.
focus_desc.gen_army_reform: The general staff redraws the army's organisation, retires tired commanders and promotes able officers.
focus_desc.gen_army_staff: A staff college teaches officers to plan operations and to move large formations without confusion.
focus_desc.gen_com_party_cells: The communists build cells in the factories, the mines and the barracks, ready for the day the call comes.
focus_desc.gen_com_red_guards: Armed workers' squads guard the councils. Their rifles come from sympathetic soldiers and from abroad.
focus_desc.gen_com_revolution: The councils call a general strike and take power in the cities they hold. The old order fights back, and the country splits in civil war.
focus_desc.gen_com_workers_councils: Strike committees become councils that run the works themselves and answer to the party, not the owners.
focus_desc.gen_dem_citizens_committees: Committees in every town collect signatures, print leaflets and list the government's broken promises.
focus_desc.gen_dem_defence_leagues: Volunteers drill to defend the constitution. The government calls them rebels; they call the government illegal.
focus_desc.gen_dem_opposition_front: Liberals, moderates and the banned parties join one front against the government and demand free elections.
focus_desc.gen_dem_uprising: The opposition proclaims a provisional government. The army and the provinces choose sides, and the country goes to civil war.
focus_desc.gen_fas_march: The squads march on the capital to take power. The government and its loyal troops resist, and the country falls into civil war.
focus_desc.gen_fas_national_party: The renewal movement becomes a party with a leader, a uniform and a programme of national rebirth.
focus_desc.gen_fas_officer_backers: Younger officers promise that the barracks will not fire on the movement, and some will march with it.
focus_desc.gen_fas_street_squads: Uniformed squads break up rival meetings and march through the towns. The police look the other way.
focus_desc.gen_ind_civ_1: Cheap credit and tax relief draw new factories to the towns with the most room to grow.
focus_desc.gen_ind_civ_2: Planned districts with power, water and workers' housing let builders raise new plants faster.
focus_desc.gen_ind_infra: New highways and branch lines bind the provinces to the capital, its markets and its garrisons.
focus_desc.gen_ind_mil_1: State arsenals are founded so that rifles, shells and guns no longer have to be bought abroad.
focus_desc.gen_ind_mil_2: Larger arsenals and new trade schools train the skilled hands that modern weapons demand.
focus_desc.gen_ind_resources: Geologists chart new deposits, and the state lays roads so that mining companies can reach them.
focus_desc.gen_ind_survey: Inspectors visit every mill, mine and workshop to learn what the country can truly make and where money would do the most good.
focus_desc.gen_navy_coast: Gun batteries and minefields guard the harbours most exposed to an attack from the sea.
focus_desc.gen_navy_yards: The best harbour gets a new slipway, and the navy orders modern ships from the yards.
focus_desc.gen_neu_coup: The generals take the ministries and dissolve the parties. The government's supporters take up arms, and the country goes to civil war.
focus_desc.gen_neu_loyal_regiments: Chosen regiments are moved near the capital, and their commanders answer to the circle.
focus_desc.gen_neu_officers_circle: Generals meet in private to agree who will govern when the politicians fail.
focus_desc.gen_neu_order_party: Landowners, clergy and senior officials gather behind one demand: an end to party quarrels and a strong hand at the top.
focus_desc.gen_pol_admin: Overlapping ministries are merged, procedures shortened and a career civil service is built.
focus_desc.gen_pol_claims: Lands lost in past wars return to the speeches, the schoolbooks and the general staff's maps.
focus_desc.gen_pol_com: Trade unions and workers' councils gain a voice, and the ideas of the left spread through the factories.
focus_desc.gen_pol_com_ally: The party seeks closer ties with Moscow and the international communist movement.
focus_desc.gen_pol_defence_spirit: Newsreels, air-raid drills and veterans' leagues remind citizens that peace has to be guarded.
focus_desc.gen_pol_dem: Parliament, a free press and fair elections are held up as the source of the nation's strength.
focus_desc.gen_pol_dem_ally: Envoys visit the leading democracies to ask how the country might enter their alliance.
focus_desc.gen_pol_fas: A mass movement calls for order and national revival under a single disciplined party.
focus_desc.gen_pol_fas_ally: The government sends envoys to Berlin to ask whether a smaller state might enter its bloc.
focus_desc.gen_pol_neu: The government formally declares that it will take no side in the quarrels of the great powers.
focus_desc.gen_pol_neu_league: Neighbours who fear the great powers are invited into a defensive entente of our own.
focus_desc.gen_pol_unity: In a hard decade, rival parties and regions are asked to set their quarrels aside and pull together.
focus_desc.gen_rs_1: University grants and a national research council let the country pursue one more line of research.
focus_desc.gen_rs_2: Company laboratories work alongside the universities, and the state pays for both.
focus_desc.grc_accept_british_expedition: London offers an expeditionary force. It may provoke Berlin, but alone we cannot hold the north.
focus_desc.grc_aegean_minefields: Mine the approaches to Piraeus and the narrow channels between the islands.
focus_desc.grc_air_defence_of_athens: Guns around the capital and the port of Piraeus, the fleet's anchorage and the country's lifeline.
focus_desc.grc_albanian_counteroffensive: The invasion is stopped in the mountains. Now throw it back across the border and take the towns beyond.
focus_desc.grc_aliakmon_line: Abandon the frontier and hold a shorter line behind the Aliakmon with the British.
focus_desc.grc_anglo_greek_staff_talks: Where would a British corps land, which airfields would it use, which line would it hold? Talk it through before the war does.
focus_desc.grc_ankara_friendship: The exchange of populations is done and the old enemies have signed a friendship. Make it a real alliance at the Straits.
focus_desc.grc_anti_tank_batteries: Italy and Germany have tanks and we have almost nothing to stop them. Buy guns and train their crews.
focus_desc.grc_armaments_programme: Shells, cartridges and rifles at home, so the next war does not wait for a foreign ship.
focus_desc.grc_army_of_asia_minor: Train an army that could cross the sea again, with landing practice in the islands and veterans of the last campaign as instructors.
focus_desc.grc_army_reorganisation: Purges and counter-purges have gutted the officer corps. Rebuild the divisions, the depots and the reserve lists.
focus_desc.grc_ask_british_guarantee: Italy is in Albania and its submarines are in our waters. Ask London to promise what it promised Poland.
focus_desc.grc_athens_piraeus_industry: Textile mills, cement works and chemical plants around the capital and its port.
focus_desc.grc_averof_refit: The old armoured cruiser that won the Balkan Wars is still the fleet's flagship. Give her new fire control and anti-aircraft guns.
focus_desc.grc_axis_accommodation: Sign what Mussolini wants signed and hope that a treaty keeps his legions on the other side of the Pindus.
focus_desc.grc_balkan_entente_bloc: Turn a paper guarantee into a staff, a treaty of mutual aid and an alliance that answers any aggressor, great power or not.
focus_desc.grc_balkan_pact: Greece, Turkey, Yugoslavia and Romania guarantee each other's borders. Bulgaria, which wants a coast on the Aegean, stays out.
focus_desc.grc_bauxite_mines: The red earth of Parnassus is bauxite. Open the mines and sell it to whoever makes aluminium.
focus_desc.grc_border_line: Concrete forts in the mountains from the Beles to the Nestos, each a small underground town.
focus_desc.grc_british_orientation: Greece lives by the sea and the sea belongs to the Royal Navy. Whatever the regime thinks of parliaments, London comes first.
focus_desc.grc_cavalry_division: Two horse brigades for the plains of Macedonia and the gaps in the mountains.
focus_desc.grc_chromite_mines: Thessaly's chromite is wanted by every steelmaker in Europe preparing for war.
focus_desc.grc_claim_constantinople: For Greeks there is only one City. Claim it, and be ready to fight Turkey for it.
focus_desc.grc_claim_ionia: Smyrna and its coast, Greek for three thousand years until the fire. Claim it back.
focus_desc.grc_com_balkan_comrades: Ask Moscow for recognition and the Yugoslav and Bulgarian comrades for friendship across the old borders.
focus_desc.grc_com_kke_underground: The Communist Party of Greece was the kingmaker of the hung parliament. Banned, it goes underground with its presses and cells.
focus_desc.grc_com_liberation_front: A front of workers, peasants and patriots, led from the shadows by the party, ready to fight whoever rules Athens.
focus_desc.grc_com_mountain_rising: The bands come down from Roumeli and the Pindus. The party calls the people to arms against the government.
focus_desc.grc_com_peoples_democracy: The committees of the villages and the factories become the state. The old parties are dissolved.
focus_desc.grc_com_popular_front: The party offers the Venizelists what it offered in the chamber: votes in return for freedom of the unions.
focus_desc.grc_com_tobacco_strikes: The tobacco warehouses of Thessaloniki and Kavala strike. When the police fire on the march, the whole north stops working.
focus_desc.grc_crown_and_army: The king keeps the officers loyal to himself rather than to his premier. The regime is safe from coups as long as the two agree.
focus_desc.grc_dem_crowned_democracy: Keep the king, but as a king who reigns and does not rule. The royalists can live with it; the army stays quiet.
focus_desc.grc_dem_liberal_party: Banned or not, the Liberal Party keeps its clubs, its newspapers in exile and its voters in Crete and the north.
focus_desc.grc_dem_opposition_pact: Liberals, Populists and the small parties agree on one demand: the constitution and elections, before anything else.
focus_desc.grc_dem_parliament_restored: Deputies return to the Boule, the exiles come home from the islands, and the newspapers print what they like.
focus_desc.grc_dem_refugee_settlement: Finish what the Refugee Settlement Commission began: title deeds, houses and credit for the families from Asia Minor.
focus_desc.grc_dem_restore_constitution: The opposition calls the country back to the constitution and the army's Venizelists answer. The regime will not go quietly.
focus_desc.grc_dem_second_republic: The crown betrayed the constitution twice. Send the king into exile again and proclaim the republic.
focus_desc.grc_dem_venizelos_legacy: The great Cretan's name still fills the squares. His heirs speak of the Greece of the treaties, the refugees housed and the schools built.
focus_desc.grc_destroyer_raids: Send the destroyers on night raids against the enemy's convoys and harbours.
focus_desc.grc_dodecanese_question: Greek islanders under the Italian flag since 1912. In peace, a grievance; in war with their owner, a war aim.
focus_desc.grc_drachma_stabilised: The default of 1932 is behind us. Settle with the bondholders, hold the drachma and win back some credit.
focus_desc.grc_electrification: Most of the country has no electric light. Power lines and new stations, starting with the industrial towns.
focus_desc.grc_epirus_defence_plan: If the enemy comes from Albania, hold the river lines and the passes, and make him pay for each valley.
focus_desc.grc_epirus_united: Our troops hold the south of Albania. Annex it, whatever the great powers say at the peace.
focus_desc.grc_evzones: The kilted mountain light infantry, the army's pride. Build whole divisions on their pattern.
focus_desc.grc_fas_axis_partner: Tie the country's trade and its future to Berlin and Rome, and hope Rome forgets its designs on Epirus.
focus_desc.grc_fas_national_socialists: A small Greek party copies the German model: uniforms, rallies and an admiring look toward Berlin.
focus_desc.grc_fas_new_order: The crown is a decoration, the party is the state. Greece takes its place in the new Europe.
focus_desc.grc_fas_seize_the_state: The movement's squads and its friends in the army move against the crown and the old parties alike.
focus_desc.grc_fas_totalitarian_turn: Turn a paternal dictatorship into a mass movement: one party, one youth, one doctrine, and the old royal court pushed aside.
focus_desc.grc_fas_youth_cadres: The regime's youth leaders want more than parades. They want a party, and they want it to rule.
focus_desc.grc_fighter_tactics: Few aircraft and fewer spares: train pilots to fight outnumbered and come home.
focus_desc.grc_fleet_in_exile_plan: Plan for the worst: the merchant fleet sails to Allied ports and carries on the war at sea.
focus_desc.grc_french_bombers: Order modern light bombers in Paris, and hope they arrive before the war.
focus_desc.grc_general_mobilisation: The war is coming or has come. Call up every class and put the country on a war footing.
focus_desc.grc_german_credits: Krupp and Rheinmetall guns, paid for with tobacco not yet harvested.
focus_desc.grc_german_trade_tilt: Germany buys the tobacco, the raisins and the ore, pays in clearing marks and offers credit for guns. Lean toward the buyer.
